Problem description:
## Description

As developers in the ecosystem migrate to **Xcode 26**, the current iOS codebase is encountering build failures and compatibility issues. This story focuses on upgrading the iOS project and related CI/CD pipelines to ensure successful builds and stable development workflows on Xcode 26.

The effort includes fixing compilation issues, updating dependencies, resolving deprecated API usage, and stabilizing the build environment for continued development and release readiness.

## Problem Statement

- Build failures due to Xcode 26 migration  
- Dependency and compatibility issues  
- CI/CD pipelines not aligned with Xcode 26 environment  
- Deprecated APIs causing compilation failures  
- Risk of unstable builds for contributors and release pipelines  

## Scope

- Upgrade project to **Xcode 26**
- Fix all compilation and dependency issues
- Update project configurations and build settings
- Commit required patches and fixes
- Update CI/CD pipelines to support Xcode 26
- Validate successful builds across supported environments

## Out of Scope

- Liquid Display native support enhancements
- UI redesign or UI modernization efforts
- Feature enhancements unrelated to migration
- Liquid Display compatibility flag removal

## Acceptance Criteria

### Xcode 26 Migration
- [ ] Project builds successfully on Xcode 26  
- [ ] All dependencies updated and compatible  
- [ ] No critical build warnings/errors blocking release  
- [ ] Deprecated APIs addressed where required for successful compilation  
- [ ] Swift version compatibility validated  
- [ ] CI/CD pipelines updated to use Xcode 26  
- [ ] Build pipeline executes successfully end-to-end  
- [ ] Patch committed with clear migration documentation  

## Technical Notes

- Address deprecated APIs introduced in Xcode 26  
- Validate Swift version compatibility  
- Update dependency versions if required  
- Review signing/build configurations impacted by Xcode upgrade  
- Ensure CI/CD runners and build agents support Xcode 26  


## Dependencies

- Xcode 26 environment setup  
- Updated third-party libraries  
- CI/CD environment updates  
- Access to macOS runners/build agents supporting Xcode 26  

## Definition of Done

- Code merged into main branch  
- CI/CD pipeline passing with Xcode 26  
- No critical build/runtime issues  
- Migration documentation updated  
- Development team able to build project successfully using Xcode 26

title: Wallet UI - DCQL-Based Credential Matching and Selection UI for VP Request
content:
Problem description:
# Wallet UI Story: DCQL-Based VP Request Credential Selection

## Summary

Implement the Requested Cards UI in Inji Wallet for Verifiable Presentation (VP) requests containing DCQL. The wallet must render credential set queries, support credential selection, apply pre-selection logic, allow user review and re-selection, and enable sharing only when all required credential set queries are satisfied.

## Scope

- Applicable only for VP requests containing DCQL.
- Covers Requested Cards page rendering, credential selection, pre-selection, review/re-selection, share button enablement, and defined edge cases.

**Figma File** - https://www.figma.com/design/F6HYVibHTUUWicHMFfBgjM/Inji-Wallet-App?node-id=4642-1155&p=f&t=xFU5hzIjBfvYFlvv-0

## Notes

### 1. Credential Set Query Rendering

A VP request can contain multiple credential set queries.

#### UI Behavior

- Each credential set query shall be displayed as either:
  - Mandatory Cards Section (when `required = true`)
  - Optional Cards Section (when `required = false`)

### 2. Option Rendering

Each credential set query can contain multiple options.

#### UI Behavior

- Each option shall be displayed with:
  - Radio button selection control
  - OR separator between options
- Exactly one option must be selected to satisfy the credential set query.


### 3. Credential Query Rendering

Each option can contain one or more credential queries.

#### UI Behavior

##### Single Credential Query

When an option contains only one credential query:

- Display a section showing all credentials matching that credential query.

##### Multiple Credential Queries

When an option contains multiple credential queries:

- Display a "Multiple Cards" section.
- Show badge:
  - `ALL Required`
- All credential queries within the option must be satisfied for the option to be satisfied.


### 4. Matching Credentials Rendering

Each credential query can match multiple credentials.

#### UI Behavior

- Display all matching credentials.
- Selection control shall be:
  - Radio button when multiple credential sharing is not allowed.
  - Checkbox when multiple credential sharing is allowed.


## Feature Logic

### 1. Pre-select Cards

To provide a seamless experience, the wallet shall pre-select the minimum credentials required to satisfy the VP request.

#### Pre-selection Criteria

##### Mandatory Cards Section

Only required credential set queries shall participate in pre-selection.

For each mandatory section:

- The first option shall be pre-selected.

If the selected option contains:

##### Single Credential Query

- If only one credential matches:
  - That credential shall be pre-selected.

- If multiple credentials match:
  - The first matching credential shall be pre-selected.

##### Multiple Credential Queries

The option shall be selected in a way that satisfies the option.

Examples:

- If option contains:
  - `govt-id`
  - `pan`

And matches are:

  - Govt ID
  - PAN Card

Then:

  - Govt ID shall be selected
  - PAN Card shall be selected

If option contains:

  - `govt-id`
  - `pan`

And matches are:

  - Govt ID / Passport
  - PAN Card

Then:

  - Govt ID shall be selected
  - PAN Card shall be selected

> Note: Examples are for illustration purposes only.

##### Optional Cards Section

- No credentials shall be pre-selected.

##### Edge Case

- Same credential matching multiple credential queries overrides pre-selection where applicable.

### 2. Review and Reselect

Users shall be allowed to review and modify selections while ensuring the VP request remains satisfiable.

#### Mandatory Cards Section

If:

- There is only one option requested (or satisfiable), and
- Only one credential satisfies that option

Then:

- The credential shall be pre-selected.
- Deselection of that credential shall be disabled.

If:

- Multiple options exist

Then:

- User may switch between options.
- Share button shall only be enabled when the mandatory section remains satisfied.

#### Optional Cards Section

- Section shall be collapsed by default.
- User may expand the section.
- User may select credentials they wish to share.

### 2.1 Option Selection

Whenever an option is selected:

- All other options within the same credential set query shall be deselected.

This applies to:

- User selection
- Pre-selection

#### Case I: Option Contains One Credential Query

##### Case I.i

Credential query matches exactly one credential.

UI:

- Credential displayed as selectable.

Selection behavior:

- Credential is selected.

##### Case I.ii

Credential query matches multiple credentials.

UI:

- All matching credentials displayed.
- Selection control shall be radio button or checkbox based on whether multiple credential sharing is allowed.

Selection behavior:

- First credential is selected.

#### Case II: Option Contains Multiple Credential Queries

UI:

- Multiple Cards section displayed.

Selection behavior:

- First matching credential for every credential query shall be selected.


### 2.2 Credential Selection User Interaction

#### Multiple Credential Sharing Allowed

When user selects another credential:

- Existing selected credential remains selected.
- Newly selected credential is also selected.

#### Multiple Credential Sharing Not Allowed

When user selects another credential:

- Newly selected credential becomes selected.
- Previously selected credential is deselected.


### 3. Share Button Enablement

The Share button shall be enabled only when:

- All required credential set queries are satisfied.


## Edge Cases

### Same Credential Matching Multiple Credential Queries

Example VP Request:

```json
[
  {
    "options": [
      ["driver_license_condition"]
    ],
    "required": true
  },
  {
    "options": [
      ["age_above_18_condition"]
    ],
    "required": true
  }
]
```

Matching Credentials:

```json
{
  "driver_license_condition": ["Driver License"],
  "age_above_18_condition": ["Driver License", "Birth Certificate"]
}
```

#### Expected Behavior

If:

- User selects Driver License in Mandatory Cards Section 1

Then:

- Driver License shall be pre-selected in Mandatory Cards Section 2.

This behavior shall override the normal pre-selection logic because the same credential satisfies both credential queries.

Users may subsequently modify the selection as part of the Review and Reselect flow.

Discussion and resolution:
[KiruthikaJeyashankar]: ## **Notes**
1. VP request will have n number of credential set queries
   - UI : Each credential set query will be shown as Mandatory cards section / optional cards section based on whether the credential set query is required
2. Each credential set query will have n number of options where exactly one option needs to be selected to satisfy the credential set query
   - UI: Each option will be shown with radio buttons for selection and OR separator indicating that one of the options needs to be selected by the user
3. Each option will have n number of credential query - all the credential queries of the option needs to be selected to say that the option is satisfied
   - If there is only one credential query - a section is shown to user showing all the credentials matching that credential query
   - If there are multiple credential queries - "Multiple cards with badge ALL Required" section is shown to the user
4. Each credential query can match with n number of credentials
  - A section will be shown to user indicating that there are multiple credentials matching with the credential query
  - radio or checkbox selection button is shown to user based on whether the  credential query allows sharing of multiple credentials or not

------

## Scope

- The scope of below pointers focus on VP request containing DCQL only

## **Feature logics**

### **1. Pre-select cards**

- To ensure seamless experience to user, the Inji Wallet pre-selects the minimal cards required to satisfy the VP request in the Requested Cards page
- Pre-selection criteria
  - Only mandatory cards section (Required credential set query) will have the credentials pre-selected
    - Very first option of the section is pre-selected
    - Say - If an option had only one credential its pre-selected / If an option had 3 credentials very first one is pre-selected
    - In case the first option is of "Multiple cards" then the option is selected in a way that satisfies the option
    - Example
    -> Option has 2 credential query IDs : govt-id and pan each of it matching with Govt ID and PAN card , then both of the cards are selected
    -> Option has 2 credential query IDs : govt-id and pan each of it matching with (Govt ID / Passport) and PAN card , then Govt ID and PAN card are selected considering the first card selection logic
    (Note: The examples are for illustration purposes only)
  - Optional cards section (Not required credential set query) will not have the credentials pre-selected (Conditions apply)

> Note: Edgecase - 1. Same credential matching multiple credential queries overrides pre-selection if applicable

### **2. Review and reselect**

User can review and change the selection of credential ensuring the VP request is satisfied

The following conditions follow here,
- The mandatory cards section has only one option requested from verifier or satisfiable by Wallet and there is only one credential satisfying that option, then that credential is pre-selected & the deselection of that credential is disabled here
- The mandatory cards section has more than one options then the user is free to toggle selection of that options / cards, share button will be enabled only if user has satisfied this mandatory section
- Optional cards section is by default not expanded - the user can expand this section and select any credentials that they want to share

#### _**2.1 Select an Option**_

When any interactions happen with an option other options of that Cards section are deselected to ensure rightness

When an option is selected (by user / pre-selected)

_Case i : Option has only one credential query ID_

- Case i.i credential query ID matches only one credential -> a credential is shown as selectable
```
Credential is selected
```

  - Case i.ii credential query ID matches more than one credential -> a section is shown with all matched credentials wrapped and selectable icon is radio / checkbox as per multiple credentials sharing of this credenital query ID is possible or not

```
Very first credential is selected
```
_Case ii: option has more than one credential query ID (Multiple cards section)_

```
All the credential query ID's matching first credential is selected
```

#### **2.2 Credential selection user interaction**
- If multiple is allowed and user selects next credential - both are selected
- If multiple is not allowed and user selects next credential - next credential is selected and first credential is deselected

### **3. Share button enablement**
- Share button is enabled iff all the required credential set queries are satisfied


### **4. Edge cases**

1. Same credential matching multiple credential queries

For example, say VP request has the credential sets as follows
```json
[
  {
    "options": [
      ["driver_license_condition"],
    ],
    "required": true
  },
  {
    "options": [
      ["age_above_18_condition"]
    ],
    "required": true
  }
]
```

Matching credentials is as follows
```json
{
  "driver_license_condition": ["Driver License"], // Mandatory cards section 1
  "age_above_18_condition": ["Driver License", "birth certificate"] // Mandatory cards section 2
}
```

If we notice here both credential queries are satisfying with Driver's license - In this case
- If user selects "Driver License" in Mandatory cards section 1
- Then "Driver License" is pre-selected in Mandatory cards section 2 irrespective of the pre-selection logic considering that driver's license has been selected in previous section. User can modify this selection as per _2. Review and reselect_ notes

1. Change the "Close" button to tertiary variant in Expandable sheet
2. Checkout on the "What you can do" heading's color with mock up in "No matching cards page" / Update title without "exclamation mark"
3. Change that "Information you choose" related instructions in the card to well-known text color

title: [Koltin] Matching of Credentials as per DCQL (Filtering and parsing)  and VP construction of DCQL
content:
Problem description:
## Description

As part of OpenID4VP v1.0 support, the `inji-openid4vp` Kotlin library must support Digital Credential Query Language (DCQL) based credential matching and Verifiable Presentation (VP) construction.

OpenID4VP v1.0 introduces DCQL as the standard mechanism for expressing credential requirements in Authorization Requests. The library should be capable of parsing DCQL requests, identifying matching credentials from the wallet, and constructing VP responses compliant with OpenID4VP v1.0.

This implementation will serve as the foundation for both regular OpenID4VP presentation flows.

Refer this for logic implementation - https://openid.net/specs/openid-4-verifiable-presentations-1_0.html#section-6.4


## Background

OpenID4VP v1.0 replaces reliance on DIF Presentation Exchange and introduces DCQL for requesting credentials.

The library currently supports credential matching mechanisms aligned with earlier drafts. To support OpenID4VP v1.0, the library must:

- Parse DCQL requests.
- Match wallet credentials against DCQL criteria.
- Validate requested claims.
- Return matching credentials to consuming applications.
- Construct VP responses using selected credentials.

Reference:
- OpenID4VP v1.0
- DCQL Specification
- OpenID4VP Version Support for V1.0 Design


## Scope

### 1. DCQL Parsing

Support parsing of DCQL queries received within OpenID4VP Authorization Requests.

Example:

```json
{
  "credentials": [
    {
      "id": "identity_credential",
      "format": "dc+sd-jwt",
      "meta": {
        "vct_values": [
          "https://example.com/identity"
        ]
      },
      "claims": [
        {
          "path": ["first_name"]
        },
        {
          "path": ["last_name"]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The parser should extract:

- Credential query identifier
- Credential format
- Credential metadata
- Requested claim paths
- Optional DCQL parameters

### 2. Credential Matching Engine

Support matching credentials based on:

#### Credential Format

Examples:

- dc+sd-jwt
- LDP VCs/JSON-LD
- mso_mdoc

#### Credential Metadata

Examples:

- vct_values
- doctype
- credential identifiers
- supported format metadata

#### Requested Claims

The matching engine should verify that requested claim paths exist within the credential.

Example:

```json
{
  "claims": [
    {
      "path": ["first_name"]
    },
    {
      "path": ["last_name"]
    }
  ]
}
```

Only credentials satisfying the query requirements should be returned.

### 3. Matching Result Generation

Provide a structured matching result to the wallet application.

Example:

```kotlin
List<MatchingCredential>
```

The response should include:

- Credential Identifier
- Credential Format
- Query Identifier
- Requested Claims
- Credential Metadata

### 4. VP Construction

Support VP construction using selected credentials.

The builder should:

- Accept selected credentials.
- Generate VP tokens.
- Preserve credential-to-query mapping.
- Support single and multiple credential presentations.
- Generate OpenID4VP-compliant responses.

### 5. Response Construction

Support VP response construction for:

- direct_post
- direct_post.jwt
- iar-post
- iar-post.jwt

Response encryption is handled by separate stories and is not part of this implementation.

Out of scope:

- Presentation during Issuance  


## Technical Approach

### DCQL Models

Introduce Kotlin models for:

```kotlin
DCQLQuery
DCQLCredentialQuery
DCQLClaim
DCQLCredentialMetadata
```

### Credential Matching Layer

Introduce a dedicated matching engine:

```kotlin
CredentialMatcher
```

Responsibilities:

- Format validation
- Metadata validation
- Claim validation
- Matching result generation

### VP Construction Layer

Introduce:

```kotlin
DCQLPresentationBuilder
```

Responsibilities:

- VP token generation
- Query mapping preservation
- OpenID4VP response construction

### Authorization Request Integration

When an OpenID4VP request is processed:

1. Parse DCQL query.
2. Match wallet credentials.
3. Return matching credentials.
4. Accept selected credentials.
5. Construct VP response.


## Out of Scope

- Presentation During Issuance flow
- Digital Credentials API implementation
- Credential storage implementation
- UI credential selection
- Response encryption
- Verifier trust validation
- Advanced DCQL operators not finalized for V1.0 support

Refer this for logic:


- https://mosip.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/Inji/pages/2494234646/VP+Request+with+DCQL+Query#Scenarios-and-DCQL-representations
- https://mosip.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/Inji/pages/2494234646/VP+Request+with+DCQL+Query#Digital-KYC-for-Opening-a-Bank-Account


## Acceptance Criteria

### AC1 - Parse DCQL Request

**Given** an OpenID4VP Authorization Request containing a DCQL query

**When** the library processes the request

**Then** the DCQL structure should be parsed successfully.


### AC2 - Match Credentials by Format

**Given** credentials of multiple formats exist in the wallet

**When** a DCQL query specifies a format

**Then** only credentials matching the requested format should be returned.


### AC3 - Match Credentials by Metadata

**Given** multiple credentials exist

**When** metadata constraints are present in the query

**Then** only credentials satisfying the metadata requirements should be returned.


### AC4 - Validate Requested Claims

**Given** a credential does not contain all requested claims

**When** matching is performed

**Then** the credential should not be considered a valid match.

### AC5 - Return Multiple Matches

**Given** multiple credentials satisfy a query

**When** matching is executed

**Then** all matching credentials should be returned.


### AC6 - Construct VP Response

**Given** one or more matching credentials are selected

**When** VP construction is triggered

**Then** a valid OpenID4VP VP response should be generated.


### AC7 - Preserve Query Mapping

**Given** multiple DCQL credential queries exist

**When** the VP response is generated

**Then** credential-to-query association should be preserved.

### AC8 - Maintain Backward Compatibility

**Given** a request that does not contain DCQL

**When** processed by the library

**Then** existing behaviour should remain unchanged.

## Dependencies

- OpenID4VP v1.0 Support
- DCQL Request Parsing Models
- Credential Format Parsers
- VP Construction Framework

## References

- OpenID4VP 1.0 Specification
- DCQL Specification
- OpenID4VP Version Support for V1.0 Design Document

title: [Koltin] Validation of DCQL Query
content:
Problem description:
## Description

As part of OpenID4VP v1.0 support, the `inji-openid4vp` Kotlin library must validate Digital Credential Query Language (DCQL) queries received within OpenID4VP Authorization Requests before credential matching is performed.

DCQL becomes the primary mechanism for expressing credential requirements in OpenID4VP v1.0. The library should ensure that incoming DCQL requests are structurally valid, contain supported formats, and conform to the requirements expected by the wallet before proceeding with credential discovery and VP construction.

This validation layer should act as a guardrail to prevent malformed or unsupported requests from entering the credential matching flow.


## Background

OpenID4VP v1.0 introduces DCQL as the standard query language for requesting credentials and deprecates the dependency on Presentation Exchange.

Before credential matching begins, the wallet must validate that:

- The DCQL query is syntactically correct.
- Mandatory fields are present.
- Requested credential formats are supported.
- Requested claim paths are well-formed.
- Query definitions do not contain unsupported combinations.
- Query structure aligns with OpenID4VP v1.0 expectations.

Validation failures should be surfaced through structured library errors.


## Scope

### 1. Validate DCQL Query Presence

Validate that:

- `dcql_query` is present when expected.
- Query object is not empty.
- Query contains at least one credential query.

Example:

```json
{
  "dcql_query": {
    "credentials": []
  }
}
```

Should be rejected.

### 2. Validate Credential Query Structure

For each credential query validate:

#### Mandatory Fields

```json
{
  "id": "identity_credential",
  "format": "dc+sd-jwt"
}
```

Required:

- id
- format

Validation should fail if any required field is missing.

### 3. Validate Supported Credential Formats

Validate requested formats against wallet-supported formats.

Examples:

Supported:

- SD-JWT
- mDOC
- JSON- LD

Out of scope - jwt_vc_json

Unsupported formats should result in validation failure.

Example:

```json
{
  "format": "unsupported_format"
}
```


### 4. Validate Claim Path Definitions

Validate requested claim paths.

Example:

```json
{
  "claims": [
    {
      "path": ["first_name"]
    }
  ]
}
```

Checks:

- path exists
- path is not empty
- path contains valid elements
- path structure is supported by the library

Invalid example:

```json
{
  "claims": [
    {
      "path": []
    }
  ]
}
```


### 5. Validate Metadata Structure

Validate metadata according to credential format.

Examples:

#### SD-JWT VC

```json
{
  "meta": {
    "vct_values": [
      "https://example.org/identity"
    ]
  }
}
```

#### mdoc

```json
{
  "meta": {
    "doctype_value": "org.iso.18013.5.1.mDL"
  }
}
```

Validation should ensure:

- Expected metadata fields are correctly structured.
- Metadata values are not empty.
- Format-specific metadata is used appropriately.


### 6. Validate Duplicate Query Identifiers

Credential query identifiers should be unique within a DCQL request.

Invalid example:

```json
{
  "credentials": [
    {
      "id": "identity"
    },
    {
      "id": "identity"
    }
  ]
}
```

Validation should fail.


### 7. Validate Supported Query Features

Only support DCQL features finalized for OpenID4VP v1.0 implementation.

Validation should reject:

- Unsupported operators
- Unsupported query constructs
- Future DCQL extensions not yet implemented

This ensures predictable wallet behavior.


### 8. Integration with Authorization Request Processing

During OpenID4VP Authorization Request processing:

1. Parse request.
2. Extract DCQL query.
3. Perform DCQL validation.
4. Return validation result.
5. Continue to credential matching only if validation succeeds.


## Technical Approach

### DCQL Validator

Introduce:

```kotlin
DCQLValidator
```

Responsibilities:

- Structural validation
- Mandatory field validation
- Format validation
- Metadata validation
- Claim path validation
- Duplicate identifier validation


### Validation Result Model

Introduce:

```kotlin
sealed class DCQLValidationResult
```

Example:

```kotlin
Success

Failure(
    code,
    message
)
```


### Validation Error Codes

Examples:

```kotlin
INVALID_DCQL_QUERY

MISSING_CREDENTIALS

MISSING_QUERY_ID

MISSING_FORMAT

UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT

INVALID_CLAIM_PATH

INVALID_METADATA

DUPLICATE_QUERY_ID

UNSUPPORTED_DCQL_FEATURE
```

These errors should be consumable by wallet applications.

## Out of Scope

- Credential matching
- Credential filtering
- VP construction
- Response encryption
- Presentation During Issuance
- Digital Credentials API validation
- Verifier trust validation


## Acceptance Criteria

### AC1 - Reject Empty DCQL Query

**Given** a DCQL query without credential definitions

**When** validation is performed

**Then** validation should fail.


### AC2 - Validate Mandatory Fields

**Given** a credential query missing mandatory fields

**When** validation is executed

**Then** validation should fail with an appropriate error.


### AC3 - Validate Credential Formats

**Given** a credential query requests an unsupported format

**When** validation is executed

**Then** validation should fail with `UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT`.


### AC4 - Validate Claim Paths

**Given** a claim path is empty or malformed

**When** validation is executed

**Then** validation should fail.

### AC5 - Validate Metadata

**Given** metadata structure does not conform to the requested credential format

**When** validation is executed

**Then** validation should fail.

### AC6 - Reject Duplicate Query IDs

**Given** multiple credential queries share the same identifier

**When** validation is executed

**Then** validation should fail.

### AC7 - Reject with Request has scope and dcql query together; then validation should fail

### AC8 - Continue Processing Only on Success

**Given** a valid DCQL query

**When** validation succeeds

**Then** credential matching processing should continue.


### AC9 - Maintain Backward Compatibility

**Given** a request that does not contain DCQL

**When** processed by the library

**Then** existing OpenID4VP request handling should remain unchanged.


## Dependencies

- OpenID4VP v1.0 Support
- DCQL Parsing Models
- Authorization Request Processing Framework


## References

- OpenID4VP 1.0 Specification
- Digital Credential Query Language (DCQL)
- OpenID4VP Version Support for V1.0 Design Document
- Inji OpenID4VP Kotlin Library

title: [Kotlin] VCI Client: Implement Nonce Endpoint Integration for Proof Generation
content:
Problem description:
**Purpose:**
Enable the wallet to fetch and use c_nonce from the issuer’s nonce endpoint for proof generation in OpenID4VCI 1.0 flows.

**Pre-requisites:**
- Story 1 completed (metadata detection)
- Token endpoint integration available
- Proof JWT generation module ready

**Basic flow:**
1. Wallet calls Token endpoint
2. Check metadata:
   - If `nonce_endpoint` exists:
     → Call nonce endpoint
3. Receive c_nonce + expiry
4. Generate proof JWT including nonce
5. Send credential request with proof

**Alternate flows:**
- If nonce endpoint absent → fallback to Draft-13 behavior (nonce from token if available)
- If nonce expired → re-fetch nonce
- If issuer does not validate nonce → proceed without blocking

**Scenarios:**
- Standard 1.0 flow (nonce required)
- Draft-13 flow (nonce optional)
- Nonce expiry scenario
- Multiple proof generation using same nonce
- Network failure while fetching nonce

**Data Fields:**
- c_nonce
- c_nonce_expires_in
- proof.jwt
- nonce_endpoint

**Business rules: (With Audit)**
- If nonce endpoint exists → nonce MUST be used in proof :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}
- Nonce must match issuer validation
- Cache nonce until expiry
- Audit:
  - Log nonce fetch
  - Log nonce usage in proof
  - Log expiry handling

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Wallet fetches nonce when endpoint exists
- Proof JWT correctly includes nonce
- Expired nonce triggers refresh
- Draft-13 flows remain unaffected
- Retry logic works for nonce failures

**Exceptions:**
- Nonce endpoint failure
- Invalid nonce response
- Expired nonce usage rejection
- Token success but nonce failure

**Documentation:**
- OpenID4VCI 1.0 Nonce Endpoint spec - https://openid.net/specs/openid-4-verifiable-credential-issuance-1_0.html
- Internal Spike Document - https://mosip.atlassian.net/wiki/external/ZmQwZTBlZTQzOTJmNDFkNmFlZWIxMDQzYjU0NWQ1YWU

**Reference UX:**
- No UI impact
- Debug logs for nonce lifecycle

**Compatibility:**
- Draft-13 (optional nonce)
- 1.0 (mandatory nonce if endpoint exists)

**Library Support:**
- Kotlin

**Implementation Details:**
- Add NonceService.swift
- Extend ProofGenerator.swift
- Add nonce cache (in-memory or secure storage)

**Non-Functional Requirements:**
- Nonce fetch latency < 1 sec
- Secure storage of nonce
- No replay attacks

Enable wallet to support new credential request structure (proofs array) and handle multi-credential responses in a single request.

**Pre-requisites:**
- Proof generation implemented

**Basic flow:**
1. Wallet prepares credential request:
   - Use credential_configuration_id
   - Include proofs array (jwt[])
2. Send request to credential endpoint
3. Receive response:
   - credentials[] array
4. Store each credential mapped to proof/key

**Alternate flows:**
- Draft-13:
  - Single proof
  - Single credential
- Deferred flow:
  - transaction_id + polling
- Partial credential issuance

**Scenarios:**
- Single proof → single credential
- Multiple proofs → multiple credentials
- Mixed proof types (jwt, attestation)
- Partial response handling
- Deferred issuance

**Data Fields:**
- credential_configuration_id
- proofs.jwt[]
- credentials[]
- transaction_id
- interval

**Business rules: (With Audit)**
- proofs must be array in 1.0 :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}
- Number of credentials may match proofs
- Same credential configuration required
- Audit:
  - Log request payload
  - Log number of proofs vs credentials
  - Log partial responses

- Wallet sends proofs array correctly
- Handles multiple credentials in response
- Backward compatible with Draft-13
- Supports deferred polling
- Supports partial issuance

- unknown_credential_configuration

title: Critically Weak Argon2i Password Hashing Configuration
content:
Problem description:
### Short Summary of the Bug

Inji Wallet uses critically weak password hashing (500 iterations instead of 600,000), making backup files vulnerable to brute-force attacks that can crack an 8-digit PIN in just 13 hours.

### Description

# Critically Weak Argon2i Password Hashing Configuration

## Issue Details

**Title:**  Argon2i Password Hashing Uses 500 Iterations Instead of Recommended 600,000

**Severity:**   - Security Vulnerability

**Type:** Security / Cryptography / Configuration

**Component:** Backup & Restore, Password Hashing


---

##  Summary

The Inji Wallet application uses an **extremely weak Argon2i configuration** for hashing backup passwords and phone numbers, making user backups **highly vulnerable to brute-force attacks**. The current implementation uses only **500 iterations** when the code itself acknowledges that **600,000 iterations** are expected - a **1,200x difference** in security strength.

---

##  Location

**File:** `shared/constants.ts`  
**Lines:** 139-146

```typescript
export const argon2iConfigForPasswordAndPhoneNumber: Argon2iConfig = {
  // TODO: expected iterations for hashing password and phone Number is 600000
  iterations: 500,        // ← CRITICALLY WEAK
  memory: 16 * 1024,
  parallelism: 2,
  hashLength: 30,
  mode: 'argon2id',
};
```

---

##  Technical Details

### Current Configuration
```typescript
{
  iterations: 500,        // Currently used
  memory: 16384,          // 16 MB
  parallelism: 2,
  hashLength: 30,
  mode: 'argon2id'
}
```

### Recommended Configuration
```typescript
{
  iterations: 600000,     // Recommended (per TODO comment)
  memory: 16384,          // 16 MB (acceptable)
  parallelism: 2,
  hashLength: 30,
  mode: 'argon2id'
}
```

### Affected Code Paths

This weak configuration is used in:

1. **Backup Encryption** - When users backup their wallet with password/phone OTP
   - File: `machines/backupAndRestore/backupWithEncryption.ts`
   - Function: Password-based backup encryption key derivation

2. **Restore Decryption** - When users restore from backup
   - File: `machines/backupAndRestore/restore/restoreMachine.ts`
   - Function: Password verification and decryption

3. **Phone Number Hashing** - For phone-based backup authentication
   - Various backup/restore utility functions

---


##  Recommended Fix

### Immediate Fix

Update the Argon2i configuration in `shared/constants.ts`:

```typescript
export const argon2iConfigForPasswordAndPhoneNumber: Argon2iConfig = {
  // Security: Increased to OWASP-recommended minimum
  iterations: 600000,     // ← Changed from 500 to 600,000
  memory: 16 * 1024,      // 16 MB (acceptable)
  parallelism: 2,
  hashLength: 30,
  mode: 'argon2id',
};
```

### Additional Security Improvements

1. **Use Random Salt Per Backup**
   ```typescript
   // Generate unique salt for each backup operation
   const generateSalt = (): string => {
     const randomBytes = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(16));
     return Buffer.from(randomBytes).toString('hex');
   };
   ```

2. **Add User-Configurable Security Level**
   ```typescript
   export const ARGON2_CONFIGS = {
     FAST: { iterations: 100000 },      // Low-end devices
     BALANCED: { iterations: 600000 },  // Recommended
     STRONG: { iterations: 1000000 },   // High security
   };
   ```

3. **Add Hardware Acceleration Detection**
   ```typescript
   // Detect device capability and adjust parameters
   const getOptimalConfig = async (): Promise<Argon2iConfig> => {
     const deviceMemory = await getAvailableMemory();
     const cpuCores = getCpuCores();
     
     if (deviceMemory < 256 * 1024 * 1024) { // < 256MB
       return { iterations: 300000, memory: 8 * 1024, parallelism: 1 };
     }
     return { iterations: 600000, memory: 16 * 1024, parallelism: 2 };
   };
   ```



## 💬 Additional Notes

The TODO comment in the code (`// TODO: expected iterations for hashing password and phone Number is 600000`) indicates that the developers were **aware** of this issue but it was never addressed. This suggests:

1. The issue was identified but deprioritized
2. May have been waiting for performance testing
3. Could be blocked by legacy device support concerns

**Recommendation:** Address immediately with proper performance testing on minimum-spec devices (minSdkVersion 24) to ensure acceptable UX while maintaining security.

---

Discussion and resolution:
[aniket866]: @Tomeshwari-02 
please assign

[Kaushikgupta469]: Hii @Tomeshwari-02 

Thank you for highlighting the Argon2i configuration issue and bringing it to the attention of the Inji Wallet team.

Currently, the backup and restore flow in Inji Wallet does not use hashing in the manner described in the report. The referenced configuration is applicable only for flows where backup and restore support password/phone-number-based hashing.

However, Argon2i/Argon2id is used in other security-sensitive areas such as passcode-related functionality. Your findings are valuable, and we are reviewing the configuration and overall implementation internally.

We appreciate the detailed report and responsible disclosure.

title: INJIMOB-3180: Retry VC download if error is invalid_proof[Kotlin]
content:
Problem description:
Ensure that when a Verifiable Credential (VC) download fails due to an `invalid*proof` error, the `vci-client` library automatically retries the VC download using a **new proof** generated with a **fresh** `c*nonce`, improving reliability of the credential issuance flow.

## Scope & Functionality

### Expected Behavior:

- When a `credential_endpoint` returns an error like:
```
{
  "error": "invalid_proof"
}
```
→ the client should retry VC download **once** with a new `proof`.

## Changes Required

### 1. **Error Detection**

In the part of the code where the response from `credential_endpoint` is handled:

- Detect when `error === "invalid_proof"`

### 2. **Retry Logic**

On detecting `invalid_proof`:

- Fetch a new `c_nonce` (either from token endpoint again or from error response if available).
- Regenerate **proof JWT** via the `requestProof()` hook using the new nonce.
- Retry calling the `credential_endpoint`.

### 3. **Add a Retry Cap**

- Avoid infinite loops:
*** Allow *only one retry** per VC request.
** Optional config: `maxRetryAttempts` (default to 1).

### 4. **Logging & Error Propagation**

- Log the retry attempt with context:
** Issuer URL
** Proof generation timestamps
- If retry also fails, propagate the final error back to the caller with full trace/log context.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Success Retry

1. Mock the `credential*endpoint` to return `invalid*proof` on first attempt, valid VC on second.
1. Assert VC is successfully downloaded after one retry.

### Retry Fails

1. Mock both attempts to return `invalid_proof`.
1. Assert that the retry stops after 1 attempt and a proper error is returned.

### No Retry Needed

1. Mock success on first attempt.
1. Assert that retry logic is not invoked.

## Affected Components

- `credential-request.ts` or wherever the actual `fetchVC()` or `callCredentialEndpoint()` is handled.
- `requestProof()` hook interface – ensure it can be re-triggered with new nonce.
- Possibly `exchangeToken()` if `c_nonce` needs to be re-fetched.

## Optional Enhancements

- Emit a `retryAttempted(reason)` hook for Wallet UI to show retry is in progress.
- Configurable backoff (exponential or fixed delay) before retry.

## References

- OpenID4CI Spec - Credential Request
- MOSIP Implementation Learnings: `invalid*proof` may occur due to expired/mismatched `c*nonce`.

title: INJIMOB-3245: [VC-VERIFIER] Verification Method Retrieval
content:
Problem description:
As a verifier, I want to retrieve and validate a cryptographic verification method (e.g., public key) using a verification method identifier, so that I can safely perform cryptographic verification (e.g., signature checks) in a trusted and secure manner.

### **Purpose**

To securely and reliably fetch a cryptographic verification method (e.g., a public key) associated with a DID (Decentralized Identifier), ensuring the key:

- Belongs to the correct controller,
- Is correctly declared in the controller’s DID document,
- Has the right verification relationship (e.g., `authentication`, `assertionMethod`),
- Has not been tampered with or spoofed via caching or hijacking.

### **Pre-requisites**

- The VC-Verifier system must support DID Resolution and Dereferencing based on the DID method in use.
- The verification method identifier must be in URL format.
- Network access to retrieve external DID Documents.
- The verifier must understand the media type of the DID Document (e.g., JSON-LD).
- Retrieve Verification Method- [https://www.w3.org/TR/cid-1.0/#retrieve-verification-method](https://www.w3.org/TR/cid-1.0/#retrieve-verification-method|smart-link) 
- Processing error - [https://www.w3.org/TR/cid-1.0/#processing-errors](https://www.w3.org/TR/cid-1.0/#processing-errors|smart-link) 

### **Basic Flow**

1. **Input**:
Receive the following inputs:
#* `vmIdentifier`: Verification method URL (e.g., `https://controller.example/123#key-456`)
#* `verificationRelationship`: Relationship to validate (e.g., `authentication`, `assertionMethod`)
#* `options`: Dereferencing options (e.g., headers, caching policies)
1. **Validate Input**:
#* Check that `vmIdentifier` is a valid URL.
#* If not, throw error `INVALID*VERIFICATION*METHOD_URL`.
1. **Parse URL**:
#* Extract `controllerDocumentUrl`: the part before `#`.
#* Extract `vmFragment`: the part after `#`.
1. **Dereference DID Document**:
#* Fetch the DID Document from `controllerDocumentUrl` using `options`.
1. **Validate DID Document**:
#* Ensure it’s a valid controlled identifier document.
#* Validate that `controllerDocument.id === controllerDocumentUrl`.
#* If not, throw `INVALID*CONTROLLED*IDENTIFIER*DOCUMENT` or `INVALID*CONTROLLED*IDENTIFIER*DOCUMENT_ID`.
1. **Extract Verification Method**:
#* Find `vmFragment` in the DID Document using fragment dereferencing logic.
1. **Validate Verification Method**:
#* Ensure it’s a valid verification method.
#* Ensure `verificationMethod.id === vmIdentifier`.
#* Ensure `verificationMethod.controller === controllerDocumentUrl`.
#* Ensure the method is referenced under the correct `verificationRelationship` in the DID Document.
1. **Return**:
#* If all checks pass, return the full `verificationMethod` object for downstream cryptographic operations (e.g., signature verification).

### **Technical Implementation Notes**

#### Data Model

- `vmIdentifier: string` (e.g., `https://controller.example/123#key-456`)
- `verificationRelationship: string` (e.g., `authentication`)
- `controllerDocument: DIDDocument` – dereferenced JSON document
- `verificationMethod: VerificationMethod` – extracted key object

### **Errors**

||Error Code||Description||
|`INVALID*VERIFICATION*METHOD_URL`|`vmIdentifier` is not a valid URL|
|`INVALID*CONTROLLED*IDENTIFIER_DOCUMENT`|Malformed or non-conformant DID Document|
|`INVALID*CONTROLLED*IDENTIFIER*DOCUMENT*ID`|`id` in DID Doc doesn't match expected controller|
|`INVALID*VERIFICATION*METHOD`|Method doesn't match identifier or lacks structure|
|`INVALID*RELATIONSHIP*FOR*VERIFICATION*METHOD`|Method not in declared verification relationship|

Discussion and resolution:
[Ivanmeneges]: **Jira Assignee:** Alka Prasad (no GitHub mapping found)

[Ivanmeneges]: Alka Prasad commented: # As part of this [PR|https://github.com/mosip/vc-verifier/pull/99], the logic of getting the verification method from the did document is updated from finding first to finding the verification method whose id matches with the given did URI.
# RSASignature2018: 
[+https://www.w3.org/2018/credentials/v1+|https://www.w3.org/2018/credentials/v1] -> This says the signature can either be jws/ proofValue
[https://w3c-ccg.github.io/lds-rsa2018/#examples|https://w3c-ccg.github.io/lds-rsa2018/#examples|smart-link]   
[https://w3c-ccg.github.io/lds-rsa2018/#modifications-to-signature-algorithm|https://w3c-ccg.github.io/lds-rsa2018/#modifications-to-signature-algorithm|smart-link]   → The above two links suggest that the signature would come as signatureValue.

title: INJIMOB-3263: Retry VC Download if error is invalid_proof [Swift]
content:
Problem description:
Ensure that when a Verifiable Credential (VC) download fails due to an `invalid*proof` error, the `vci-client` library automatically retries the VC download using a **new proof** generated with a **fresh** `c*nonce`, improving the reliability of the credential issuance flow. New `c_nonce` is generated, and no new access token is generated

**Draft 13 openIDVCI Spec** - [https://openid.net/specs/openid-4-verifiable-credential-issuance-1*0-ID1.html#name-credential-issuer-provided-](https://openid.net/specs/openid-4-verifiable-credential-issuance-1*0-ID1.html#name-credential-issuer-provided-|smart-link) 

## Scope & Functionality

### Expected Behaviour:

- When a `credential_endpoint` returns an error like:
```
{
  "error": "invalid_proof"
}
```
→ the client should retry VC download **once** with a new `proof`.
- Below is a non-normative example of a Credential Response when the Credential Issuer is requesting a Wallet to provide in a subsequent Credential Request a key proof that is bound to a `c_nonce`:
```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json
Cache-Control: no-store

{
  "error": "invalid_proof"
  "error_description":
       "Credential Issuer requires key proof to be bound to a Credential Issuer provided nonce.",
  "c_nonce": "8YE9hCnyV2",
  "c*nonce*expires_in": 86400
}
```

## Changes Required

### 1. **Error Detection**

In the part of the code where the response from `credential_endpoint` is handled:

- Detect when `error === "invalid_proof"`

### 2. **Retry Logic**

On detecting `invalid_proof`:

- Fetch a new `c_nonce` (either from token endpoint again or from error response if available).
- Regenerate **proof JWT** via the `requestProof()` hook using the new nonce.
- Retry calling the `credential_endpoint`.

### 3. **Add a Retry Cap**

- Avoid infinite loops:
*** Allow *only one retry** per VC request.
** Optional config: `maxRetryAttempts` (default to 1).

### 4. **Logging & Error Propagation**

- Log the retry attempt with context:
** Issuer URL
** Proof generation timestamps
- If retry also fails, propagate the final error back to the caller with full trace/log context.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Success Retry

1. Mock the `credential*endpoint` to return `invalid*proof` on first attempt, valid VC on second.
1. Assert VC is successfully downloaded after one retry.

### Retry Fails

1. Mock both attempts to return `invalid_proof`.
1. Assert that the retry stops after 1 attempt and a proper error is returned.

### No Retry Needed

1. Mock success on first attempt.
1. Assert that retry logic is not invoked.

## Affected Components

- `credential-request.ts` or wherever the actual `fetchVC()` or `callCredentialEndpoint()` is handled.
- `requestProof()` hook interface – ensure it can be re-triggered with new nonce.
- Possibly `exchangeToken()` if `c_nonce` needs to be re-fetched.

## Optional Enhancements

- Emit a `retryAttempted(reason)` hook for Wallet UI to show retry is in progress.
- Configurable backoff (exponential or fixed delay) before retry.

## References

- OpenID4CI Spec - Credential Request
- MOSIP Implementation Learnings: `invalid*proof` may occur due to expired/mismatched `c*nonce`.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Check the internal logs in the adb. (Adding in telemetry)
- An external issuer can be used to verify error messages 
- Feature health check
- Expiry time of `c_nonce` comes from the issuer, and this is optional also as per the spec.
- `c_nonce` is active only for one request if the expiry time is not set defined by the issuer.
- Retry can only happen once if the proof is invalid

title: INJIMOB-3564: Credential refresh for Inji Stack
content:
Problem description:
**Implementation needed on Certify, Wallet:**

- [https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#refreshing](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#refreshing|smart-link) 
- [https://openid.net/specs/openid-4-verifiable-credential-issuance-1*0.html#name-refreshing-issued-credentia](https://openid.net/specs/openid-4-verifiable-credential-issuance-1*0.html#name-refreshing-issued-credentia|smart-link) 

**Details:**

This specification defines a `refreshService` [property](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-property), which enables an [issuer](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-issuers) to include a link to a refresh service.

The [issuer](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-issuers) can include the refresh service as an element inside the [verifiable credential](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-verifiable-credential) if it is intended for either the [verifier](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-verifier) or the [holder](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-holders) (or both), or inside the [verifiable presentation](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-verifiable-presentation) if it is intended for the [holder](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-holders) only. In the latter case, this enables the [holder](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-holders) to refresh the [verifiable credential](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-verifiable-credential) before creating a [verifiable presentation](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-verifiable-presentation) to share with a [verifier](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-verifier). In the former case, including the refresh service inside the [verifiable credential](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-verifiable-credential) enables either the [holder](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-holders) or the [verifier](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-verifier) to perform future updates of the [credential](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-credential).

The refresh service is only expected to be used when either the [credential](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-credential) has expired or the [issuer](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-issuers) does not publish [credential](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-credential) status information. [Issuers](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-issuers) are advised not to put the `refreshService` [property](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-property) in a [verifiable credential](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-verifiable-credential) that does not contain public information or whose refresh service is not protected in some way.

```
refreshService
```

The value of the `refreshService` [property](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-property) *MUST* be one or more refresh services that provides enough information to the recipient's software such that the recipient can refresh the [verifiable credential](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-verifiable-credential). Each `refreshService` value *MUST* specify its `type`. The precise content of each refresh service is determined by the specific `refreshService` [type](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-type) definition.

Use of the refreshService property by an issuer

```
{
  "@context": [
    "https://www.w3.org/ns/credentials/v2",
    "https://w3id.org/age/v1"
  ],
  "type": ["VerifiableCredential", "AgeVerificationCredential"],
  "issuer": "did:key:z6MksFxi8wnHkNq4zgEskSZF45SuWQ4HndWSAVYRRGe9qDks",
  "validFrom": "2024-04-03T00:00:00.000Z",
  "validUntil": "2024-12-15T00:00:00.000Z",
  "name": "Age Verification Credential",
  "credentialSubject": {
    "overAge": 21
  },
  "refreshService": {
    "type": "VerifiableCredentialRefreshService2021",
    "url": "https://registration.provider.example/flows/reissue-age-token",
    "refreshToken": "z2BJYfNtmWRiouWhDrbDQmC2zicUPBxsPg"
  }
}
```

In the example above, the [issuer](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-issuers) specifies an automatic `refreshService` that can be used by POSTing the [verifiable credential](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-verifiable-credential) to the refresh service `url`. Note that this particular verifiable credential is not intended to be shared with anyone except for the original issuer.

Note: Non-authenticated credential refresh

Placing a `refreshService` [property](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-property) in a [verifiable credential](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-verifiable-credential) so that it is available to [verifiers](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-verifier) can remove control and consent from the [holder](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-holders) and allow the [verifiable credential](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-verifiable-credential) to be issued directly to the [verifier](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-verifier), thereby bypassing the [holder](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/#dfn-holders).

title: INJIMOB-3612: Revocation Feature enhancements
content:
Problem description:
**“Last Checked”** means *the last time the wallet attempted to check status* — not whether it succeeded.
It should always update when the user manually refreshes or when an auto-refresh occurs.

This provides the user a clear signal:

{quote}“The wallet last tried to verify your credential’s status at [timestamp].”{quote}

### **Rationale for always updating timestamp**

- **User Transparency:** It helps users know when the last verification *attempt* happened, even if the backend or network failed.
- **Debugging clarity:** Easier to differentiate between network or verification failures and old cached data.
- **Consistency:** Keeps the “Last Checked” label meaningful in all states — success, revoked, expired, or failed.

### Important: Distinguish in UI

To avoid confusion, ensure UI clearly separates:

- `Status: Revoked / Valid / Unknown`
- `Last Checked: <timestamp>`

If the last check failed (due to connectivity or backend issue), you can optionally show:

{quote}“Last checked at [time] — status could not be verified.”{quote}

### **Summary**

||Concept||Definition||Updated when||
|**Last Checked**|Timestamp of last status check attempt|Always (on every check attempt)|
|**Last Known Status**|Latest successfully verified status|Only when status check succeeds|

title: INJIMOB-3722: Support CWT Verification for Android in vc-verifier
content:
Problem description:
Currently, `vc-verifier` supports CWT (COSE_Sign1) verification using the **Authlete COSE** library.
This works correctly in JVM environments (backend, unit tests), but **fails on Android** due to cryptographic limitations in the Android runtime.

Android does **not support** the JCA algorithm:

```
SHA256withECDSAinP1363Format
```

This algorithm is internally used by the current COSE library when verifying **ES256 (-7)** signatures, which causes CWT verification to fail on Android.

Although there is **no mobile application at present**, a future Android application will require **CWT verification on-device**.
This card tracks the required changes to ensure Android compatibility when a mobile app is introduced.

### Proposed Solution (For Future Mobile Support)

Adopt an Android-compatible COSE verification approach by either:

- Forking and patching the existing Authlete COSE library, **or**
- Switching to an alternative COSE library that:
** Uses `SHA256withECDSA`
** Explicitly converts COSE P1363 signatures to DER before verification

### Reference Library (Android-compatible)

- **Library**: `se.digg.cose`
- **Why it works on Android**:
** Uses `SHA256withECDSA`
*** Performs explicit *P1363 → DER** conversion before signature verification
** Fully compatible with Android crypto providers

This library can be used as:

- A direct replacement for Android, or
- A reference implementation while patching Authlete COSE.

title: INJIMOB-3785: Adaptive Biometric Icon Based on Device OS and Supported Authentication Method (Android)
content:
Problem description:
**As an Inji Wallet user,**
I want the app to automatically detect whether my device supports **Face Authentication** or **Fingerprint Authentication**,
so that the **correct biometric icon and label** are displayed based on my device’s OS and biometric capability, ensuring a clear and intuitive user experience.

## **Problem Statement**

Currently, the app displays a **fingerprint icon** even on devices (especially newer iOS models) that **do not support fingerprint** and only support **Face Authentication**. This creates confusion and an inconsistent user experience across platforms.

The Inji Wallet mobile app should dynamically:

- Detect the **device OS** (Android or iOS) - Android should be above **8* for fingerprint and face unlock, and iOS should be above **14*
- Detect **supported biometric type** (Fingerprint / Face )
- Display the **appropriate biometric icon and label** in relevant screens (e.g., Settings, Unlock screen)

### Expected Behaviour:

[https://www.figma.com/design/F6HYVibHTUUWicHMFfBgjM/Inji-Wallet-App?node-id=1977-299&p=f&t=s3HqgyvSreooq8Fu-0](https://www.figma.com/design/F6HYVibHTUUWicHMFfBgjM/Inji-Wallet-App?node-id=1977-299&p=f&t=s3HqgyvSreooq8Fu-0|smart-link) 

- On devices supporting **Face ID / Face Unlock** → Show **Face Auth icon**
- On devices supporting **Fingerprint** → Show **Fingerprint icon**
- On devices supporting **both** → Prefer OS-recommended primary biometric (Fallback image can be a face icon(Android + iOS if the device supports both and both are enabled)
- On devices supporting **none** → Hide biometric option or show disabled state (Optional can be skipped based on device availability)
- Ensure **consistent UI behaviour across Android & iOS**

+**iOS Face Icon**+

+**Andriod Face Icon**+

+**iOS and Android Fingerprint Icon**+

## **Acceptance Criteria**

- App detects whether the device supports **Fingerprint**, **Face Authentication**, or both
- The correct biometric **icon** is displayed based on the detected capability
- Correct biometric **label** is shown (e.g., *Unlock with Face ID*, *Unlock with Fingerprint*)
- Behaviour works consistently on **Android and iOS**
- No fingerprint icon is shown on devices that **do not support fingerprint**
- UI updates dynamically across **Settings**, **Login**, and **Unlock** screens
- No regression in existing biometric login functionality

## **Scenarios**

||**Device Type**||**Biometric Support**||**Expected Icon**||
|iPhone (Face ID only)|Face|Face icon|
|Older iPhone (Touch ID)|Fingerprint|Fingerprint icon|
|Android (Fingerprint only)|Fingerprint|Fingerprint icon|
|Android (Face Unlock only)|Face|Face icon|
|Device with no biometric|None|Hide or disable biometric option|

## **Business Value**

- Improves **user trust and clarity**
- Ensures **platform-consistent UX**
- Prevents **confusion caused by incorrect biometric icons**
- Aligns with **modern device biometric standards**
- Enhances **Inji Wallet UI polish and professionalism**

## **Subtasks** 

- Detect biometric capability on Android
- Detect biometric capability on iOS
- Update biometric icons and labels in UI
- Regression testing on multiple device models
- UX validation and design update

title: INJIMOB-3376: Claims Not Displayed in 'No Matching Credentials Found' Error Screen
labels: bug, inji_mobile_githubmovement, inji_mobile_bug_github_movement, qa-inji_mob_release0180, inji_mob_sprint_15_2025, qa-inji_mob_release0180_reopened, inji_mob_sprint_14_2025
content:
Problem description:
When the wallet encounters a "No matching credentials found" scenario during the VP (Verifiable Presentation) flow, the error screen is supposed to display the list of claims requested by the verifier. However, the claims list is currently displayed as an empty array `[]`, even when the verifier has sent valid claims in the presentation definition.

**Steps to Reproduce:**

1. Trigger a VP request from the verifier with specific claims.
1. Open the QR code on your wallet and proceed with the sharing flow.
1. If there are no matching credentials in the wallet, the error screen is shown.
1. Observe the placeholder for claims: `[]` is shown instead of actual claim names.

**Expected Result:**
The error screen should show the actual claims requested by the verifier so the user knows what credentials are missing.

**Actual Result:**
The claims section appears as `[]` (empty array) on the UI.

**Impact:**

- Poor user experience: The User is unaware of what specific credential(s) to download.
- Debugging becomes harder for verifiers and users.
- Incomplete communication of request context.

**Suggested Fix:**
Ensure that the claims extracted from the `presentation_definition` or equivalent request object are parsed and displayed correctly on the UI.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
If **no fields are requested by the verifier** (i.e., the presentation definition has no input descriptors or constraints), then showing an empty claim list like `[]` is confusing.

**Fallback message** should be showcased instead:

**Header:**
**No matching credentials found!**

**Message:**
We couldn’t find any credentials in your wallet that match this request. You may need to download the right credentials or try again later.
{panel}

title: INJIMOB-3474: iOS – Mock VC with v2 context (ldp_vc) not sharable via OVP; shows “Something went wrong” after scanning QR
content:
Problem description:
When attempting to share a mock Verifiable Credential (VC) with **v2 context (**`ldp_vc`**)* using the OVP flow on *Inji Mobile (iOS)**, the app displays a **“Something went wrong”** error message. No related error logs are seen in the terminal.

This issue is **not related to Verifier authorization request validation**, but rather due to the fact that **v2 context VCs are not sharable via OVP**, since the **Verifiable Presentation (VP)** is constructed as **v1 context**.

**Steps:**

1. Install the inji application
1. Open Inji app
1. Download VCs. mock vc
1. Open the OVP or code in Chrome browser 
1. Scan the QR code on the injimobile 
1. After scanning the QR code, choose MOCK VC and share

**Observed:** After removing the MDL from the presentation definition mock JSON file and scanning the QR code on InjiMobile, we are seeing a 'Something went wrong' error message. No errors are being logged in the terminal either.

!iOS Device 2025-08-05 17-51-50.mp4|width=592,height=1440,alt="iOS Device 2025-08-05 17-51-50.mp4"!

**Expected:**  The user should be able to share the mock VC without encountering any errors.

**Wallet Device:**
Phone make/model: iPhone 14
OS: IOS 18.5
BLE version : 5.3
Mimoto version:
MOSIP Version: 0.18.0
APP link:  [https://play.google.com/apps/test/io.mosip.residentapp/20](https://play.google.com/apps/test/io.mosip.residentapp/200)5
IPA test flight version: Orange - 0.18.0 (11)

### Attachments

Discussion and resolution:
[Ivanmeneges]: Kiruthika J commented: *Findings*

*_Root cause_*

{quote}Canonicalization failure is occuring with context - {{"@context": ["https://www.w3.org/ns/credentials/v2", "https://vharsh.github.io/DID/mock-context.json"]}}{quote}

*_Logs / Screen recordings_*

* Android

{noformat}2025-08-06 12:38:42.747 14581-14761 ReactNativeJS           io.mosip.residentapp                 E  'Error:', 'There was a problem encountered loading a remote context [code=LOADING_REMOTE_CONTEXT_FAILED].', 'ERR_UNKNOWN'{noformat}

Note: qa-inji1 → mock → last credential type has context {{"https://www.w3.org/ns/credentials/v2"}} which is causing issue on VP construction

!injimob-3474.mov|width=3456,height=1890,alt="injimob-3474.mov"!

* iOS

{noformat}'Canonization failed:', { [jsonld.SyntaxError: Invalid JSON-LD syntax; tried to redefine "VerifiableCredential" which is a protected term.]
  name: 'jsonld.SyntaxError',
  details: 
   { code: 'protected term redefinition',{noformat}

attachment - [^canc.log] 

_More details:_

VC with context as below is causing cononicalization failure

{noformat}"@context": ["https://www.w3.org/ns/credentials/v2", "https://vharsh.github.io/DID/mock-context.json"]{noformat}

And as of now its happening in Android device and iOS (logs attached, screen recording attached)

cc: [~accountid:639195c95fc160544e1df6df] [~accountid:557058:cc7f3f06-5f70-4e7e-a2e3-4de09e09e29b]

[Ivanmeneges]: nitin.k commented: Hi [~accountid:70121:a52958ed-5a7c-47c7-8764-43b057751667] ,

# Verified OVP for mock VC 

* iOS - working fine
* Android - getting 'Soemthing went wrong'

Video:

ADB Logs:

[^Android_3474_realme-RMX3371-Android-14_2025-08-07_094554.logcat]

NOTE: No errors from mock services side

*One more observation is* 

# VC is getting verified at Android and status is 'Pending' from iOS side

!image-20250807-041801.png|width=820,height=985,alt="image-20250807-041801.png"!

[Ivanmeneges]: Kiruthika J commented: Hi [~accountid:712020:e382cb85-926e-4bb7-951e-8b6647c51bb0] 
This is depending on the VC with context as 

{noformat}"@context": ["https://www.w3.org/ns/credentials/v2", "https://vharsh.github.io/DID/mock-context.json"]{noformat}

As of analysis, have noticed the canonicalization failure for VP construction which has VC with above mentioned context 

From the issuer → Mock (qa-inji1) one of the credential type has this context which is causing failure in both the platforms

[Ivanmeneges]: nitin.k commented: Hi [~accountid:70121:a52958ed-5a7c-47c7-8764-43b057751667] ,

Verified with the same 3rd credential type from mock issuer in both iOS and Android. either it should have failed or pass - based on the context is valid OR not as per my understanding

[Ivanmeneges]: Kiruthika J commented: Update:

Connected with [~accountid:712020:e382cb85-926e-4bb7-951e-8b6647c51bb0] [~accountid:639195c95fc160544e1df6df]  reg the bug

* credential type v2 under qa-inji1 mock issuer is having the issue
* There is a difference in ordering of credential types b/w iOS and Android which caused the confusion

cc: [~accountid:712020:e382cb85-926e-4bb7-951e-8b6647c51bb0] [~accountid:639195c95fc160544e1df6df] [~accountid:557058:cc7f3f06-5f70-4e7e-a2e3-4de09e09e29b]

[Ivanmeneges]: Kiruthika J commented: As per the downloaded mock VC, proof type is {{Ed25519Signature2020}} 

* This type of VC is ignored for VC verification in iOS ([ref|https://github.com/mosip/inji-wallet/blob/develop/shared/vcjs/verifyCredential.ts#L83]) // reason: VC verification in iOS uses digital-bazaar which does not support this proof type. 
* Due to this , in iOS the canonicalization happens only during VP construction which fails due to “redefinition of protected term“ error

[Ivanmeneges]: Kiruthika J commented: VP is contsructed with context v1 so if any v2 context VC is present inside the VP, we are facing context loading issue

Attaching error from univerifier:

!image-20250811-044058.png|width=1724,height=835,alt="image-20250811-044058.png"!

*Action:*

* raise issue in openid4vp github spec reg managing the VP with VCs having v2 context

[Ivanmeneges]: Kiruthika J commented: Github issue raised in openid4vp repo - [https://github.com/openid/OpenID4VP/issues/664|https://github.com/openid/OpenID4VP/issues/664|smart-link]

[Ivanmeneges]: Kiruthika J commented: Update:

Date: {{2025-08-11}} 

* Raised Github issue to ovp spec reg mixing of v1 and v2 context for VP - [https://github.com/openid/OpenID4VP/issues/664|https://github.com/openid/OpenID4VP/issues/664|smart-link]

[Ivanmeneges]: Kiruthika J commented: Update:

* For the issue opened, its suggested to maintain 2 VPs for each Data model of ldp_vc
* Ref - [https://github.com/openid/OpenID4VP/issues/664#issuecomment-3183166922|https://github.com/openid/OpenID4VP/issues/664#issuecomment-3183166922|smart-link]

[Ivanmeneges]: sanchi singh commented: [~accountid:639195c95fc160544e1df6df] [~accountid:712020:e382cb85-926e-4bb7-951e-8b6647c51bb0] I have updated the title to avoid confusion based on inputs and analysis from [~accountid:70121:a52958ed-5a7c-47c7-8764-43b057751667] can you please check from your end as well if this is ok

title: INJIMOB-3738: INJIMOBILE – During the credential offer flow, if the issue name is long, the trusted screen issue name UI alignment and action buttons are not displayed correctly.
content:
Problem description:
**Steps:**

1. Open the animo in the browser.
1. Select the **Bundeszentralamt fur Steuern** issuer.
1. Scroll down and choose the Credential Format as mdoc
1. Select the **Authentication** code as the transaction code
1. Click on the issue credential
1. In injimobileapp, click on the + icon and choose the scan download option
1. Scan the animo QR Code
1. Check in the trusted screen 

**Observed:**  During the credential offer flow, if the issue name is long, the trusted screen issue name UI alignment and action buttons are not displayed correctly.

**Expected Result:**
During the credential offer flow, the trusted screen issue name and action buttons should be properly aligned and displayed correctly, even when the issue name is long. The UI should adapt dynamically without overlapping, misalignment, or truncation issues.

### Ticket Contents

As part of enhancing credential display capabilities, we need to explore support for SVG-based rendering of SD-JWT VCs in the wallet. This spike aims to analyze how SVG templates (as per SD-JWT VC spec metadata) can be used to dynamically render credentials in a visually rich and standardized format.

The analysis should refer to the SD-JWT VC specification (Type Metadata section) and evaluate:

- How rendering metadata is provided
- How SVG templates can be interpreted and rendered
- How this can be integrated into existing wallet rendering logic


### Goals & Mid-Point Milestone

1. Understand how SVG rendering is defined in the SD-JWT VC spec
2. Identify how rendering metadata is structured and consumed
3. Evaluate the feasibility of:
- Parsing SVG templates
- Binding credential data to SVG
4. Identify changes required in:
- Wallet rendering layer
- Credential parsing layer
5. Define an approach for the dynamic rendering of credentials using SVG


### Setup/Installation

No setup and installation needed as it is a spike and research

1. Clear understanding of:

- SVG rendering support in SD-JWT VC
- Metadata structure for rendering

2. Documented approach for:

- Parsing SVG templates
- Injecting credential data into templates
- Rendering in mobile/web wallet

3. Identified:

- Technical dependencies
- Risks and limitations

4. Proposed step-by-step implementation plan documented


### Acceptance Criteria

1. SD-JWT VC spec (rendering/type metadata) is analyzed and summarized
2. SVG rendering approach is clearly documented
3. Feasibility of SVG rendering in:

- Android (Kotlin)
- iOS (Swift)

4. Data binding strategy between:

- Credential claims
- SVG placeholders is defined

5. Edge cases identified:

- Missing fields
- Invalid SVG
- Unsupported attributes

6. Final output includes:

- Architecture approach
- Implementation steps
- Open questions / risks


### Implementation Details

Spec reference:

- https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-oauth-sd-jwt-vc/
- https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-oauth-sd-jwt-vc-10.html#ExampleTypeMetadata 

### 1. Spec Analysis

### Review
- SD-JWT VC **Type Metadata section**

### Identify
- How rendering templates are provided  
- Expected format of SVG templates  
- Structure of metadata carrying rendering instructions  

### 2. Rendering Approach Evaluation

### Evaluate

- [ ] Static SVG vs Dynamic SVG  
  - Static → predefined templates  
  - Dynamic → data-driven rendering  

- [ ] Inline SVG vs External Template  
  - Inline → embedded within metadata  
  - External → fetched via URL/reference  


### Considerations

- [ ] Nested claim handling  
- [ ] Fallback values for missing fields

- [ ] Identify required libraries  
- [ ] Evaluate performance considerations

- [ ] Identify native vs third-party support

- [ ] Credential Parsing Layer  
  - Extract rendering metadata  
  - Handle SVG templates  

- [ ] Rendering Engine  
  - Bind data to SVG  
  - Render dynamically  

- [ ] UI Components  
  - Display rendered SVG  
  - Handle responsiveness  

### 6. Error Handling Strategy

Define handling for:

- [ ] Invalid SVG → fallback to default rendering  
- [ ] Missing data fields → show placeholder/fallback  
- [ ] Rendering failures → display error state  

## 7. Output Deliverables

  - Rendering flow  
  - Data mapping strategy  
  - Sample SVG template  

### Implementation Planning
- [ ] Suggested implementation approach

- [ ] Effort estimation

- Feasibility assessment across platforms

- Actionable next steps for implementation

The `rendering` key in Type Metadata supports two methods:

`VCProcessor.ts` already produces a `fullResolvedPayload` from the SD-JWT - this can flow directly into the native binding layer with minimal changes.

title: Spike : DCQL Analysis with OpenIDVP v1.0
content:
Problem description:
**Digital Credentials Query Language (DCQL)**
[OpenID for Verifiable Presentations 1.0](https://openid.net/specs/openid-4-verifiable-presentations-1_0.html#section-6) 

The Digital Credentials Query Language (DCQL, pronounced [ˈdakl̩]) is a JSON-encoded query language that allows the Verifier to request Presentations that match the query. The Verifier MAY encode constraints on the combinations of Credentials and claims that are requested. The Wallet evaluates the query against the Credentials it holds and returns Presentations matching the query.

A valid DCQL query is defined as a JSON-encoded object with the following top-level properties:

credentials:

REQUIRED. A non-empty array of Credential Queries as defined in [Section 6.1](https://openid.net/specs/openid-4-verifiable-presentations-1_0.html#credential_query) that specify the requested Credentials.

credential_sets:

OPTIONAL. A non-empty array of Credential Set Queries as defined in [Section 6.2](https://openid.net/specs/openid-4-verifiable-presentations-1_0.html#credential_set_query) that specifies additional constraints on which of the requested Credentials to return.

Note: Future extensions may define additional properties both at the top level and in the rest of the DCQL data structure. Implementations MUST ignore any unknown properties.

**Spike Document** - https://mosip.atlassian.net/wiki/external/ZjcwZDBkODcyYTdiNDcwMjg5MGI0YTg2YmQ4MTI0YWI

title: [Kotlin] VCI Client: Support Updated Issuer Metadata & Nonce Endpoint Discovery (OpenID4VCI 1.0)
content:
Problem description:
**Purpose:**
Enable Kotlin-based wallet to detect issuer version (Draft-13 vs 1.0) via metadata and support nonce endpoint discovery.

**Pre-requisites:**
- Metadata fetch module
- Android networking layer ready

**Basic flow:**
1. Wallet scans or receives credential offer
2. Extract issuer identifier
3. Construct well-known metadata URL (1.0 compliant insertion logic)
4. Fetch metadata
5. Parse metadata:
   - If `nonce_endpoint` exists → classify as VCI 1.0
   - Else:
     - If `display` or display attributes exist → classify as Draft-13
     - Else fallback → VCI 1.0
6. Store issuer version context for further flows

**Alternate flows:**
- If metadata partially available → fallback detection using display attributes
- If issuer supports both → prioritize 1.0 detection
- If metadata missing fields → continue with safe defaults (fields are optional)

title: [Swift] Encryption Process for direct_post.jwt
content:
Problem description:
## Purpose
Implement spec-compliant encryption for VP responses in Swift using OpenID4VP 1.0 (direct_post.jwt), aligning with Kotlin implementation.

## Pre-requisites
- VP response successfully constructed and signed  
- Verifier public key (JWKS) available  
- direct_post.jwt flow supported  

## Basic Flow
1. Wallet receives signed VP token  
2. Extract verifier public key from metadata  
3. Generate shared key using:
   - ECDH (Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman)  
   - Concat KDF (Key Derivation Function)  
4. Apply encryption (e.g., A256GCM / supported enc values)  
5. Send encrypted VP response to verifier  

## Alternate Flows
- Fallback to default encryption (A128GCM) if not specified  
- Multiple `enc` values supported by verifier  
- Missing encryption config → fail or fallback based on config  

## Scenarios
- direct_post.jwt response encryption  
- Encryption with `apu` / `apv` parameters  
- Verifier supporting multiple encryption algorithms  

##Data Fields
- `clientId`  
- `nonce`  
- `responseUri`  
- `jwkThumbprint`  
- `apu`  
- `apv`  
- `encrypted_response_enc_values_supported`  

## Business Rules (With Audit)
- Default encryption: A128GCM (if not specified)  
- Encryption must use context binding:
  - Algorithm  
  - `apu`  
  - `apv`  
- Wallet MUST log:
  - Encryption start  
  - Key derivation process  
  - Encryption success/failure  

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Swift supports ECDH-based encryption  
- [ ] Concat KDF implemented as per spec  
- [ ] Supports multiple encryption algorithms  
- [ ] Encrypted VP response successfully sent  
- [ ] Matches Kotlin behavior  

## Exceptions
- Missing verifier public key → fail encryption  
- Encryption failure → reject response  
- Unsupported encryption algorithm → error  

## Documentation
- OpenID4VP 1.0 Encryption Specification-  https://openid.net/specs/openid-4-verifiable-presentations-1_0.html#name-requirements-notation-and-c
- Design Decisions - https://mosip.atlassian.net/wiki/external/ZjcwZDBkODcyYTdiNDcwMjg5MGI0YTg2YmQ4MTI0YWI

## Reference UX: NA  

## Compatibility
- OpenID4VP 1.0  
- direct_post.jwt flow  

## Environment
- Swift  

## Implementation Details
- Replace:
  - HMAC-SHA256 based key derivation  
- Implement:
  - ECDH + Concat KDF  
- Include:
  - `apu` / `apv` binding in encryption context  

## Non-Functional Requirements
- Secure key derivation  
- Compliance with spec  
- Optimized encryption performance
