title: [Swift] VP Response Construction & Parsing with DCQL
content:
Problem description:
## Purpose
Enable the wallet to construct Verifiable Presentation (VP) responses as per spec version (Draft 23 / 1.0) and support parsing and handling of DCQL-based requests.

## Pre-requisites
- VP request validation completed  
- Credential storage available in wallet  
- Support for credential formats (mdoc, SD-JWT, W3C VC)  
- AuthorizationRequest (v1/v2) available  

## Basic Flow
1. Wallet receives validated VP request  
2. Identify spec version (Draft 23 / 1.0)  
3. Parse DCQL query (if present)  
4. Match credentials against query  
5. Construct unsigned VP token  
6. Sign VP token  
7. Send VP response to Verifier  

## Alternate Flows
- Multiple credentials satisfy a single query  
- Same credential satisfies multiple queries  
- No matching credentials → partial/empty response  
- Non-DCQL (scope-based) request handling  

## Scenarios
- DCQL-based VP request  
- Scope-based VP request  
- Multi-credential response generation  
- Multi-format credential handling (mdoc, SD-JWT, VC)  

## Data Fields
- `verifiableCredentials` (Map<String, Map<FormatType, List<Any>>>)  
- `holderId`  
- `signatureSuite`  
- `UnsignedVPTokenV2`  
- `dcql_query`  
- `meta` (mandatory in DCQL)  
- `credential_configuration_id`  

## Business Rules (With Audit)
- DCQL `meta` field is mandatory  
- Arrays in DCQL must be non-empty  
- Wallet MUST log:
  - Credentials selected  
  - Query matching results  
  - VP construction outcome  
- Same credential can satisfy multiple queries  
- Multiple presentations per query are allowed  

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] VP constructed correctly for Draft 23 and 1.0  
- [ ] DCQL parsing and validation works as expected  
- [ ] Supports multiple credentials in response  
- [ ] Format-specific VP construction is correct  
- [ ] Response structure aligns with spec  

## Exceptions
- Invalid DCQL query → reject request  
- Missing mandatory `meta` fields → error  
- No matching credentials → return empty/partial VP  
- Parsing errors → fail VP construction  

## Documentation
- OpenID4VP 1.0 specification  - https://openid.net/specs/openid-4-verifiable-presentations-1_0.html#name-requirements-notation-and-c
- Internal VP construction design  - https://mosip.atlassian.net/wiki/external/ZjcwZDBkODcyYTdiNDcwMjg5MGI0YTg2YmQ4MTI0YWI

## Reference UX: NA  

## Compatibility
- Draft 23  
- OpenID4VP 1.0  

## Environment
- Kotlin  
- Swift  

## Implementation Details
- Method: `constructUnsignedVPTokenV3`  
- Uses stored AuthorizationRequest to determine spec version  
- Construct:
  - Format-specific VP tokens  
  - mdoc session transcript based on version  
- Output:
  - `List<UnsignedVPTokenV2>`  

## Non-Functional Requirements
- Efficient credential matching  
- Scalable handling for multiple queries  
- Maintain format-agnostic design  
- Minimal latency in VP construction

title: [Kotlin] VP Response Construction and sending VP response to verifier+ Parsing with DCQL
content:
Problem description:
## Purpose
Enable the wallet to construct Verifiable Presentation (VP) responses as per spec version (Draft 23 / 1.0) and support parsing and handling of DCQL-based requests.

## Pre-requisites
- VP request validation completed  
- Credential storage available in wallet  
- Support for credential formats (mdoc, SD-JWT, W3C VC)  
- AuthorizationRequest (v1/v2) available  

## Basic Flow
1. Wallet receives validated VP request  
2. Identify spec version (Draft 23 / 1.0)  
3. Parse DCQL query (if present)  
4. Match credentials against query  
5. Construct unsigned VP token  
6. Sign VP token  
7. Send VP response to Verifier  

## Alternate Flows
- Multiple credentials satisfy a single query  
- Same credential satisfies multiple queries  
- No matching credentials → partial/empty response  
- Non-DCQL (scope-based) request handling  

## Scenarios
- DCQL-based VP request  
- Scope-based VP request  
- Multi-credential response generation  
- Multi-format credential handling (mdoc, SD-JWT, VC)  

## Data Fields
- `verifiableCredentials` (Map<String, Map<FormatType, List<Any>>>)  
- `holderId`  
- `signatureSuite`  
- `UnsignedVPTokenV2`  
- `dcql_query`  
- `meta` (mandatory in DCQL)  
- `credential_configuration_id`  

## Business Rules (With Audit)
- DCQL `meta` field is mandatory  
- Arrays in DCQL must be non-empty  
- Wallet MUST log:
  - Credentials selected  
  - Query matching results  
  - VP construction outcome  
- Same credential can satisfy multiple queries  
- Multiple presentations per query are allowed  

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] VP constructed correctly for Draft 23 and 1.0  
- [ ] DCQL parsing and validation works as expected  
- [ ] Supports multiple credentials in response  
- [ ] Format-specific VP construction is correct  
- [ ] Response structure aligns with spec  

## Exceptions
- Invalid DCQL query → reject request  
- Missing mandatory `meta` fields → error  
- No matching credentials → return empty/partial VP  
- Parsing errors → fail VP construction  

## Documentation
- OpenID4VP 1.0 specification  - https://openid.net/specs/openid-4-verifiable-presentations-1_0.html#name-requirements-notation-and-c
- Internal VP construction design  - https://mosip.atlassian.net/wiki/external/ZjcwZDBkODcyYTdiNDcwMjg5MGI0YTg2YmQ4MTI0YWI

## Reference UX: NA  

## Compatibility
- Draft 23  
- OpenID4VP 1.0  

## Environment
- Kotlin  
- Swift  

## Implementation Details
- Method: `constructUnsignedVPTokenV3`  
- Uses stored AuthorizationRequest to determine spec version  
- Construct:
  - Format-specific VP tokens  
  - mdoc session transcript based on version  
- Output:
  - `List<UnsignedVPTokenV2>`  

## Non-Functional Requirements
- Efficient credential matching  
- Scalable handling for multiple queries  
- Maintain format-agnostic design  
- Minimal latency in VP construction

title: [Swift] OpenIDVP 1.0 Changes - Wallet metadata changes and Client ID prefix
content:
Problem description:
## Purpose
Enable wallet to validate VP requests based on spec version (Draft 23 / 1.0) and support updated wallet metadata structures.

## Pre-requisites
- Support for OpenID4VP draft 23
- Existing WalletMetadata implementation
- Authorization request parsing logic

## Basic Flow
1. Wallet receives VP request  
2. Identify spec version:
   - `dcql_query` → 1.0  
   - `vp_formats_supported` → 1.0  
   - Else → Draft 23  
3. Parse verifier metadata  
4. Validate request based on version  
5. Load corresponding WalletMetadata (v1 or v2)  
6. Proceed with validation 

> [!NOTE]
> ### Version Detection and Client Identification Flow

When a VP Request is received, the wallet shall first determine whether the request is received **By Value** or **By Reference** and then identify the OpenID4VP specification version before applying validation rules.

#### By Reference Request Processing

The wallet currently supports the following client identification mechanisms:

- Pre-Registered Client
- DID-based Client Identifier

##### Pre-Registered Client

1. Wallet scans a QR Code or receives a Deep Link containing a Request URI.
2. Wallet fetches the VP Request from the Verifier API.
3. Wallet extracts the `client_id` from the fetched request.
4. Wallet identifies the verifier as a Pre-Registered Client.
5. Wallet determines the OpenID4VP version using verifier metadata/configuration.
6. Wallet applies Draft 23 or OpenID4VP 1.0 validation rules accordingly.

##### DID Client Identifier

1. Wallet scans a QR Code or receives a Deep Link containing a Request URI.
2. Wallet fetches the VP Request from the Verifier API.
3. Wallet extracts the `client_id`.
4. Wallet identifies the verifier using the configured DID Client Identifier Prefix.
5. Current implementation uses `decentralized_identifier` and DID schemes for verifier identification.
6. Wallet determines the OpenID4VP version using verifier metadata/configuration.
7. Wallet applies Draft 23 or OpenID4VP 1.0 validation rules accordingly.

#### By Value Request Processing

1. Wallet receives the complete VP Request directly.
2. Wallet parses the Authorization Request.
3. Wallet identifies the OpenID4VP version based on request content.
4. Wallet applies the corresponding validation rules.

### OpenID4VP Version Detection Logic

The wallet shall determine the specification version using the following rules:

| Condition | Version |
|------------|----------|
| `dcql_query` present in request | OpenID4VP 1.0 |
| `client_id_prefixes_supported` present in metadata | OpenID4VP 1.0 |
| New `vp_formats_supported` structure present | OpenID4VP 1.0 |
| Draft 23 metadata/configuration explicitly present | Draft 23 |
| Draft 23 metadata/configuration not available | OpenID4VP 1.0 |

### Validation Rules

The wallet shall:

- Detect the OpenID4VP version before validation.
- Load the corresponding Wallet Metadata structure.
- Apply version-specific validation rules.
- Maintain backward compatibility with Draft 23 requests.

### QE Test Coverage

#### By Reference Flows

| Scenario | Expected Result |
|-----------|----------------|
| Pre-Registered Client + Draft 23 | Validation succeeds |
| Pre-Registered Client + OpenID4VP 1.0 | Validation succeeds |
| DID Client + Draft 23 | Validation succeeds |
| DID Client + OpenID4VP 1.0 | Validation succeeds |
| Unknown Client Identifier Prefix | Accept/Reject based on configuration |
| Missing Verifier Metadata | Validation error |
| Incorrect Version Metadata | Validation error |

#### By Value Flows

| Scenario | Expected Result |
|-----------|----------------|
| Draft 23 Request | Validation succeeds |
| OpenID4VP 1.0 Request | Validation succeeds |
| Request with `dcql_query` | Identified as OpenID4VP 1.0 |
| Request with `scope` only | Identified as Draft 23 |
| Request containing both `scope` and `dcql_query` | `invalid_request` |

#### Metadata Validation

| Scenario | Expected Result |
|-----------|----------------|
| Draft 23 Metadata Parsing | Success |
| OpenID4VP 1.0 Metadata Parsing | Success |
| `client_id_prefixes_supported` Parsing | Success |
| DID Prefix Validation | Success |
| Pre-Registered Client Validation | Success |

## Alternate Flows
- VP request via reference (QR / deep link)  
- Pre-registered `client_id` → fetch version from trusted list  
- Unknown `client_id` prefix → accept/reject based on config  

## Scenarios
- Draft 23 request validation  
- 1.0 request validation  
- Mixed metadata handling  
- Unknown prefix handling  
- Missing required fields  

## Data Fields
- `client_id`  
- `client_id_prefixes_supported`  
- `vp_formats_supported`  
- `dcql_query`  
- `scope`  
- `typ` (must be `oauth-authz-req+jwt`)  
- `authorizationEncryptionEncValuesSupported`  

## Business Rules (With Audit)
- Wallet MUST detect spec version before validation  
- `typ` must be `oauth-authz-req+jwt`  
- Either `dcql_query` OR `scope` must exist (not both)  
- Wallet MUST log:
  - Request received  
  - Spec version identified  
  - Validation result  
- Wallet MAY accept unknown prefixes as pre-registered  

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Wallet identifies spec version correctly  
- [ ] Supports both Draft 23 & 1.0  
- [ ] Metadata parsing supports new fields  
- [ ] Validation errors thrown as per spec  
- [ ] Backward compatibility maintained  

## Exceptions
- `invalid_request` if:
  - client_id prefix validation fails  
  - both `dcql_query` and `scope` are present  
  - required parameters are missing  

## Documentation
- OpenID4VP 1.0 specification  - https://openid.net/specs/openid-4-verifiable-presentations-1_0.html
- Internal metadata design docs  -https://mosip.atlassian.net/wiki/external/ZjcwZDBkODcyYTdiNDcwMjg5MGI0YTg2YmQ4MTI0YWI

## Reference UX: NA  

## Compatibility
- Draft 23  
- OpenID4VP 1.0  

## Library Support
- Swift library  

## Implementation Details
- Introduce:
  - `WalletMetadataV2`  
  - `AuthorizationRequestV2`  
- Use strategy pattern for validation  
- Constructor overloading to support both metadata versions  

## Non-Functional Requirements
- Backward compatibility  
- Minimal performance overhead for version detection  
- Extensible for future spec updates

title: [C4GT Community]: [Spike] Explore SVG Rendering for SD-JWT VC in Inji Wallet
content:
Problem description:
### Ticket Contents

## Description

As part of enhancing credential display capabilities, we need to explore support for SVG-based rendering of SD-JWT VCs in the wallet. This spike aims to analyze how SVG templates (as per SD-JWT VC spec metadata) can be used to dynamically render credentials in a visually rich and standardized format.

The analysis should refer to the SD-JWT VC specification (Type Metadata section) and evaluate:

- How rendering metadata is provided
- How SVG templates can be interpreted and rendered
- How this can be integrated into existing wallet rendering logic


### Goals

1. Understand how SVG rendering is defined in the SD-JWT VC spec
2. Identify how rendering metadata is structured and consumed
3. Evaluate the feasibility of:
- Parsing SVG templates
- Binding credential data to SVG
4. Identify changes required in:
- Wallet rendering layer
- Credential parsing layer
5. Define an approach for the dynamic rendering of credentials using SVG

### Expected Outcome

1. Clear understanding of:

- SVG rendering support in SD-JWT VC
- Metadata structure for rendering

2. Documented approach for:

- Parsing SVG templates
- Injecting credential data into templates
- Rendering in mobile/web wallet

3. Identified:

- Technical dependencies
- Risks and limitations

4. Proposed step-by-step implementation plan documented

### Acceptance Criteria

1. SD-JWT VC spec (rendering/type metadata) is analyzed and summarized
2. SVG rendering approach is clearly documented
3. Feasibility of SVG rendering in:

- Android (Kotlin)
- iOS (Swift)

4. Data binding strategy between:

- Credential claims
- SVG placeholders is defined

5. Edge cases identified:

- Missing fields
- Invalid SVG
- Unsupported attributes

6. Final output includes:

- Architecture approach
- Implementation steps
- Open questions / risks

### Implementation Details

Spec reference:

- https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-oauth-sd-jwt-vc/
- https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-oauth-sd-jwt-vc-10.html#ExampleTypeMetadata 

### 1. Spec Analysis

### Review
- SD-JWT VC **Type Metadata section**

### Identify
- How rendering templates are provided  
- Expected format of SVG templates  
- Structure of metadata carrying rendering instructions  

### 2. Rendering Approach Evaluation

### Evaluate

- [ ] Static SVG vs Dynamic SVG  
  - Static → predefined templates  
  - Dynamic → data-driven rendering  

- [ ] Inline SVG vs External Template  
  - Inline → embedded within metadata  
  - External → fetched via URL/reference  


### Considerations
- [ ] Placeholder format standardization  
- [ ] Nested claim handling  
- [ ] Fallback values for missing fields  

### 4. Platform Feasibility

### Android
- [ ] Assess SVG rendering support  
- [ ] Identify required libraries  
- [ ] Evaluate performance considerations  

### iOS
- [ ] Evaluate SVG parsing/rendering feasibility  
- [ ] Identify native vs third-party support  

### 5. Integration Points for Kotlin, Swift & Wallet Code

Identify required changes in:

- [ ] Credential Parsing Layer  
  - Extract rendering metadata  
  - Handle SVG templates  

- [ ] Rendering Engine  
  - Bind data to SVG  
  - Render dynamically  

- [ ] UI Components  
  - Display rendered SVG  
  - Handle responsiveness  

### 6. Error Handling Strategy

Define handling for:

- [ ] Invalid SVG → fallback to default rendering  
- [ ] Missing data fields → show placeholder/fallback  
- [ ] Rendering failures → display error state  

## 7. Output Deliverables

### Documentation

title: Support Verifiable Credential Refresh (refreshService) in Inji Wallet (Mobile & Web) - Technical Design Requirment
content:
Problem description:

Propose a technical design for supporting the Verifiable Credential Refresh mechanism as defined in the W3C VC Refresh specification, enabling Inji Wallet (Mobile) and Inji Web Wallet to refresh credentials issued by Inji Certify or other compatible issuers.

Reference specification:
https://w3c-ccg.github.io/vc-refresh/

This feature will enable wallets to refresh expired or soon-to-expire credentials through issuer-provided refresh endpoints defined via the refreshService property.

Problem

Many credentials issued through Inji Certify contain validity periods (validUntil). Once expired:

  • The credential becomes unusable

  • The user must manually re-initiate issuance

  • The wallet does not guide the user to obtain an updated credential

This creates friction for credentials such as:

  • Age verification credentials

  • Student IDs

  • Permits

  • Temporary certificates

  • Membership credentials

The VC Refresh specification introduces a standardized mechanism to refresh credentials through issuer-defined services.

Goal

Enable Inji Wallet (Mobile and Web) to:

  1. Detect refresh instructions inside credentials

  2. Notify users when credentials are expiring

  3. Initiate refresh interactions with issuers

  4. Obtain updated credentials automatically or manually

VC Data Model Support

Wallet must detect the refreshService property inside the credential.

Example:

"refreshService": {
  "type": "VerifiableCredentialInteractionService",
  "serviceEndpoint": "https://issuer.example/interactions/3732?iuv=1",
  "validFrom": "2034-09-01T19:23:24Z"
}

Fields to support:

Field | Description -- | -- type | Refresh service type serviceEndpoint | Endpoint used to initiate refresh interaction validFrom | Earliest time refresh can occur validUntil | Optional latest refresh time

Refresh Interaction Flow

Manual Refresh

User manually refreshes credential.

Flow:

User opens credential
        │
Wallet detects refreshService
        │
User clicks "Refresh Credential"
        │
Wallet sends request to issuer
        ▼
GET serviceEndpoint

Issuer returns exchange workflow.

Wallet performs interaction.

Automatic Refresh

Wallet may refresh credentials automatically when:

credential nearing expiry
AND refreshService available
AND holder consent provided

This can run:

  • On wallet startup

  • Background refresh check

  • Notification trigger

Refresh Interaction Protocol

The refresh service should follow VC API Lifecycle interactions.

Flow:

  1. Wallet calls refresh endpoint

  2. Issuer returns exchange URL

  3. Wallet initiates interaction

  4. Issuer may request presentation

  5. Issuer issues refreshed credential

Presentation During Refresh

Issuer may request existing credential.

Example request:

QueryByExample
UniversityDegreeCredential

Wallet must:

  • Identify matching credential

  • Generate verifiable presentation

  • Submit to issuer

This is similar to Presentation During Issuance (PDI).

Wallet Behaviour After Refresh

Options:

Replace credential

Recommended.

Old credential replaced
New validity period applied

Version history

Alternative:

Old credential archived
New credential stored
[Refresh Credential]

Notifications

Wallet may notify:

Your credential will expire soon.
Tap to refresh.

Changes Required

Inji Mobile Wallet

Required updates:

  • Credential parsing

  • Expiration monitoring

  • Refresh interaction flow

  • UI refresh option

  • Notification system integration

Inji Web Wallet

Required updates:

  • Credential metadata parsing

  • Refresh UI action

  • Refresh interaction execution

  • Credential replacement

Inji Certify (Issuer)

Issuer must support:

  • refreshService in issued credentials

  • refresh interaction endpoint

  • VC API lifecycle interaction

  • issuance of refreshed credential

Security Considerations

Wallet must ensure:

  • Refresh endpoint belongs to issuer

  • Holder authentication before refresh

  • Presentation requests validated

  • Prevent refresh endpoint misuse

Privacy Considerations

Important considerations:

  • Refresh should require holder consent

  • Issuer should not bypass wallet

  • Wallet must mediate refresh process

Deliverables

Engineering design covering:

  • Wallet refresh architecture

  • Mobile implementation plan

  • Web wallet implementation plan

  • Issuer integration model

  • API interaction details

  • UI updates

  • Security controls

Acceptance Criteria

  • Wallet detects refreshService property

  • Wallet displays refresh option

  • Wallet initiates refresh interaction

  • Wallet supports presentation-based refresh

  • Wallet stores refreshed credential successfully

  • Feature works in both Inji Mobile Wallet and Inji Web Wallet

References

VC Refresh Specification
https://w3c-ccg.github.io/vc-refresh/

Verifiable Credentials Data Model
https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/

VC API Lifecycle Management
https://w3c-ccg.github.io/vcalm/

title: Support `credential_configuration_id` parameter in Credential Request for scope-based authorization flow
content:
Problem description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

The current implementation does not support Authorization Servers that utilize the scope-based credential request flow without returning `credential_identifiers` in the Token Response. According to the [OpenID for Verifiable Credential Issuance (OID4VCI) specification](https://openid.net/specs/openid-4-verifiable-credential-issuance-1_0.html), Section 3.3.4, Authorization Servers are permitted two implementation approaches when processing scope-based authorization requests:

1. Include `credential_identifiers` parameter in the Token Response
2. Omit `credential_identifiers` parameter, requiring the Wallet to utilize `credential_configuration_id` in subsequent Credential Requests

The absence of support for the second approach prevents interoperability with specification-compliant Authorization Servers that implement this methodology, thereby limiting the wallet's compatibility with a significant subset of conformant credential issuers.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Implementation of support for the `credential_configuration_id` parameter in Credential Requests when the Authorization Server's Token Response does not include `credential_identifiers`.

**Proposed Implementation:**

The wallet should implement the following behavior:

1. **Authorization Request Phase** - Transmit scope parameter identifying requested credentials:
```http
GET /authorize?
  scope=UniversityDegree EmployeeID&
  response_type=code&
  client_id=inji-wallet&
  redirect_uri=https://wallet.example.com/callback
```

2. **Token Response Handling** - Process responses lacking `credential_identifiers`:
```json
{
  "access_token": "eyJhbGc...",
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "expires_in": 86400
}
```

3. **Credential Request Construction** - Utilize `credential_configuration_id` parameter:
```json
{
  "credential_configuration_id": "UniversityDegree",
  "proof": {
    "proof_type": "jwt",
    "jwt": "eyJraWQ..."
  }
}
```

**Technical Requirements:**
- Persistence of `scope` values from the initial Authorization Request
- Mapping of scope values to corresponding `credential_configuration_id` values as defined in Credential Issuer metadata
- Conditional logic to detect absence of `credential_identifiers` in Token Response
- Construction of Credential Requests using `credential_configuration_id` when applicable
- Successful credential retrieval from the Credential Endpoint using this approach

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Discussion and resolution:
[swatigoel]: Thanks @shashimalcse for raising this issue. We acknowledge that this is a valid requirement and plan to address it.
However, it has not been prioritised so far, as our interoperability testing with multiple issuer systems indicates that using scopes has been sufficient.
If you could share a concrete use case or any limitations you are experiencing with scopes, it would help us better assess the need and prioritise this accordingly.

title: Presentation During Issuance
content:
Problem description:
When issuing credentials to a user, authentication or authorization is often required. The most common factor used is an OTP. However, using OTPs means the user must recall their identifier each time they access their credential. To simplify this, the specification allows submitting an existing credential to authorize the user for credential issuance — a process known as Presentation during Issuance. In essence, it means presenting one credential to obtain another.

Example use cases:

To issue a Student ID Credential, the user presents an Enrollment Credential issued by the educational institution.
To issue a Health Insurance Credential, the user presents an Identity Credential issued by a government authority.
This document focuses on the tech design to support presentations during the issuance process, particularly in scenarios where the issuer requires a presentation to be made before issuing a credential.

Basic Flow

The OVP request received is no different from current OVP request structure followed in Wallet. [Draft 23 OpenID4VP specification using DIF presentation exchange](https://openid.net/specs/openid-4-verifiable-presentations-1_0-ID3.html#name-dif-presentation-exchange-2).
The VP response created is also similar to the current VP response structure followed in Wallet. [Draft 23 VP response (Presentation Exchange)](https://openid.net/specs/openid-4-verifiable-presentations-1_0-ID3.html#name-examples-presentation-excha).
Wallet supports for openid4vp_presentation interaction type only. Other interaction types like redirect_to_web will be supported in the future.
Future scope
redirect_to_web interaction type support during issuance.
Pre-requisites
The Issuer supporting the Interactive Authorization Request Endpoint as per the specification.
Overall Flow diagram
Actors involved
User: The individual requesting the credential.
Wallet - Inji Wallet: The digital wallet application used by the user to manage credentials.
Issuer - Inji Certify (OAuth AS + VCI): The entity responsible for issuing the credential, which also acts as an OAuth Authorization Server and Verifiable Credential Issuer.
Sequence of interactions between entities

Sequence of interactions between entities via inji-* Libraries
Actors involved
User: The individual requesting the credential.
Wallet - Inji Wallet: The digital wallet application used by the user to manage credentials.
Issuer - Inji Certify (OAuth AS + VCI): The entity responsible for issuing the credential, which also acts as an OAuth Authorization Server and Verifiable Credential Issuer.
Inji VCI Client Library: The library used by the wallet to handle OpenID for VC issuance. (Download of credential into Wallet)
Inji OpenID4VP Library: The library used by the wallet to handle OpenID for Verifiable Presentations. (Wallet presenting of the credential to a Verifier)

Notes
In Step 0, why is it interactionCallbacks rather than just presentationRequestCallback?
Because in the future, there can be other interaction types (eg - redirect_to_web or any custom interaction) supported during issuance as well. Hence, to keep it extensible, we have designed it this way.
In Step 4, why is ovp request validation or any other processing propogated to Wallet rather than being handled in inji-openid4vp library?
Because the Wallet is responsible for user interactions, including displaying requests and obtaining user consent. Hence, the Wallet needs to validate the request and process it accordingly.
This also allows the Wallet to have control over how it wants to handle the presentation request and which library to use for VP response creation.
In step 5, why is authenticateVerifier called with urlEncodedAuthorizationRequest = null and authorizationRequest = ovpRequest?
Because in this flow, the openid4vp request is received by value (as JSON and not as a URL). Hence, we pass it as authorizationRequest.
In step 6, why is there a special validation for response_mode?
Because in this flow, the response_mode can be iar-post or iar-post.jwt, which are specific to interactive authorization requests.
Hence, we need to skip the response_uri check for these modes as ovp_request may not contain response_uri in such cases and response is sent to the interaction endpoint of the issuer.
In step 11, why is method constructVPResponse used rather than sendAuthorizationResponseToVerifier?
Because in this flow, the VP response needs to be sent to the Issuer (/iar) which is known to vci client library.
The method sendAuthorizationResponseToVerifier is designed to send the VP response directly to the verifier endpoint, which is not applicable in this case.
check below point for more clarity on why vci-client needs only the OVP response.
In Step 13, why is vci client library responsible for sharing VP response to issuer rather than inji-openid4vp library?
Because the vci client library is responsible for handling the overall issuance flow, including interactions with the issuer.
The inji-openid4vp library is focused on handling OpenID for Verifiable Presentations, including creating VP responses, but not managing the entire issuance process.
Also, There is a mandation to add authSession to the request which is more specific to issuance flow and not related to openid4vp.
The VP response submission body of OVP flow - {vp_token:..., presentation_submission:...} is wrapped inside but in PDI flow {auth_session:..., openid4vp_presentation:{vp_token:..., presentation_submission:...}} it differs. To handle this wrapping and addition of auth_session, it is better to keep this logic in vci client library to have more control.
Changes summary
Inji VCI Client Library
Add support for client metadata to accept supported interaction types of Wallet. (interactionTypesSupported field)
Update requestCredentialFromTrustedIssuer and requestCredentialFromOffer methods to accept interactionCallbacks map to handle different interaction types during issuance.
Implement logic to handle openid4vp_presentation interaction type, including invoking the appropriate callback in the Wallet.
Add logic to share VP response to Issuer's /iar endpoint after receiving it from Wallet.
Inji OpenID4VP Library
Add support to validate openid4vp request with response_mode as iar-post or iar-post.jwt by skipping response_uri check.
Add support to create VP response for openid4vp request with response_mode as iar-post or iar-post.jwt.
Add method constructVPResponse to create VP response and return it as Map<String, Any> to Wallet.
Inji Wallet
Implement the openid4vp interaction callback to handle the presentation request, display it to the user, and obtain user consent.
Use inji-openid4vp library to process the openid4vp request and create the VP response.
Handle error scenarios and propagate errors to the user appropriately.
Integrate with the updated inji-vci-client library to support the new interaction flow during credential issuance.
References
[OpenID for Verifiable Credentials Issuance 1.1 - Interactive Authorization Request Endpoint](https://openid.github.io/OpenID4VCI/openid-4-verifiable-credential-issuance-1_1-wg-draft.html#name-interactive-authorization-e)
[OpenID for Verifiable Presentations - Draft 23](https://openid.github.io/openid4vp/draft-23.html)
[RFC 9126 - Pushed Authorization Requests (PAR)](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9126)
[Spike card](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/INJIMOB-3601)

[fredguth]: Please let me ask you some questions:
1) This method allows receiving a VC given a VC. Right?
2) the inji-certify that creates a VC given a VC is in the wallet's provider backend, right? So the verifier must trust the wallet provider, right?  the wallet provider plays a role of issuer here or are you suggesting it is accessing the issuer that created the first VC?

title: Integrate OpenID4VP Library and Expand Sample Wallet Capabilities
content:
Problem description:
**Note: Requirement gathering in progress**

Enhance the Sample Credentials Wallet (Android Kotlin app) to integrate OpenID4VP functionality and extend its existing support for issuance, verification, and presentation of Verifiable Credentials using the Inji library ecosystem.

This enhancement aims to make the sample app a full demonstration wallet capable of both credential issuance (VCI) and presentation (OpenID4VP) flows — aligned with the latest verifiable credential interoperability standards.

References:

Sample Wallet Source: [Inji Sample Wallet Repository](https://github.com/mosip/inji-wallet/tree/sample-android-wallet/SampleAppVCIclient/SampleAppVCIClient)

OpenID4VP Library: [Inji OpenID4VP v0.5.0](https://github.com/mosip/inji-openid4vp/tree/v0.5.0)

Objectives:

Integrate OpenID4VP Kotlin library into the Sample Wallet.

Implement Verifiable Presentation (VP) generation and submission flow.

Maintain existing VCI issuance and VC verification features.

Demonstrate an end-to-end user flow:

Download VC from issuer → Store → Verify → Present via OpenID4VP.

Add basic UI to showcase the flow and display success/failure messages.

Key Tasks:
Integration

Add OpenID4VP dependency to build.gradle.

title: Login Feature - Inji Mobile Wallet
content:
Problem description:
**Note** : Requirement gathering in progress, soon it will be available for development to start.

# Unified Login and Credential Sync for Inji Mobile Wallet

## 1. Objective

The objective of this feature is to introduce a **secure, unified login mechanism** for the **Inji Mobile Wallet**, ensuring that users can access their wallet using the same credentials and identity as used in **Inji Web Wallet**.

This enhancement also introduces **bidirectional credential synchronization** between the web and mobile wallets upon user login — ensuring that any credential downloaded or deleted on one device is reflected on the other.

### 🎯 Key Goals
- Enable consistent authentication for both web and mobile clients  
- Maintain synchronized wallet access across devices (**bidirectional sync**)  
- Leverage **OIDC-compliant login** via trusted IDPs (eSignet, Google, Keycloak)  
- Ensure **secure key management** and per-wallet session handling  
- Maintain **user privacy** through strong encryption and token management  

## 2. Scope

| In Scope | Out of Scope |
|-----------|---------------|
| Login feature for Inji Mobile Wallet using **OIDC Authorization Code Flow with PKCE** | Integration with non-OIDC IDPs |
| Shared authentication and user mapping between Web and Mobile | Common centralized session management across devices |
| **Bidirectional credential sync** on login (web ↔ mobile) | Non-login-based wallet access |
| Per-wallet session management (**single active session per user**) | Any backend unrelated to authentication (e.g., VC verification APIs) |
| Key management via **Mimoto API-based key generation** | — |

## 3. Assumptions

- Both **Inji Web** and **Inji Mobile Wallets** are registered **OIDC clients** with the same IDP  
- **Mimoto** supports secure token exchange, key generation, and credential sync APIs  
- Credential syncing occurs **only during user login** (not continuous background sync)  
- Each wallet maintains its own session — logging in from a new device **logs out the previous one**  
- Credential data is **encrypted locally**; server (**Mimoto**) stores only **encrypted metadata** for syncing  
- Internet connectivity is required for login and sync; **offline mode** supports local access only  

## 4. Basic Flows

### 4.1 Login Flow — Mobile Wallet (Authorization Code + PKCE)

1. User selects **“Login with eSignet / Google.”**  
2. App initiates **OIDC authorization request** with PKCE challenge.  
3. IDP authenticates user and redirects via deep link:  com.mosip.inji:/callback
4. App exchanges **authorization code** with Auth Backend for tokens.  
5. **Mimoto** validates tokens and issues wallet session.  
6. During login, **sync API** triggers credential sync from Mimoto.  
7. User sees updated wallet contents post-login.  


### 4.2 Credential Sync Flow (Bidirectional)

**Trigger:** User login (manual or auto-login)

**Flow Steps:**
1. Wallet calls: POST /api/credentials/sync
2. **Mimoto** compares encrypted credential metadata for that user.  
3. Differences are reconciled:
- Newly downloaded VCs on one device → synced to the other  
- Deleted VCs on one → removed from the other  
4. Both wallets now reflect consistent credential lists.  


### 4.3 Key Management Flow

- Keys are generated on Web (**Mimoto**) via a secure API — similar to the Brazil implementation  
- **Mimoto acts as Key Manager**, creating key pairs and storing only metadata  
- **Mobile Wallet** owns a fragment of the key; private key remains device-bound  
- **Shamir Secret Sharing** (future scope) to be explored internally for distributed key management  


### 4.4 Session Management Flow (Per-Wallet)

- Each wallet maintains a **distinct session**  
- Logging in from another device prompts:  
> “You are already logged in on another device. Please log out before continuing.”  
- Previous session must end before new login succeeds  
- Prevents conflicting credential actions (like deletion) and ensures clean sync post-login  


## Summary

This feature ensures that Inji Wallet users have a **unified login experience** across web and mobile, while maintaining **data security**, **session integrity**, and **synchronized access** to their digital credentials — setting the foundation for a seamless, interoperable, and secure ecosystem.

title: [Spec Impl] Add checksum to all writes
content:
Problem description:
## Background
Every write from/to Wallet has a possibility to have corruption. Hence all writes should include a checksum at the last.

## What to do
1. Modify all the structures chunk write, transfer report request, transfer summary report to include checksum at the end.
2. Finalise on the CRC to be used. The suggestion is to use CRC16-CCITT-True which is used in Bluetooth 5.3
3. Update Transfer report structure to match with the specification. Also investigate if the mentioned structure is okay for a success and failure case. Since it will have CRC, on a success case, it will still have CRC value to differentiate between a success report Vs a spurious empty characteristic read.

## References for finalising the CRC
[https://reveng.sourceforge.io/crc-catalogue/16.htm](https://www.google.com/url?q=https://reveng.sourceforge.io/crc-catalogue/16.htm&sa=D&source=docs&ust=1674716915666010&usg=AOvVaw3WdhsT1NFOnGfSyMRlTPxL)

The spec says 

The session MUST be terminated if at least one of the following conditions occur: 

* After a time-out of no activity occurs. 
* If the Wallet does not want to receive any further requests.

Termination is as per the default BLE write. 

In case of a termination, the Wallet and Verifier MUST perform at least the following actions: 

* Destruction of session keys and related ephemeral key material 
* Closure of the communication channel used for data retrieval

Problem description:
## Background
The QR code structure used in INJI is a JSON with two fields. one of the field "cid" is holding dummy value and another field "pk" holds the hex encoded advertisement payload of verifier.
{"cid":"ilB8l","pk":"4f56504d4f5349505f2f9377eb06"}

## What should be done
We will implement the format of QR code data mentioned in specification. We need to put 32bytes of pubkey in QR code data to be compatible with IOS as well. Do not use JSON as we need the QR code data to be used or enabling deeplinks.
```
OPENID4VP://connect?name=STADIONENTRANCE&key=8520f0098930a754748b7ddcb43ef75a0dbf3a0d26381af4eba4a98eaa9b4e6a&nonce=6e91ab1b48396d3e 
```

- nonce to be used in QR code is yet to be decided as we don't have the concept of nonce being shared from Verifier side today

title: [Spec Impl] Change the format of response size value written to RESPONSE_SIZE char
content:
Problem description:
## Problem
At the moment, the value written to REPSONSE_SIZE char is byte representation of the total byte count ASCII value. 

E.g: 
If the response size is 139234 bytes. The value written to RESPONSE_SIZE char will be `31 33 39 32 33 34`

It should be changed to a proper big-endian(network byte order) representation like `10 00011111 11100010`. We can finalise on the max number of bytes we can use for this. If we choose the value as 3 bytes, we can represent maximum response size value of 2^24 = 16777216 bytes ~ 16MB in 3bytes.

title: UI/UX Revocation Feature enhancements
content:
Problem description:
“Last Checked” means the last time the wallet attempted to check status — not whether it succeeded.
It should always update when the user manually refreshes or when an auto-refresh occurs.
This provides the user a clear signal:
“The wallet last tried to verify your credential’s status at [timestamp].”
 Rationale for always updating timestamp
User Transparency: It helps users know when the last verification attempt happened, even if the backend or network failed.
Debugging clarity: Easier to differentiate between network or verification failures and old cached data.
Consistency: Keeps the “Last Checked” label meaningful in all states — success, revoked, expired, or failed.
Important: Distinguish in UI
To avoid confusion, ensure UI clearly separates:
Status: Revoked / Valid / Unknown
Last Checked: <timestamp>
If the last check failed (due to connectivity or backend issue), you can optionally show:
“Last checked at [time] — status could not be verified.”

Step 4: Authenticate Using eSignet KBI – Perform eSignet KBI authentication for security.

title: UI/UX: Create Profile - Profiling with Single VC
content:
Problem description:
Description

Create a complete UI flow diagram for the Inji Mobile Wallet Profile feature inside the Inji Mobile Wallet application. The flow should represent the user journey from login to verified profile creation and credential storage.
Flow Overview
The user must first authenticate using Gmail, which creates a wallet account space. After login, the user proceeds to create their profile by uploading a foundational ID or functional ID containing a face photo. The profile is initially marked as Non-Verified.
To upgrade the profile to Verified, the user must perform live face capture, which is matched with the photo present on the uploaded credential. Once the match is successful, the profile status becomes Verified, allowing the user to download and store multiple Verifiable Credentials (VCs) in the wallet.
The wallet must also support PIN setup and passcode entry for future logins.
Reference Prototype: [Design Inji Wallet Profile UI](https://www.figma.com/make/evEAcdGzW03Dr2gm1VQyou/Design-Inji-Wallet-Profile-UI?p=f&t=nENiPky5Nksdypd4-0)
 
User can now:
Download credentials from issuers
Store credentials
View credentials
Share credentials for verification
Examples:
National ID
Driver’s License
Insurance
Tax Number
Degree Certificate
Farmer ID
Purpose:
Unlock wallet
Protect credentials
Steps:
Enter PIN
Confirm PIN
Returning User Login
Flow:
Login with Gmail
Wallet detected
Prompt for Passcode / PIN
Screen:
“Enter PIN to unlock your wallet”
After successful PIN entry:
User lands on:
Wallet Home
Edge Cases
Include branches for:
Face match failure
Credential missing photo
Credential verification failure
User cancels face verification
PIN forgotten
Diagram Requirements
User actions
System actions
Decision points
Screen transitions
Verification states
Use clear states:
New User
Wallet Created
Non-Verified Profile
Verified Profile
Credential Wallet
Final Flow Structure
The UI flow should visually represent:
Login → Wallet Creation → Profile Setup → Upload Credential → Non-Verified Profile → Face Capture → Face Match → Verified Profile → Wallet Credential Storage
With security flow:
Login → Enter PIN → Wallet Access

title: Inji Web UI: Addition of Spanish and Sinhala Language Support
content:
Problem description:
## User Story

**As a** user of the Inji Wallet (Web), **I want** the option to use the interface in **Spanish** and **Sinhala**, **so that** I can navigate and use the application in my preferred language, improving usability and accessibility for Spanish-speaking and Sinhala-speaking users.

## Acceptance Criteria

### 1. Language Selection
- Users should be able to switch between available languages, including all existing supported languages, **Spanish**, and **Sinhala**, through the language selection option.
- The selected language should persist across sessions based on the existing localization behavior.

### 2. Full Interface Translation
- Ensure all UI components, including buttons, labels, dialogs, error messages, validation messages, tooltips, notifications, and prompts, are accurately translated into **Spanish** and **Sinhala**.
- **Spanish (Spain)** should be used from **Google Translator** as the initial translation source.
- Maintain consistency and accuracy of translations across all features, screens, and user workflows.

### 3. Resource Bundles
- Implement separate localization resource bundles for **Spanish** and **Sinhala**.
- Follow the existing internationalization (i18n) structure to enable easy maintenance and future language additions.
- Ensure all newly introduced strings are externalized into the localization resources.

### 4. Validation and Testing
- Conduct thorough testing to verify:
  - All UI text is translated correctly.
  - No layout issues, truncation, or overflow occur across supported screen sizes.
  - Language switching works seamlessly throughout the application.
  - The translated content preserves the intended meaning and functionality.

### 5. Fallback Behavior
- If a translation is unavailable for any key in Spanish or Sinhala, the application should gracefully fall back to the English translation.

## Technical Notes

- Utilize the existing localization/internationalization (i18n) framework used by Inji Web Wallet.
- Add localization resource files for:
  - `es` (Spanish)
  - `si` (Sinhala)
- Ensure all existing and newly introduced UI strings are sourced from localization resources.
- Follow the existing language loading and fallback mechanism.
- Validate translations across all supported browsers.


## Definition of Done

- [ ] Spanish (`es`) language support added.
- [ ] Sinhala (`si`) language support added.
- [ ] Language selector updated.
- [ ] All UI strings externalized and translated.
- [ ] English fallback verified.
- [ ] Cross-browser testing completed.
- [ ] No UI layout or localization regressions observed.
- [ ] QA sign-off completed.

title: Story: UI/UX Revamp of Inji Web Wallet (Landing Page → Login Flow)
content:
Problem description:
This story covers the UI/UX revamp of the existing Inji Web Wallet experience from the Landing Page until the user reaches the Login page. The objective is to align the web wallet with the latest design system while keeping existing functional behavior unchanged wherever possible.

The implementation primarily focuses on UI restructuring, navigation improvements, onboarding experience, language selection updates, and introducing a few new informational screens.

Since this work modifies existing screens, a detailed impact analysis of the current implementation is required before development.

- Figma Prototype - https://www.figma.com/proto/FDsPKPWcNRjzsKeZzT9Gzc/Inji-Web-Wallet?page-id=2864%3A3355&node-id=4077-4795&viewport=-13%2C1548%2C0.15&t=m2ZF74fMHcC7TwiU-1&scaling=min-zoom&content-scaling=fixed&starting-point-node-id=4061%3A428

- Figma Design - https://www.figma.com/design/FDsPKPWcNRjzsKeZzT9Gzc/Inji-Web-Wallet?node-id=3985-5080&t=ehNcIoX6T4UoetQJ-0


# Objective

Implement the latest approved Figma designs for the Inji Web Wallet onboarding flow while:

- Preserving existing business logic wherever applicable.
- Introducing new UI elements and navigation.
- Supporting additional languages.
- Adding new informational components.
- Ensuring existing authentication flow continues to work as before.


# Scope

The scope includes:

- Landing Page
- Tour Guide (Landing Page only)
- Language Selection
- Login Page
- Sign Up flow (UI only if impacted)
- Password Setup screens
- No Cards state
- Home Page restructuring
- Issuer List Page
- Sidebar Navigation
- Profile Dropdown
- About Platform Information
- Browser Back Navigation behavior validation

# Functional Requirements

# 1. Landing Page Redesign

## Existing

Current landing page contains:

- Hero section
- Login CTA
- Language selector
- Introduction content

## New

Implement the redesigned landing page as per Figma.

### Acceptance Criteria

- Landing page should match latest design.
- Responsive layout should remain supported.
- Existing login entry point should remain unchanged.
- Existing routing should remain unchanged.

# 2. Landing Page Tour Guide

The redesigned landing page introduces an updated guided walkthrough.

## Requirements

- Tour guide should only appear on the Landing Page.
- Tour should follow the new design.
- Tour completion state should persist as currently implemented.
- Existing logic for showing/hiding tour should be reused wherever possible.

### Out of Scope

Tour guides for Login Page and authenticated screens. These will be covered under a separate story.

# 3. Language Selection Popup Redesign

The language selection popup has been redesigned.

## UI Changes

- Updated layout
- Updated visual hierarchy
- Improved selection experience

## Functional Changes

Two additional languages are introduced.

These languages are currently **not supported** by Inji Web.

Implementation must include:

- Display in language popup.
- Functional language switching.
- Translation loading.
- Locale persistence.
- Application-wide localization.

### Acceptance Criteria

- Newly added languages are selectable.
- Selected language persists across sessions.
- Entire application reflects selected language.
- Existing supported languages continue to function.

# 4. Login Flow UI Refresh

The Login page receives visual updates only.

## Functional Behaviour

No authentication logic changes.

Existing:

- Login
- Password validation
- Session creation
- Error handling

should continue functioning without modification unless required due to UI restructuring.


# 5. No Cards Screen (First-Time User Experience)

Introduce a dedicated "No Cards" screen.

This screen is shown when:

- User has successfully logged in.
- Wallet contains zero credentials.

Previously users landed directly on the existing Home page.

Now they should see the dedicated empty state.

### Screen should include

- Empty wallet illustration
- Informational message
- CTA to browse issuers
- Any actions defined in Figma

### Acceptance Criteria

- Only shown when wallet has no credentials.
- Once credentials are available, user should never see this state unless all credentials are removed.


# 6. Home Page Restructure

The current landing/dashboard after login has been redesigned.

## Previous

Dashboard mixed:

- Wallet cards
- Issuer list
- Other information

## New

Home page now becomes primarily the user's wallet.

### Home page should contain

- User credential cards
- Card management
- Relevant wallet actions

Issuer listing is removed from this page.


# 7. Dedicated Issuer List Page

Issuer discovery has been moved into a separate page.

## Requirements

Create dedicated navigation and page for:

- Available issuers
- Issuer listing
- Existing issuer functionality

### Functional Behaviour

Existing issuer APIs should continue working.

Only navigation and presentation changes.


# 8. Sidebar Navigation Updates

Sidebar has been redesigned.

New navigation includes:

- Home
- Issuers
- FAQ
- Other items defined in Figma

### Functional Changes

FAQ has now moved into the left sidebar.

Previously accessible elsewhere.

### Acceptance Criteria

Navigation should correctly route between:

- Home
- Issuers
- FAQ
- Other pages

# 9. Profile Dropdown

Profile interaction has been simplified.

Selecting profile avatar opens dropdown containing:

- Profile
- Logout

### Functional Behaviour

Profile screen remains unchanged unless specified.

Logout behaviour remains unchanged.


# 10. About Platform Information

Introduce a new information icon.

Selecting the icon displays static platform information.

### Content

Static content only.

No backend integration required unless future enhancements demand dynamic content.

Possible information:

- Platform version
- About Inji
- Static description
- Other content from design


# 11. Browser Back Navigation Behaviour

This story does **not** introduce any behavioural change.

Current functionality must remain intact.

### Existing Behaviour

When user presses browser Back:

- Navigation should continue moving through browser history.
- User should not immediately receive Exit Wallet popup.

The Exit Wallet confirmation should appear **only after the user reaches the original application entry point**, exactly as current implementation behaves.

This requirement is included for regression validation only.

No functional modification is expected.

# Functional Scenarios

## Scenario 1

New user opens wallet.

Landing Page displayed.

↓

Language selection available.

↓

Tour Guide available.

↓

User logs in.

↓

No Cards screen displayed.

↓

User navigates to Issuers.

↓

Imports first credential.

↓

Home page now displays wallet cards.


## Scenario 2

Existing user.

↓

Landing Page.

↓

Login.

↓

Cards already exist.

↓

Navigate directly to Home page.

↓

Cards displayed.


## Scenario 3

User changes language.

↓

Entire application updates.

↓

Preference persists after refresh.


## Scenario 4

User opens FAQ.

↓

FAQ page opens from sidebar.


## Scenario 5

User opens Profile dropdown.

↓

Profile

↓

Logout


## Scenario 6

User repeatedly presses browser Back.

↓

Application navigates through history.

↓

Exit confirmation appears only when original application state is reached.

# Technical Analysis Required

Since this story modifies existing code rather than introducing entirely new functionality, a complete impact assessment is required.

## 1. Routing Analysis

Review:

- Landing routes
- Login routes
- Home routing
- Issuer routing
- FAQ routing
- Sidebar navigation
- Browser history handling

## 2. Existing Component Reuse

Identify reusable components for:

- Cards
- Sidebar
- Login
- Header
- Footer
- Language popup
- Tour guide

Minimize duplicate implementation.

## 3. Localization Analysis

Review:

- Current localization framework
- Translation file structure
- Locale persistence
- RTL/LTR implications
- Newly added languages

Determine if backend/config changes are required.

## 4. Home Page Refactoring

Assess impact of moving:

Issuer listing

from

Home Page

to

Dedicated Issuer Page.

Review:

- API calls
- State management
- Navigation
- Loading logic

## 5. No Cards State

Determine whether existing wallet APIs already expose:

- Empty wallet state

or

whether frontend logic alone can determine it.

## 6. Issuer Page

Review whether:

Current issuer APIs

can directly support the new page

without backend modifications.

## 7. Sidebar Refactoring

Review:

- Existing navigation implementation
- Routing guards
- Active menu highlighting
- Responsive behaviour


## 8. About Platform

Determine:

- Static frontend implementation only

OR

- Future backend-configurable implementation

## 9. Browser History

Regression testing required for:

- Browser Back
- Refresh
- Session restore
- Deep links

Ensure no behavioural regressions.

## 10. Authentication Flow Validation

Validate existing:

- Login
- Session
- Logout
- Token persistence
- Password setup

remain unaffected.

# Backend Impact Assessment

Potential areas requiring verification:

| Feature | Backend Change Expected |
|----------|-------------------------|
| Landing redesign | No |
| Login redesign | No |
| Tour Guide | No |
| Sidebar | No |
| Home restructuring | Likely No |
| Issuer page | Verify routing only |
| About Platform | No (Static) |
| FAQ relocation | No |
| No Cards screen | Verify wallet API response |
| Additional languages | Possibly configuration/translation assets |
| Browser back behaviour | No |


# Regression Areas

The following existing functionality must be regression tested:

- Login
- Sign Up
- Password setup
- Password reset
- Session persistence
- Logout
- Browser refresh
- Browser Back
- Language switching
- Tour completion
- Responsive layouts
- Existing wallet cards
- Issuer listing
- FAQ access
- Empty wallet state
- Profile access


# Out of Scope

- Login Page Tour Guide (Separate Story)
- Authentication logic changes
- Wallet business logic changes
- Credential management changes
- Issuer backend enhancements
- Exit wallet flow modifications
- Profile feature enhancements

title: # Web Wallet UI Story: DCQL-Based VP Request Credential Selection
content:
Problem description:
## Summary

Implement the Requested Cards UI in Inji Wallet for Verifiable Presentation (VP) requests containing DCQL. The wallet must render credential set queries, support credential selection, apply pre-selection logic, allow user review and re-selection, and enable sharing only when all required credential set queries are satisfied.

## Scope

- Applicable only for VP requests containing DCQL.
- Covers Requested Cards page rendering, credential selection, pre-selection, review/re-selection, share button enablement, and defined edge cases.

**Figma File** - https://www.figma.com/design/FDsPKPWcNRjzsKeZzT9Gzc/Inji-Web-Wallet?node-id=3930-749&p=f&t=ArQYPUlCmDZW09AU-0

## Notes

### 1. Credential Set Query Rendering

A VP request can contain multiple credential set queries.

#### UI Behavior

- Each credential set query shall be displayed as either:
  - Mandatory Cards Section (when `required = true`)
  - Optional Cards Section (when `required = false`)

### 2. Option Rendering

Each credential set query can contain multiple options.

#### UI Behavior

- Each option shall be displayed with:
  - Radio button selection control
  - OR separator between options
- Exactly one option must be selected to satisfy the credential set query.


### 3. Credential Query Rendering

Each option can contain one or more credential queries.

#### UI Behavior

##### Single Credential Query

When an option contains only one credential query:

- Display a section showing all credentials matching that credential query.

##### Multiple Credential Queries

When an option contains multiple credential queries:

- Display a "Multiple Cards" section.
- Show badge:
  - `ALL Required`
- All credential queries within the option must be satisfied for the option to be satisfied.


### 4. Matching Credentials Rendering

Each credential query can match multiple credentials.

#### UI Behavior

- Display all matching credentials.
- Selection control shall be:
  - Radio button when multiple credential sharing is not allowed.
  - Checkbox when multiple credential sharing is allowed.


## Feature Logic

### 1. Pre-select Cards

To provide a seamless experience, the wallet shall pre-select the minimum credentials required to satisfy the VP request.

#### Pre-selection Criteria

##### Mandatory Cards Section

Only required credential set queries shall participate in pre-selection.

For each mandatory section:

- The first option shall be pre-selected.

If the selected option contains:

##### Single Credential Query

- If only one credential matches:
  - That credential shall be pre-selected.

- If multiple credentials match:
  - The first matching credential shall be pre-selected.

##### Multiple Credential Queries

The option shall be selected in a way that satisfies the option.

Examples:

- If option contains:
  - `govt-id`
  - `pan`

And matches are:

  - Govt ID
  - PAN Card

Then:

  - Govt ID shall be selected
  - PAN Card shall be selected

If option contains:

  - `govt-id`
  - `pan`

And matches are:

  - Govt ID / Passport
  - PAN Card

Then:

  - Govt ID shall be selected
  - PAN Card shall be selected

> Note: Examples are for illustration purposes only.

##### Optional Cards Section

- No credentials shall be pre-selected.

##### Edge Case

- Same credential matching multiple credential queries overrides pre-selection where applicable.

### 2. Review and Reselect

Users shall be allowed to review and modify selections while ensuring the VP request remains satisfiable.

#### Mandatory Cards Section

If:

- There is only one option requested (or satisfiable), and
- Only one credential satisfies that option

Then:

- The credential shall be pre-selected.
- Deselection of that credential shall be disabled.

If:

- Multiple options exist

Then:

- User may switch between options.
- Share button shall only be enabled when the mandatory section remains satisfied.

#### Optional Cards Section

- Section shall be collapsed by default.
- User may expand the section.
- User may select credentials they wish to share.

### 2.1 Option Selection

Whenever an option is selected:

- All other options within the same credential set query shall be deselected.

This applies to:

- User selection
- Pre-selection

#### Case I: Option Contains One Credential Query

##### Case I.i

Credential query matches exactly one credential.

UI:

- Credential displayed as selectable.

Selection behavior:

- Credential is selected.

##### Case I.ii

Credential query matches multiple credentials.

UI:

- All matching credentials displayed.
- Selection control shall be radio button or checkbox based on whether multiple credential sharing is allowed.

Selection behavior:

- First credential is selected.

#### Case II: Option Contains Multiple Credential Queries

UI:

- Multiple Cards section displayed.

Selection behavior:

- First matching credential for every credential query shall be selected.


### 2.2 Credential Selection User Interaction

#### Multiple Credential Sharing Allowed

When user selects another credential:

- Existing selected credential remains selected.
- Newly selected credential is also selected.

#### Multiple Credential Sharing Not Allowed

When user selects another credential:

- Newly selected credential becomes selected.
- Previously selected credential is deselected.


### 3. Share Button Enablement

The Share button shall be enabled only when:

- All required credential set queries are satisfied.


## Edge Cases

### Same Credential Matching Multiple Credential Queries

Example VP Request:

```json
[
  {
    "options": [
      ["driver_license_condition"]
    ],
    "required": true
  },
  {
    "options": [
      ["age_above_18_condition"]
    ],
    "required": true
  }
]
```

Matching Credentials:

```json
{
  "driver_license_condition": ["Driver License"],
  "age_above_18_condition": ["Driver License", "Birth Certificate"]
}
```

#### Expected Behavior

If:

- User selects Driver License in Mandatory Cards Section 1

Then:

- Driver License shall be pre-selected in Mandatory Cards Section 2.

This behavior shall override the normal pre-selection logic because the same credential satisfies both credential queries.

Users may subsequently modify the selection as part of the Review and Reselect flow.

title: Backend for DCQL OpenIDVP 1.0 Mimoto
content:
Problem description:
> This document covers **only what changes inside Mimoto** for the 0.7.0 → 0.8.0 migration.
> Each flow diagram shows: the old behaviour, the new behaviour, and the exact Mimoto file/method being changed.

## Flow 1 — Authorization Request Phase

**Triggered by:** `POST /wallets/{id}/presentations`

---

### 🔴 BEFORE (0.7.0)

POST /wallets/{id}/presentations
  Body: { authorizationRequestUrl: "openid4vp://..." }
         │
         ▼
:page_facing_up: WalletPresentationServiceImpl.handleVPAuthorizationRequest()
  │
  ├─① verifierService.getTrusted[Verifier](https://github.com/inji/inji-web/issues/Verifier)s()  → ListVerifier
  │
  ├─② OpenID4VPService.create(presentationId)
  │       └─ new OpenID4VP(id, new WalletMetadata())
  │               ↑ verifiers NOT passed here — lost after this point
  │
  └─③ openID4VP.authenticateVerifier(
            urlString,
            preRegisteredVerifiers,   ← passed as method arg (removed in 0.8.0)
            shouldValidate
        )---

### 🟢 AFTER (0.8.0)

POST /wallets/{id}/presentations
  Body: { authorizationRequestUrl: "openid4vp://..." }
         │
         ▼
:page_facing_up: WalletPresentationServiceImpl.handleVPAuthorizationRequest()
  │
  ├─① getPreRegistered[Verifier](https://github.com/inji/inji-web/issues/Verifier)s()  → ListVerifier
  │
  ├─② OpenID4VPService.create(presentationId, trustedVerifiers)
  │       └─ new WalletConfig(..., trustedVerifiers)
  │               ↑ verifiers now INSIDE WalletConfig at creation time
  │       └─ new OpenID4VP(id, walletConfig)
  │
  ├─③ openID4VP.authenticateVerifier(
  │         urlString,
  │         shouldValidate            ← only 2 args, no trustedVerifiers
  │     )
  │       └─ returns AuthorizationRequest subtype
  │
  ├─④ detect spec version
  │         if (authReq instanceof AuthorizationDcqlRequest)
  │               → specVersion = V1_0
  │         else
  │               → specVersion = DRAFT_23
  │
  └─⑤ store in session:
            presentationId, authorizationRequest, specVersion, isPreRegistered---

### Changes in this flow

| # | What changes | Mimoto file | Type |
|---|-------------|-------------|------|
| 1 | `create()` now takes `trustedVerifiers` as second arg | `OpenID4VPService.java` | Fix |
| 2 | `WalletConfig` replaces `WalletMetadata`; verifiers go inside it | `OpenID4VPService.java` | Fix |
| 3 | `authenticateVerifier` drops the middle `trustedVerifiers` arg | `WalletPresentationServiceImpl.java` | Fix |
| 4 | Spec version is detected from the `AuthorizationRequest` subtype | `WalletPresentationServiceImpl.java` | New |
| 5 | `specVersion` field stored in session | `VerifiablePresentationSessionData.java` | New |

> **Summary**
> This is the entry point of the entire VP flow. The wallet receives the verifier's authorization request URL, validates who the verifier is, and sets up the session for all subsequent calls.
> The two key problems fixed here are:
> - In 0.7.0, trusted verifiers were passed directly as a method argument to `authenticateVerifier()` — the 0.8.0 library removed that argument, so they must now live inside `WalletConfig` at creation time.
> - 0.8.0 introduces two spec versions (Draft-23 and OVP 1.0 / DCQL). Mimoto detects which one the verifier is using by inspecting the returned `AuthorizationRequest` subtype (`AuthorizationDcqlRequest` → `V1_0`, anything else → `DRAFT_23`) and stores it as `specVersion` in the session. Every downstream call uses this value to pick the right code path. If `specVersion` is somehow absent (e.g. older session data), the fallback is `V1_0`.

---

## Flow 2 — Credential Matching Phase

**Triggered by:** `GET /wallets/{id}/presentations/{pid}/credentials`

---

### 🔴 BEFORE (0.7.0) — only one path existed

GET /wallets/{id}/presentations/{pid}/credentials
         │
         ▼
:page_facing_up: CredentialMatchingServiceImpl.getMatchingCredentials()
  │
  ├─ openID4VPService.resolvePresentationDefinition(presentationId, authRequest, preReg)
  │       └─ called authenticateVerifier with 3 args (broken in 0.8.0)
  │       └─ cast to AuthorizationPresentationExchangeRequest
  │       └─ return presentationDefinition
  │
  ├─ walletCredentialService.getDecryptedCredentials(walletId, key)
  │
  ├─ for each InputDescriptor:
  │       match credentials by format + constraints/fields
  │       descriptorId NOT recorded — map key will be wrong at submission
  │
  └─ store matchingCredentials in session (WITHOUT descriptorId)---

### 🟢 AFTER (0.8.0) — Draft-23 path

GET /wallets/{id}/presentations/{pid}/credentials
         │
         ▼
:page_facing_up: CredentialMatchingServiceImpl.getMatchingCredentials()
  │
  ├─ session.specVersion == DRAFT_23  (explicit only — null defaults to V1_0)
  │
  ├─ openID4VPService.resolvePresentationDefinition(presentationId, authRequest, preReg)
  │       └─ authenticateVerifier now called with 2 args
  │       └─ cast to AuthorizationPresentationExchangeRequest
  │       └─ return presentationDefinition
  │
  ├─ walletCredentialService.getDecryptedCredentials(walletId, key)
  │
  ├─ for each InputDescriptor:
  │       match credentials by format + constraints/fields
  │       record: credentialId → InputDescriptor.id  (stored as descriptorId)
  │
  ├─ build MatchingCredentialsResponseDTO:
  │       availableCredentials: List[CredentialDTO](https://github.com/inji/inji-web/issues/CredentialDTO)  (flat, deduped)
  │       missingClaims: Set[String](https://github.com/inji/inji-web/issues/String)
  │
  └─ store matchingCredentials WITH descriptorId per DTO in session---

### 🟢 AFTER (0.8.0) — OVP 1.0 / DCQL path (entirely new)

GET /wallets/{id}/presentations/{pid}/credentials
         │
         ▼
:page_facing_up: CredentialMatchingServiceImpl.getMatchingCredentials()
  │
  ├─ session.specVersion == V1_0
  │
  ├─ openID4VPService.resolveDcqlQuery(presentationId, authRequest, preReg)
  │       └─ create(id, verifiers) → authenticateVerifier(url, shouldValidate)
  │       └─ cast to AuthorizationDcqlRequest
  │       └─ return dcqlQuery
  │
  ├─ walletCredentialService.getDecryptedCredentials(walletId, key)
  │
  ├─ for each CredentialQuery in dcqlQuery.credentials:
  │       queryId = credentialQuery.id
  │       format  = credentialQuery.format
  │       match wallet VCs by format
  │       if credentialQuery.claims != null → filter by claim paths/values
  │       if credentialQuery.multiple == false → allow only 1 match
  │       store dto.descriptorId = credentialQuery.id  (queryId as bridge key)
  │
  ├─ evaluate credentialSets (if present):
  │       for each CredentialSetQuery:
  │           if required=true and no option satisfied → mark missing
  │
  ├─ build DcqlMatchingCredentialsResponseDTO:
  │       queryGroups: List[DcqlQueryGroup](https://github.com/inji/inji-web/issues/DcqlQueryGroup)
  │           each: { queryId, multiple, availableCredentials, missingClaims }
  │       credentialSets: List[CredentialSetInfo](https://github.com/inji/inji-web/issues/CredentialSetInfo)   ← option structure for the UI
  │           each: { required, options: List[List<queryId](https://github.com/inji/inji-web/issues/List%3CqueryId)> }
  │           e.g. { required:true, options:[["pan"],["aadhaar"],["voter_id","dl"]] }
  │       mandatory/optional logic lives only in credentialSets (not on queryGroup)
  │
  └─ store dcqlMatchingCredentials (with queryId as descriptorId) in session
```

---

### Changes in this flow

| # | What changes | Mimoto file | Type |
|---|-------------|-------------|------|
| 1 | resolvePresentationDefinition() fixes authenticateVerifier to 2 args | OpenID4VPService.java | Fix |
| 2 | descriptorId recorded on each matched DTO during Draft-23 matching | CredentialMatchingServiceImpl.java | Fix |
| 3 | Top-level routing by specVersion added | CredentialMatchingServiceImpl.java | New |
| 4 | resolveDcqlQuery() new method to extract DCQLQuery | OpenID4VPService.java | New |
| 5 | matchDcql() — full DCQL matching loop | CredentialMatchingServiceImpl.java | New |
| 6 | matchesDcqlQuery() — format + claim path matching helper | CredentialMatchingServiceImpl.java | New |
| 7 | DcqlQueryGroup DTO per query in response | DcqlQueryGroup.java | New |
| 8 | descriptorId field added to carry descriptor/…

title: Spike: Analyse and Design Support for mdoc (mso_mdoc) Credentials in Inji Web Wallet
content:
Problem description:
## Background

Inji Mobile Wallet currently supports issuance, storage, rendering, and presentation of mdoc (mso_mdoc) credentials. The implementation includes handling OpenID4VCI mdoc credential responses, CBOR decoding, transformation into a renderable JSON structure, issuer metadata-driven rendering, and mdoc-specific processing.

As part of feature parity and broader credential format support, Inji Web Wallet should support mdoc credentials alongside existing credential formats.

Before implementation, a technical analysis is required to understand architecture changes, browser-specific considerations, reusable components from existing Kotlin, Swift, and JavaScript implementations, and OpenID4VCI/OpenID4VP requirements.

## Problem Statement

Inji Web currently does not support mdoc credentials.

Supporting mdoc credentials requires analysis of:

- OpenID4VCI issuance flow for mso_mdoc credentials
- Processing Base64URL encoded CBOR payloads in browser environments
- Credential storage strategy
- Rendering mdoc claims using Credential Issuer metadata
- OpenID4VP presentation requirements
- Future verification and trust framework considerations
- Reusability of existing mobile wallet implementations

## Objective

Analyse the effort, architecture, dependencies, and technical approach required to support mdoc credentials in Inji Web Wallet.

The outcome of this spike should be a proposed implementation approach and a set of follow-up engineering stories.

## Scope

### Issuance Flow Analysis

Analyse how mdoc credentials are currently issued and processed in the mobile wallet implementation.

Areas to investigate:

- OpenID4VCI mso_mdoc credential request structure
- Credential response handling
- Base64URL encoded credential processing
- Browser compatibility considerations
- Required changes in Web Wallet issuance flows
- Alignment with OID4VCI 1.0 specifications

### CBOR Processing

Investigate browser-compatible approaches for decoding and parsing CBOR payloads received as mdoc credentials.

Areas to analyse:

- Existing JavaScript CBOR libraries
- Browser performance considerations
- Error handling strategy
- Handling large credential payloads
- Conversion from CBOR to renderable JSON

Expected Outcome:

- Recommended CBOR processing library
- Proposed parsing architecture
- Reusability analysis from existing JavaScript implementation

### Credential Storage Strategy

Analyse how mdoc credentials should be stored in Inji Web.

Areas to investigate:

- Storage of original CBOR payload
- Storage of processed JSON representation
- IndexedDB compatibility
- Browser storage limitations
- Synchronisation with current credential storage model

Questions:

- Should the original CBOR payload always be preserved?
- Should processed JSON be cached for rendering?
- How should browser refresh and session recovery be handled?

Expected Outcome:

- Recommended storage architecture
- Data model changes required

### Credential Rendering

Analyse rendering requirements for mdoc credentials.

Areas to investigate:

- Mapping processed mdoc claims to existing UI components
- Rendering labels from Credential Issuer metadata
- Support for display metadata
- Support for nested claims and arrays
- Field ordering using issuer metadata order property

Expected Outcome:

- Rendering architecture proposal
- UI component impact analysis

### OpenID4VP Presentation Support

Analyse requirements for presenting mdoc credentials using OpenID4VP.

Areas to investigate:

- Presentation Definition processing
- mdoc-specific credential matching
- Presentation submission generation
- Cross-device presentation flows
- Compatibility with verifier expectations
- Mixed format requests containing mdoc and W3C VC credentials

Questions:

- Can a verifier request mso_mdoc and W3C VC formats together?
- What changes are required in credential matching logic?
- How should mdoc presentation responses be generated?

Expected Outcome:

- Proposed presentation architecture
- Identified implementation dependencies

### Verification and Trust Framework Analysis

Analyse future requirements for verification and trust validation of mdoc credentials.

Areas to investigate:

- Document Signer (DS) certificate validation
- Certificate chain validation
- Root CA trust management
- VICAL integration requirements
- Trust framework dependencies

Expected Outcome:

- High-level verification architecture
- Future roadmap recommendations

### Reusability Analysis

Review existing implementations available in:

- Kotlin VCI Library
- Swift VCI Library
- JavaScript VCI Library
- Inji Mobile Wallet

Identify:

- Reusable parsing logic
- Shared utilities
- Common rendering approaches
- Shared data models
- Potential code consolidation opportunities

## Deliverables

### Architecture Proposal

Document the proposed architecture for:

- Issuance
- Storage
- Rendering
- Presentation
- Verification

### Gap Analysis

Compare:

- Existing Mobile Wallet capabilities
- Current Inji Web capabilities

Identify missing functionality and implementation dependencies.

### Technical Design Recommendations

Provide recommendations for:

- CBOR processing
- Storage model
- Rendering model
- Metadata handling
- Presentation handling
- Verification strategy

### Implementation Backlog

Create follow-up engineering stories covering:

- mdoc issuance support
- mdoc storage support
- mdoc rendering support
- OpenID4VP presentation support
- Verification and trust framework support

### Effort Estimation

Provide effort estimates and implementation sequencing recommendations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Existing mobile wallet mdoc implementation is analysed.
- Reusable components are identified.
- Browser-specific implementation considerations are documented.
- Storage strategy is proposed.
- Rendering strategy is proposed.
- OpenID4VP presentation requirements are analysed.
- Verification and trust framework requirements are documented.
- Gap analysis between Mobile Wallet and Web Wallet is completed.
- Follow-up implementation stories are identified.
- Risks, assumptions, and open questions are documented.

## References: 
-  https://mosip.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/Inji/pages/1377337347/mDoc+mDL
- OpenID4VCI 1.0 Specification
- OpenID4VP Specification
- ISO 18013-5 mdoc Specification
- Existing mdoc implementation in Kotlin, Swift, and JavaScript VCI libraries
- Existing Inji Mobile Wallet mdoc implementation
- Existing mdoc rendering and storage ADRs
- Existing mdoc verification and VICAL analysis documents

title: UI/UX Revocation Feature enhancements
content:
Problem description:
“Last Checked” means the last time the wallet attempted to check status — not whether it succeeded.
It should always update when the user manually refreshes or when an auto-refresh occurs.
This provides the user a clear signal:
“The wallet last tried to verify your credential’s status at [timestamp].”
Rationale for always updating timestamp
User Transparency: It helps users know when the last verification attempt happened, even if the backend or network failed.
Debugging clarity: Easier to differentiate between network or verification failures and old cached data.
Consistency: Keeps the “Last Checked” label meaningful in all states — success, revoked, expired, or failed.
Important: Distinguish in UI
To avoid confusion, ensure UI clearly separates:
Status: Revoked / Valid / Unknown
Last Checked:
If the last check failed (due to connectivity or backend issue), you can optionally show:
“Last checked at [time] — status could not be verified.”
