title: INJIVER-1041: Inji Verify SDK: Customize UI Component styling
content:
Problem description:
*Purpose:* Customizing the UI component styling in Inji Verify SDK for SCAN/UPLOAD or OPENID4VP flows serves several key purposes:

1. *1. Branding & Theming for Integrators*

- Different system integrators or countries using Inji Verify may have their own branding guidelines.

- Custom styling allows them to align the UI with their existing design systems, ensuring consistency in look and feel.

- Example: Colors, fonts, and button styles can be adjusted to match the integrator’s theme.

1. *2. Seamless User Experience*

- Users should not feel like they are interacting with an external module when scanning, uploading, or performing OpenID4VP verifications.

- Customization ensures the UI Components blends naturally with the host application’s UX/UI.

1. *3.* *-Accessibility & Localization-*

- -Different users may have specific accessibility needs (e.g., high contrast, font sizes, text alignments).-

- -Custom styling helps enhance readability and usability for a diverse user base.-

- -Right-to-left (RTL) language support (e.g., Arabic) can be adjusted for correct layout direction.-

1. *4. Device & Platform Adaptability*

- Custom styles can be optimized to look great on mobile, tablet, and desktop devices.

- Ensures smooth experience across different browsers and OS environments.

1. *5. Custom Animations & UI Behavior*

- Allows integrators to add custom animations, transitions, or loading indicators to improve UX.

- Example: Custom loading spinners when scanning a QR code or fetching credentials via OpenID4VP.

1. ----

1. *Examples of UI Customization in Different Components*

||Component||Customization Possibilities||
|*SCAN/ UPLOAD Component* (QR code scanning)|Modify scanner frame color, button styles, animations, success/error messages|
|*OPENID4VP Component* (Verifiable Presentation flow)|Adjust layout, colors, buttons, and text for credential sharing and verification
if a verifier wants to have a logo added inside|

1. *Conclusion*

Customizing the UI in Inji Verify SDK enhances adoption, usability, and integration flexibility while ensuring the SDK remains visually and functionally aligned with diverse partners’ ecosystems.

title: INJIVER-1051:  Implement OpenID4VP Draft 24 Enhancements in Inji Verify
content:
Problem description:
refer [https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/INJIMOB-3083](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/INJIMOB-3083|smart-link)  for draft 23 compatibility with mobile wallet

----

*Purpose:* ​The OpenID for Verifiable Presentations (OpenID4VP) specification has undergone several revisions between Draft 21 and Draft 24, incorporating significant enhancements and refinements. Therefore, Inji Verify should be able to support the latest OpenID4VP Draft 24 specifications, so that the system remains compliant with the latest standards, ensures better interoperability, and enhances security in verifiable presentations.

1. *Pre-Requisites*

1. Wallet and verifier implementations compliant with earlier OpenID4VP drafts.

1. Existing support for JSON-LD and Verifiable Presentation exchange.

1. Ensure the following +introductions/ modifications as per latest draft version+ is taken care of:

1. Draft 22

1. *Introduction of the Digital Credentials Query Language (DCQL):*
#* DCQL was introduced as an alternative to the Presentation Exchange protocol, providing a flexible mechanism for querying digital credentials.

1. *Addition of Transaction Data Mechanism:*
#* A new mechanism was added to bind user identification/authentication with authorization processes, facilitating use cases such as completing payment transactions or signing documents using Qualified Electronic Signatures (QES).​

1. *Modification of Client Identifier Scheme:*
#* The `client_id_scheme` parameter is removed. Instead, the client ID scheme is now represented as a prefix on the `client_id`, addressing security concerns associated with the previous approach.

1. *Clarification on* `client_metadata` *parameter*

  1. OPTIONAL. A JSON object containing the Verifier metadata values. It MUST be UTF-8 encoded. The following metadata parameters MAY be used:
##* `jwks`: OPTIONAL. It MAY contain one or more public keys, such as those used by the Wallet as an input to a key agreement that may be used for encryption of the Authorization Response, or where the Wallet will require the public key of the Verifier to generate the Verifiable Presentation. This allows the Verifier to pass ephemeral keys specific to this Authorization Request. Public keys included in this parameter MUST NOT be used to verify the signature of signed Authorization Requests.
##* `vp_formats`: REQUIRED when not available to the Wallet via another mechanism.
##* `authorization_signed_response_alg`: OPTIONAL.
##* `authorization_encrypted_response_alg`: OPTIONAL.
##* `authorization_encrypted_response_enc`: OPTIONAL.

1. -Fixed #227: Enabled non-breaking extensibility.-

1. -Fixed #383: Completed IANA Considerations section.-

1. Draft 23

1. *Corrections and Consistency Improvements:*
#* Percent-encoding of URI examples was fixed.​
#* An example was corrected to use 'wallet' instead of 'client' for clarity.​
#* Consistency between Self-Issued OpenID Provider (SIOP) example requests and responses was improved.​
#* Alignment was achieved between example requests and the SD-JWT key binding JWT.​

1. *Encryption Algorithm Options:*
#* A note was added highlighting the availability of various encryption algorithms, including those from the Hybrid Public Key Encryption (HPKE) draft.​

1. *Parameter Additions and Updates:*
#* `transaction_data` and `dcql_query` were added to the list of allowed parameters in the W3C Digital Credentials API appendix.​
#* The credential format identifier `vc+sd-jwt` was changed to `dc+sd-jwt` to align with the media type in draft -06 of [I-D.ietf-oauth-sd-jwt-vc], and corresponding updates were made to the `typ` value in examples.​

1. *Clarifications and Generalizations:*
#* References to the OpenID for Verifiable Credential Issuance (OpenID4VCI) credential format section were removed.​
#* Clarifications were made regarding the profiling of OpenID4VP.​
#* Credential format-specific DCQL parameters were moved to an annex.
#* References to the W3C Digital Credentials API were generalized.​
#* The response mode value for OpenID4VP over the Digital Credentials API was changed.​
#* The specification was updated to use Presentation Exchange version 2.1.1 (previously 2.0.0).

1. fixed percent-encoding of URI examples

1. fixed an example that used 'client' where 'wallet' is more appropriate

1. make SIOP example request/response consistent with each other

1. make example request and example SD-JWT key binding JWT consistent

1. add note that there are a choice of encryption JWE algorithms available, including the HPKE draft

1. add `transaction_data` & `dcql_query` to list of allowed parameters in W3C Digital Credentials API appendix

1. change credential format identifier `vc+sd-jwt` to `dc+sd-jwt` to align with the media type in draft -06 of [[I-D.ietf-oauth-sd-jwt-vc](https://openid.net/specs/openid-4-verifiable-presentations-1_0-24.html#I-D.ietf-oauth-sd-jwt-vc)] and update `typ` accordingly in examples

1. remove references to the openid4vci credential format section

1. clarified what profiling OID4VP means

1. moved credential format specific DCQL parameters to the annex

1. generalized W3C Digital Credentials API references

1. changed response mode value for the OID4VP over the DC API

1. updated to PE ver 2.1.1 (used to be 2.0.0)

1. Draft 24

1. *Authorization Request Object Requirements:*
#* The `typ` value in the request object is now required to be `oauth-authz-req+jwt`

1. *Session Transcript Requirements:*
#* New requirements for `SessionTranscript` were specified to enhance security and interoperability.​

1. *-Mobile Driving License (mdoc) Specific Enhancements:-*
#* -An intent_to_retain mechanism was added for mdoc, utilizing definitions from ISO/IEC 18013-5-
#* -The use of claims path pointers for mdoc-based credentials was introduced.​-

These revisions reflect the ongoing efforts to enhance the OpenID4VP specification, addressing security considerations, improving interoperability, and incorporating feedback from implementers and the broader community.

1. *Basic Flow of OpenID4VP Cross Device flow:*

The following outlines the step-by-step flow for implementing and handling the changes introduced in Draft 23 and thereby continued in Draft 24:

1. *Verifier Initiates Authorization Request*
#* The verifier generates an Authorization Request containing only the `request_uri`.
#* The `request_uri` points to a URL where the signed Authorization Request Object is hosted.
#* The QR code is generated with minimal data, including `client_id` and `request_uri`.

1. *Wallet Scans QR Code*
#* The wallet scans the QR code containing the `request_uri` and `client_id`.
#* The wallet retrieves the full Authorization Request data from the `request_uri` using the specified HTTP method (default is GET).

1. *Authorization Request Validation*
#* The wallet validates the retrieved Authorization Request Object, including signature verification and parsing of required fields such as `request_uri` ,`client_id`(mandatory field).
#* `request_uri_method `(Optional Field) .

1. *Credential Selection by Wallet*
#* The wallet matches the verifier's presentation definition with its stored credentials.
#* The wallet constructs the `VP_token` as an array containing multiple credentials in supported formats.

1. *Constructing the Presentation Submission*
#* The wallet constructs the presentation submission, including paths to each credential within the `VP_token`.
#* The presentation submission is securely signed and optionally encrypted if required.

1. *Wallet Sends Authorization Response*
#* The wallet sends the Authorization Response back to the verifier, including the `VP_token` array and the presentation submission.

1. *Verifier Validates Response*
#* The verifier validates the Authorization Response, including signature checks and parsing the `VP_token` array.
#* The verifier ensures all required credentials are included and meet the presentation definition criteria.

1. *Presentation Complete*
#* Upon successful validation, the verifier completes the presentation process and displays the results on verifier portal.

 

1. *Acceptance Criteria*

1. The `VP_token` is implemented as an array holding different credentials but it is a single credential format then it will a JSON object not an array.

1. Wallet’s authorization response includes credentials in different VC formats, supporting Presentation Exchange.

1. The presentation submission properly constructs paths to credentials and includes this in the response.

1. The `client_id_scheme` is removed, and `client_id` is updated to use a prefix addressing the security issue (e.g., `redirect_uri:http.client.example.org`).

1. All changes are tested for compliance with Draft 24 and functionality across wallet and verifier systems.

1. *Technical Tasks*

1. *VP Token as Array*
#* Update wallet logic to construct and return `VP_token` as an array holding multiple credentials in different VC formats.
#* Update verifier logic to parse and validate `VP_token` arrays.

1. *Presentation Exchange Updates*
#* Modify wallet's authorization response to include credentials of different VC formats.
#* Construct the presentation submission, including paths to credentials, and ensure compliance with the specification.

1. *Client ID Changes*
#* Remove `client_id_scheme` from the Authorization Request.
#* Update `client_id` to use the required prefix format (e.g., `redirect_uri:http.client.example.org`).

1. *Testing and Validation*
#* Conduct compliance testing to ensure all changes align with Draft 24.
#* Perform end-to-end testing of the Verifiable Presentation flow for different VC formats.

1. *Subtasks*

1. Update wallet logic for `VP_token` array construction and handling.

1. Update verifier logic to process and validate `VP_token` arrays.

1. Modify the Authorization Request construction to remove `client_id_scheme` and implement the prefixed `client_id`.

1. Implement the use of `request_uri` in Authorization Requests.

1. Add mechanisms for signing and encrypting the Request Object.

1. Ensure presentation submission includes credential paths in compliance with the specification.

1. Test different VC formats (e.g., JSON-LD) in the Presentation Exchange flow.

1. *Dependencies*

1. Wallet and verifier libraries supporting Presentation Exchange.

1. Signing and encryption libraries for Request Objects.

1. QR code generation and parsing tools.

1. *Deliverables*

1. Updated wallet and verifier logic compliant with Draft 24.

1. A minimized and secure Authorization Request process using `request_uri`.

1. Support for `VP_token` arrays and multiple VC formats.

1. Documentation outlining the changes and providing implementation details.

1. Testing and compliance reports confirming functionality and standards alignment.

*Out of scope:*

1. Testing different VC format is out of scope for this card because currently mDoc sharing support is not available to test different VC format.

title: INJIVER-1072: UI/UX Design: Adding Flash Functionality to QR Code Scanning in Inji Verify
content:
Problem description:
*Purpose:*
To enhance the usability and effectiveness of the QR code scanning feature in Inji Verify by adding a flash functionality. This will improve the scanning experience in various lighting conditions and ensure accurate scanning.

*Pre-requisites:*

- The user has a device with a camera.

- The Inji Verify portal is accessible online.

- A QR code is available for scanning.

*Basic Flow:*

1. *Initiate Scan:*
The user navigates to the QR code scan page within Inji Verify.

1. *Activate Camera:*
The device camera activates, displaying the camera view on the screen.

1. *Flash Toggle:*
The user toggles the flash to either on or off, based on lighting conditions.

1. *Scan QR Code:*
The system processes the captured image with the flash settings to scan and verify the QR code.

1. *Verification Result:*
The system displays the verification result to the user.

*Alternate Flows:*

- *Flash Auto Mode:*
Implement an automatic flash mode that activates the flash based on ambient lighting conditions.

*Scenarios:*

- *Daylight Scanning:*
The user scans a QR code in a well-lit environment without needing to use the flash.

- *Low Light Scanning:*
The user scans a QR code in a dim environment and toggles the flash to improve visibility.

*Data Fields:*

- Flash state (on/off/auto)

*Acceptance Criteria:*

1. 1. Flash Toggle Functionality:

- *Objective:* Ensure users can control the flash according to their scanning environment.

- *Criteria:*

  - The user interface includes a toggle switch or button clearly labeled for flash functionality.

  - The flash can be toggled on or off before and during the scanning process.

  - Changes in flash status (on/off) are immediately reflected in the UI and affect subsequent scans.

1. 2. Shadow Elimination:

- *Objective:* Ensure clear visibility of QR codes by eliminating shadows cast by the device or surroundings.

- *Criteria:*

  - During scanning, there should be no significant shadows obscuring the QR code on the screen or document.

  - The lighting should be evenly distributed to avoid any part of the QR code being in shadow.

1. 3. Impact of Flash in Well-Lit Environments:

- *Objective:* Prevent unnecessary activation of flash in well-lit environments where it may not be needed.

- *Criteria:*

  - Flash functionality is designed to enhance scanning in dimly lit or dark environments.

  - In well-lit conditions (daylight or bright indoor lighting), the users should not activate the flash.

  - Minimizing reflections or glare to improve QR code visibility.

1. 4. Optimal Camera Positioning:

- *Objective:* Ensure the QR code remains in focus and clear during scanning with or without flash.

- *Criteria:*

  - Users are instructed to maintain a medium distance between the camera and the QR code.

  - Too close or too far positioning should be avoided to prevent blurring or loss of focus.

  - The system provides visual or audio feedback if the camera is too close or far from the QR code, if possible.

1. 5. Scanning Accuracy with Flash Settings:

- *Objective:* Ensure the system accurately scans and verifies QR codes regardless of flash settings.

- *Criteria:*

  - Verification results are displayed promptly after scanning, indicating whether the QR code is valid or not.

  - The system handles different lighting conditions effectively without compromising scan accuracy.

*Exceptions:*

- *Device Camera Permissions Not Granted:*
Prompt the user to enable camera permissions.

- *Flash Hardware Not Available:*
Disable the flash toggle and notify the user.

- *Unclear QR Code Image:*
Prompt the user to recapture the image or upload it manually.

||*Scenario*||*Error Message*||
|Device Camera Permissions Not Granted
{color:#0747a6} (To be Updated from the previous one){color}|"Camera permissions not granted. Please enable camera access in your device or browser settings to proceed with QR code scanning."|
|{color:#bf2600}Unclear QR Code Image/Blurry Image{color}
{color:#bf2600}(Updated from the previous one){color}|{color:#bf2600}"QR code not clear. Please recapture the image or upload the QR code manually."{color}|
|{color:#bf2600}Flash Hardware Not Available{color}|{color:#bf2600}"Flash functionality is not available on this device."{color}|
|Camera Initialization Failure

- If phone camera is broken

- If hardware is damged|"Camera Failed"|
|Poor Lighting Detected|No error message in this scenario; flash should open up automatically.|
|Partially Obstructed QR Code|No error message (Out of Scope)|
|Low Contrast QR Code|No error message (Out of Scope)|
|Distorted QR Code|No error message (Out of Scope)|
|Reflections or Glare on QR Code|No error message (Out of Scope)|
|QR Code is Too Small or Too Far Away|No error message (Out of Scope)|
|QR Code is Damaged or Illegible|No error message (Out of Scope)|
|QR Code is Out of Focus|No error message (Out of Scope)|

*Documentation:*

- End-user guide updated to include instructions for using the Flash features.

- Technical documentation detailing the implementation of the flash functionalities.

*Reference UX:*

- Include wireframes or mockups showing the QR code scan page with the flash toggle.

- Mobile UX *-* [*Link to mobile flow wireframes*](https://xd.adobe.com/view/5d08134e-023c-428d-ba88-679b0cd2aaad-085b/screen/915af328-d22a-400a-8b59-a2c8bfed67df/)

*Compatibility:*

- Ensure the feature works across all supported devices and operating systems (iOS, Android).

- Test on various device models with different camera capabilities.

*Environment:*

- dev1

- qa-inji

*Design Principles:*

- User-centred design focuses on ease of use and accessibility.

- Ensure responsive design to accommodate different screen sizes and orientations.

- Maintain consistent UI/UX across the portal.

*GenderMag:*

- *Motivations:* Ensure the feature appeals to users motivated by efficiency and completeness.

- *Information Processing Style:* Provide clear instructions and feedback to support users with different cognitive styles.

- *Computer Self-Efficacy:* Offer guidance and reassurance to users who might lack confidence in using the new feature.

- *Attitude Toward Risk:* Allow safe experimentation with the flash features without negative consequences.

- *Learning Style:* Support both guided and exploratory learning through clear prompts and intuitive design.

title: INJIVER-1095: Enhancing Inji Verify SDK - Scan/ Upload & OpenID4VP Components for Multi-Platform Support
content:
Problem description:
*Problem Statement:* Currently, the Inji Verify SDK - Scan/ Upload & OpenID4VP Components is designed to work exclusively with ReactJS applications. To enable broader adoption across various platforms, the component needs to be re-written in WebAssembly (WASM) and provided with necessary wrappers.

1. *Proposed Approach:*

1. *Rewrite in WASM:*
#* Convert the core logic of the OpenID4VP Component into WebAssembly to ensure compatibility across different environments.

1. *Develop Platform-Specific Wrappers:*
#* Create wrappers around the WASM implementation to make the component accessible in *non-ReactJS* applications, such as *Angular, Vue, NativeScript, and mobile frameworks like React Native and Flutter*.

1. *Provide WASM & Wrappers as Deliverables:*
#* Deliver the WASM package along with a set of pre-built wrappers for common platforms.
#* Offer clear documentation on how others can extend support for additional platforms by writing their own wrappers around the WASM implementation.

This approach will enhance the portability and usability of the OpenID4VP Component, allowing integrators to use it seamlessly across various frontend and mobile environments.

----

- Inji Verify SDK works on ReactJS applications.

- To support on other platforms, re-write in WASM and write wrapper around it to make it compatible with different platforms.

- Provide wrappers and WASM as a deliverable too so that others can pick same up and write wrapper for it then use it for their use case.

title: INJIVER-1119: Optimize vp-result call
content:
Problem description:
*Purpose:* Optimize the `vp-result` call so that fetching the submission result is faster and requires fewer database operations, leading to improved system performance.

*Description:*
Currently, the `vp-submission` table stores submissions based only on the `requestId`, while the result is fetched based on the `transactionId`. This leads to additional database operations:

- First, the latest `requestId` must be fetched using the `transactionId`.

- Then, the result is retrieved using that `requestId`.

This two-step process negatively impacts performance, especially under high loads.
The goal is to *optimize the logic* to minimize database queries, reduce latency, and improve the overall performance of the `vp-result` call in the OpenID4VP cross-device flow.

*Acceptance Criteria:*

1. The system should directly retrieve the result using the `transactionId` without needing an additional lookup for the `requestId`.

1. Database queries for the `vp-result` call should be reduced from two steps to a single optimized query.

1. Performance benchmarking should show improved response times for the `vp-result` API compared to the current implementation.

1. No functional regression — the optimized logic must return the correct and expected results for valid transaction IDs.

1. Adequate unit and integration tests must be updated/added to validate the new retrieval logic.

{color:#ff5630}*Additional Notes:*{color}

- {color:#ff5630}Consider schema changes or additional indexing if necessary to support direct lookup using {color}`transactionId`{color:#ff5630}.{color}

- {color:#ff5630}Ensure backward compatibility where needed.{color}

----

_Currently the vp-submission table stores submissions based on only_ `requesId` _and the result is fetched based on_ `transactionId`_.  This impacts the performance as we have to fetch the latest_ `requestId` _and then fetch the result. Optimise this logic to improve on lesser DB operations and higher performance._

title: INJIVER-1194: INJI Verify SDK should support non-react components
content:
Problem description:
Inji Verify SDK is a library which exposes React components for integrating Inji Verify features seamlessly into any relaying party application.  This is because the component is written in React + TypesScrpt.  It does not support other frameworks such as Angular, Vue, Ajax etc 

This is a limitation.

Countries may not have adopted progressive frameworks like React.   They might be running older frameworks, may be even PhP.    They need integration with INJI Verify SDK if we have to get them to use the INJI Credentialing stack.   

This is causing some trouble in executing our pilots.

title: INJIVER-1142: <to be removed>: Support Array Format for vp_token When Multiple VCs Are Shared
content:
Problem description:
*Title:* Enhance `vp_token` Handling to Support Array Format for Multiple VCs

*Purpose:*
To enable Inji Verify to handle `vp_token` as an array when multiple formats (e.g., `ldp_vc` and `mso_mdoc`) are shared by the Wallet, while retaining current behavior for single-format sharing.

*Pre-requisites:*

- Inji Mobile v0.17.0 supports sharing multiple VC formats.

- Inji Verify already processes `vp_token` as an object for a single format.

*Basic Flow:*

1. Inji Mobile sends a `vp_token` containing one or more VC formats.

1. Inji Verify parses the `vp_token`.

1. If only `ldp_vc` is shared, it is received as an object.

1. If `ldp_vc` and `mso_mdoc` are shared, `vp_token` is received as an *array*.

1. Inji Verify adjusts its logic to process both object and array structures.

*Acceptance Criteria:*

- System continues to function when `vp_token` is a single object (backward compatible).

- System can parse and handle `vp_token` when received as an array.

- Verification continues successfully regardless of VC format(s) shared.

Discussion and resolution:

title: INJIVER-1143: Convert Verify Service into a Library (POM Dependency)
content:
Problem description:
*Description / Purpose:*
Verify Service to be packaged as a reusable library (POM dependency) instead of a standalone deployable service, so that it can be directly integrated into other components (e.g., Certify) without requiring an additional deployment.

- For *Inji Verify*, it will continue functioning as a service.

- For *Certify*, during the _Presentation in Issuance_ flow, it will be consumed as a library dependency.

This approach avoids the need for a separate deployment and reduces external service dependencies, ensuring Certify can internally create VP requests and validate VP responses using the same logic already available in Verify Service.

1. *Acceptance Criteria*

1. Verify Service codebase is refactored to support dual usage:
#* As a standalone service (for Inji Verify).
#* As a library (POM dependency) for integration into Certify so that Certify should be able to Create VP requests using the library and Validate/verify VP responses using the library.

1. No additional deployable Verify Service should be required when using Certify’s issuance features.

1. Backward compatibility must be maintained for Inji Verify.

1. _Documentation updated to explain how to include Verify as a POM dependency in Certify._

* Use a rewiring bundler → yet to try ref: [https://github.com/wojtekmaj/react-pdf/issues/280#issuecomment-522574510|https://github.com/wojtekmaj/react-pdf/issues/280#issuecomment-522574510|smart-link]

title: INJIVER-1183: [VC-VERIFIER] - Adding support for JsonWebSignature2020 with Ed25519 algorithm type for VC verification
content:
Problem description:
As a VC-Verifier library, I want to support `JsonWebSignature2020` with Ed25519 signatures, so that I can verify Verifiable Credentials issued with this modern cryptographic standard and ensure broader interoperability.

*Description:*

Extend VC-Verifier library's capabilities to validate Verifiable Credentials (VCs) that leverage `JsonWebSignature2020` as a verification method, specifically when used with the `Ed25519` algorithm type for digital signatures. By implementing support for this combination, the verifier will be able to process a wider range of secure and compliant credentials from various issuers.

*Acceptance Criteria:*

- *VC-Verifier library Update:* The VC-Verifier library is updated to include the necessary cryptographic libraries and parsing logic for `JsonWebSignature2020` and `Ed25519`.

- *Successful Key Parsing:* Given a Verifiable Credential containing a `JsonWebSignature2020` verification method with an `Ed25519` public key, the VC-Verifier library successfully parses and extracts the public key.

- *Successful Signature Validation:* When presented with a Verifiable Credential signed using an `Ed25519` private key (whose corresponding public key is expressed via `JsonWebSignature2020`), the VC-Verifier library successfully validates the digital signature.

- *Error Handling for Invalid Signatures:* The VC-Verifier library provides clear and informative error messages when it encounters an invalid `Ed25519` signature or a malformed `JsonWebSignature2020` representation.

- *Documentation Update:* Relevant technical documentation (e.g., API documentation, internal developer guides, GitHub README etc) is updated to reflect the new support for `JsonWebSignature2020` and `Ed25519`.

title: DCQL support in Authorization Request as per OpenID4VP spec v1.0
content:
Problem description:
**Purpose**
**As a** Verifier  
**I want to** submit VP Authorization Requests using DCQL syntax instead of presentationDefinition  
**So that** I can flexibly request distributed credentials in compliance with OpenID4VP v1.0 specification.

To comply with OpenID4VP 1.0 Final Specification,all existing verifier configurations in Inji Verify that store **presentation_definition** and **presentation_definition_uri** parameters must be migrated to ***DCQL*** using ***dcql*query or scope.***

## Description

Implement support for Distributed Claims Query Language (DCQL) in Inji Verify's VP Request endpoints to comply with OpenID4VP v1.0 specifications. This requires updating the VP request initiation and retrieval endpoints to accept  `dcql_query` (v1.0 standard) format while establishing a migration path for existing requests.

 VPRequestController

1. POST /vp-request → /v2/vp-request
Supports DCQL query
❗ Not backward compatible

2. POST /vp-session-request → /v2/vp-session-request
Supports DCQL query
❗ Not backward compatible

3. GET /vp-request/{requestId} → /v2/vp-request/{requestId}
Supports DCQL query
❗ Not backward compatible

4. GET /vp-request/{requestId}/status
✅ No changes

New Request Body Schema (Example for /generate):

```
{
  "client_id": "https://verifier.example.com",
  "nonce": "MTc2Mzk1NTY5NDI5NQ",
  "dcql_query": {
    "credentials": [
      {
        "id": "student_id_credential_query",
        "format": "dc+sd-jwt",
        "meta": {
          "vct_values": [
            "student_id_credential"
          ]
        },
        "claims": [
          {
            "id": "last_name",
            "path": [
              "last_name"
            ]
          },
          {
            "id": "first_name",
            "path": [
              "first_name"
            ]
          },
          {
            "id": "given_name",
            "path": [
              "given_name"
            ]
          }
        ],
        "claim_sets": [
          [
            "first_name",
            "last_name"
          ],
          [
            "given_name"
          ]
        ]
      },
      {
        "id": "age_credential_query",
        "format": "ldp_vc",
        "meta": {
          "type_values": [
            "https://www.w3.org/2018/credentials#VerifiableCredential",
            "https://example.org/credentials#AgeCredential"
          ]
        },
        "claims": [
          {
            "id": "last_name",
            "path": [
              "credentialSubject",
              "last_name"
            ]
          },
          {
            "id": "first_name",
            "path": [
              "credentialSubject",
              "first_name"
            ]
          },
          {
            "id": "given_name",
            "path": [
              "credentialSubject",
              "given_name"
            ]
          }
        ],
        "claim_sets": [
          [
            "first_name",
            "last_name"
          ],
          [
            "last_name",
            "given_name"
          ]
        ]
      }
    ],
    "credential_sets": [
      {
        "options": [
          [
            "age_credential_query"
          ]
        ]
      },
      {
        "options": [
          [
            "student_id_credential_query"
          ]
        ],
        "required": false
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

**Data Fields**
- dcql_query: JSON object (per OpenID4VP 1.0)
- scope: String (optional alternative)
- dcql_query.credentials is an array of credential requests
- Each credential request can have id, format, meta (with vct_values and other DCQL meta fields), and claims.
- Removed permanently: presentation*definition, presentation*definition_uri

**Business Rules (With Audit)**
- All existing Presentation Definition data **must** be migrated to DCQL.
- No endpoint or request generation can include or accept legacy presentation_definition fields.

**Acceptance Criteria (DoD)**

- DCQL Enforcement: API rejects any request body missing dcql_query or containing deprecated legacy query parameters.
- Spec Compliance: Generated Authorization Request JWTs contain the dcql_query parameter and exclude presentation_definition.
- Data Fetching: Fetching a previously stored (and now migrated) request returns a valid DCQL response structure.
- Migration Verification: All historical request definitions in the database have been successfully converted to DCQL; broken/un-mappable records are identified and logged.
- No Backward Compatibility: Integration tests verify that legacy payload submissions return a 400 Bad Request or equivalent validation error.

**Error Handling**
| Code | HTTP | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| dcql_query | 400 | dcql_query is required |
| ambiguous_query | 400 | Both dcql_query and presentationDefinition provided  |
| dcql_validation_error | 400 | DCQL structure invalid |
| dcql_query.credentials| 400 | dcql_query.credentials is required. |
| Credential entry missing id | 400 | Each DCQL credential entry must contain id. |
| Credential entry missing format| 400 | Each DCQL credential entry must contain format. |
| presentation_definition | 400 | presentation_definition is not supported|
| Invalid claims structure | 400 | dcql_query.credentials[].claims must contain valid claim path definitions. |
| dcql_query.credentials empty or not an array| 400 | dcql_query.credentials must be a non-empty array. |

Note - All other attribute validations remain unchanged and continue as per the existing implementation.

title: INJIVER-1317: Handling client_metadata for Pre-registered client_id Scheme as per OpenID4VP spec v1.0
content:
Problem description:
**Purpose**
**As a** Verifier  
**I want to** reject any Authorization Request that includes `client_metadata` when the `client_id` scheme is `pre-registered`,  
**So that** I comply with [OpenID4VP v1.0 Section 8.5](https://openid.net/specs/openid-4-verifiable-presentations-1_0.html#section-8.5-6) which explicitly prohibits `client_metadata` for pre-registered clients, preventing protocol errors and ambiguity.

**Background & Specification Context**

Per **[OpenID4VP v1.0 Section 8.5](https://openid.net/specs/openid-4-verifiable-presentations-1_0.html#section-8.5-6)**, when the `client_id` scheme is `pre-registered`, the Verifier's metadata is already known to the Wallet through prior registration. Therefore:

- `client_metadata` **MUST NOT** be included in an Authorization Request when the scheme is `pre-registered`.
- If `client_metadata` **is** present in such a request, it constitutes a **protocol error** and the request **MUST be rejected**.

For all other `client_id` schemes (e.g.,  `decentralized_identifier`), `client_metadata` **may** be supplied and processed. 

**Current Behavior**

- In our implementation, for the **pre-registered** `client_id` **scheme**, `client_metadata` can still be passed as a query parameter.
- This leads to non-compliance with the spec and creates ambiguity.

**Requirement**

- For **pre-registered** `client_id` **scheme**:
- [ ] If `client_metadata` is included in the Authorization Request (whether directly in the request or as a query parameter), the system *must return an error**.   - invalid_request
- For other schemes (e.g., `client_id`scheme = "decentralized_identifier"):
- [ ] `client_metadata` may be supplied and should be processed accordingly.

**Acceptance Criteria**

1. When `client_id scheme` = pre-registered` and Authorization Request contains `client_metadata`:
- [ ] The request is rejected.
- [ ] An appropriate error response is returned (e.g., `invalid_request`).
2. When `client_id scheme = pre-registered` and no `client_metadata` is present:
- [ ] Request proceeds normally.

**Spike Reference** 
https://mosip.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/Inji/pages/2532114603/Spike+Inji+Verify+OpenID4VP+draft+Version+update+-+draft+23+to+V1.0

**Note**- As per 1.0 specification other changes includes
Renaming `vp_formats` → `vp_formats_supported` - covered as a part of https://github.com/inji/inji-verify/issues/1758
Updating the `did:` → `decentralized_identifier:` prefix - covered as a part of https://github.com/inji/inji-verify/issues/1721

title: INJIVER-1351: Changes in client_metadata as per OpenID4VP spec v1.0
content:
Problem description:
# Update client metadata to use `vp_formats_supported` and align with OpenID4VP v1.0

## Purpose

**As a** Verifier

**I want to** receive `vp_formats_supported` instead of `vp_formats` in client metadata

**So that** I can comply with OpenID4VP v1.0 specification naming conventions and maintain interoperability with v1.0-compliant wallets.

## Description

Update Inji Verify's client metadata response to align with OpenID4VP v1.0 specifications.

The following changes are required:

1. Rename the `vp_formats` field to `vp_formats_supported` in client metadata as defined in OpenID4VP v1.0 Section 5 (Client Metadata).
2. Remove the optional `client_name` field from generated client metadata responses. As per RFC 7591, `client_name` is optional and should not be included unless explicitly required.
3. Use `ldp_vc` instead of `ldp_vp` within `vp_formats_supported` for Linked Data Proof credentials, as defined in OpenID4VP v1.0 Appendix B.1.3.2.3.

These changes affect the Authorization Request response structure and the client metadata passed to wallets.

## Example Response

```json
{
  "response_type": "vp_token",
  "response_mode": "direct_post",
  "response_uri": "https://verifier.example.com/callback",
  "client_id": "verifier-001",
  "client_metadata": {
    "vp_formats_supported": {
      "ldp_vc": {
        "proof_type": ["Ed25519Signature2020"]
      },
      "dc+sd-jwt": {
        "sd-jwt_alg_values": ["ES256", "ES384"],
        "kb-jwt_alg_values": ["ES256", "ES384"]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Authorization Request object returned includes `client_metadata.vp_formats_supported`
- [ ] `client_name` is not included in generated client metadata responses
- [ ] `vp_formats_supported` uses `ldp_vc` as the Linked Data Proof format identifier
- [ ] Field name is consistent across all endpoints returning authorization requests
- [ ] Structure and values within the formats object remain unchanged except for the required field name and format identifier updates

## Backward Compatibility

- [ ] Old `vp_formats` field is NOT included in responses
- [ ] `client_name` is NOT included in responses
- [ ] Responses always follow the OpenID4VP v1.0 format (`vp_formats_supported`)
- [ ] API documentation updated to reference OpenID4VP v1.0 specification naming and examples

## References

- OpenID4VP v1.0 Section 5 - Client Metadata
- OpenID4VP v1.0 Appendix B.1.3.2.3
- RFC 7591 - OAuth 2.0 Dynamic Client Registration Protocol

## Spike Reference

https://mosip.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/Inji/pages/2532114603/Spike+Inji+Verify+OpenID4VP+draft+Version+update+-+draft+23+to+V1.0

title: INJIVER-1360: As a Verifier, I should be able to Upload a Multi-QR file to Verify the VCs with claims mapped to Claim 169
content:
Problem description:
*Title:*
Enable Multi-QR Upload for Claim 169 QR Codes

*User Story*

*As a* user of Inji Verify
*I want* to upload multiple Claim 169 QR codes at once and selectively verify one or more of them
*So that* I can complete specific verification tasks such as age verification, address verification, or identity checks efficiently.

1. *Description*

Users may possess multiple Claim 169 QR codes, each containing different claims. The system should allow bulk uploading of these QR codes and provide a clear interface for selecting which codes to verify based on the required verification purpose. The verification results should be shown separately for each selected QR code.

1. *Acceptance Criteria*

1. *Bulk Upload*
#* The system shall allow users to upload multiple Claim 169 QR codes in one action (camera, gallery, file upload).
#* The system shall parse each uploaded QR and mark valid vs. invalid entries.

1. *QR Code Listing*
#* The system shall display all successfully scanned QR codes in a list with:
#** Unique identifier/label
#** Supported claim types (e.g., age, address)
#** Valid/invalid status

1. *Selection for Verification*
#* The user shall be able to select one or more QR codes for verification.
#* The user shall be able to choose the verification type (age, address, etc.) if applicable.

1. *Verification Process*
#* The system shall verify selected QR codes using Claim 169 decoding rules.
#* The system shall return results for each QR code individually.
#* Results shall include:
#** Verification success/failure
#** Extracted and validated claims
#** Errors (revoked/tampered/unsupported)

1. *Error Handling*
#* The system shall display meaningful messages for invalid or unreadable QR codes.
#* Users shall be able to remove invalid QR codes and reupload.
#* Partial successes (some valid, some invalid) shall still allow the flow to continue.

1. *Performance & UX*
#* The system should handle bulk QR scans without freezing or lagging.
#* The system should provide progress indicators during verification.

1. *Dependencies*

- Claim 169 decoding module

- Multi-file upload or multi-scan feature

- Verification engine updates

1. *Definition of Done*

- All acceptance criteria met

- Unit tests and integration tests added

- UI tested across supported devices

Discussion and resolution:
[Ivanmeneges]: Pragya commented: This will be taken by after MOSIP Connect 2026 i.e. this is not in scope of 0.17.0.

title: INJIVER-1367: Same Device Flow: As a Verifier, I want to be redirected back to Inji Verify after a VC is shared, so that I can seamlessly view the VC verification status.
content:
Problem description:
{color:#36b37e}*User Story:*{color}

{color:#ff991f}*As a* {color}Verifier*,*
{color:#ff991f}*I want to be*{color} redirected back to Inji Verify after a Verifiable Credential (VC) is shared,
{color:#ff991f}*so that*{color}{color:#ff991f} {color}I can seamlessly view the VC verification status.

{color:#36b37e}*Pre-requisites*{color}:

1. The system will have to be connected to internet.

1. This is only for VP Verification - Same device flow

{color:#36b37e}*Problem Statement:*{color}

When a verifier initiates a verification process (for example, by scanning or uploading a VC), for same device flow, the process may involve redirection to an external application or service where the VC is shared or retrieved (e.g., from a wallet, email, or third-party system).

Once the VC sharing is complete, the verifier should automatically be redirected back to the *Inji Verify* interface. On return, the application should automatically trigger the verification process and display the *verification result* (e.g., _Valid_, _Invalid_, _Expired_) along with the credential details in the original design layout.

{color:#36b37e}*Value:* {color}This feature provides a *seamless verification experience* by ensuring that the verifier can complete the process in one continuous flow thereby reducing friction, avoiding rework, and enhancing trust in the verification journey.

{color:#36b37e}*Basic Flow:*{color}

1. *Redirection Flow*
#* After the VC is shared, the verifier is automatically redirected back to the Inji Verify interface.
#* The redirect should retain necessary verification parameters (e.g., session ID, token, or VC reference).

1. *Auto-Verification*
#* On returning to Inji Verify, the system should automatically initiate verification without requiring any human intervention. Verifier should immediately display the VC Verification Result.

1. *Display Verification Result*
#* The verification status should be clearly displayed as one of the following:
#** *Valid* – The VC is authentic and unaltered.
#** *Invalid* – The VC has been tampered with or cannot be verified.
#** *Expired* – The VC has passed its validity period.
#* The credential should appear in its *original visual layout* with the verification result unobtrusively overlaid.

1. *Error Handling*
#* If redirection fails or verification data is missing, the verifier should be shown an error message with an option to retry or re-initiate the process.

1. *Multilingual Support* 
#* The verification result and messages should be displayed in the verifier’s selected language.

Discussion and resolution:

title: INJIVER-1437: OVP for Web Wallet
content:
Problem description:
1. *Title:*

End-to-End OpenID4VP Flow Integration Between Inji Verify and Inji Web Wallet

1. *User Story:*

As a *user undergoing credential verification*, I want to *open the Inji Web Wallet from Inji Verify* to present my verifiable credentials, and once I complete, fail, or cancel the presentation process, I want to be *automatically redirected back to Inji Verify*, so that the entire verification flow feels seamless, unified, and easy to follow without manually switching screens or dealing with technical parameters.

1. *Description:*

In the OpenID4VP verification process, users may prefer or be required to use the *Inji Web Wallet* to present their credentials instead of a mobile wallet. To support this, Inji Verify must provide the ability to initiate the OVP request and open the Inji Web Wallet in a new browser window or tab, passing all required parameters such as `presentation_definition`, `client_id`, `nonce`, `state`, and `redirect_uri`.

Once the user performs any action—successfully presenting credentials, encountering an error, or choosing to cancel—the Inji Web Wallet must automatically send the user back to Inji Verify through the pre-validated `redirect_uri`. The redirect must carry the appropriate OVP response (token, submission, or error) so Inji Verify can interpret the result and display a clear outcome.

This ensures a *smooth end-to-end verification journey*, reducing confusion, eliminating manual navigation, and maintaining strong security and compliance with OpenID4VP standards.

1. *Acceptance Criteria*

1. *Flow Initiation*

- Inji Verify must initiate the verification flow with the correct OVP request parameters.

- Selecting “Present via Inji Web Wallet” must open the Inji Web Wallet in a new tab/window.

- Only trusted, pre-validated redirect URIs may be used.

1. *Credential Presentation*

- Inji Web Wallet must authenticate the user and allow them to select and present credentials.

- OVP protocol rules must be followed throughout the presentation process.

1. *Redirect Back to Inji Verify*

- After the user action (success, failure, cancellation), Inji Web Wallet must redirect back to Inji Verify with the appropriate response:

  - *Success:* `vp_token`, `presentation_submission`, `state`

  - *Failure:* `error`, `error_description`, `state`

  - *Cancelled:* `user_cancelled`, `state`

- Redirect must happen automatically, with no user intervention.

1. *Displaying Results*

- Inji Verify must validate the `state`, parse the response, and show:

  - Verified credentials (on success)

  - Error messages (on failure)

  - Session closure or cancellation messages (if cancelled)

1. *Security & Integrity*

- All redirects must:

  - Use HTTPS

  - Validate `state` to prevent CSRF

  - Ensure no token leakage

  - Comply with OpenID4VP/OIDC redirect best practices

- Only the redirect_uri included in the signed request may be used.

1. *User Experience*

- Navigation between apps must feel smooth, intuitive, and quick (under 2 seconds ideally).

- No blank pages or dead ends should appear.

- The flow must work consistently on desktop/mobile browsers and PWA versions of Inji Verify.

title: INJIVER-1438: Ability to open Web Wallet from Inji Verify to initiate the OpenID4VP Flow
content:
Problem description:
1. *User Story: OVP Flow Integration Between Inji Verify and Inji Web Wallet*

1. *Title:*

Seamless Navigation Between Inji Verify and Inji Web Wallet During the OpenID4VP Flow

1. *User Story:*

As a *Verifier using Inji Verify*, I want the ability to *open the Inji Web Wallet directly from the OVP (OpenID4VP) flow* and later *return to Inji Verify automatically after completing the credential presentation*, so that I can *provide a smooth and uninterrupted verification experience for users*, even when they choose to present credentials through the web wallet instead of the mobile app.

1. *Description:*

In OIDC-based verifiable presentation (OpenID4VP) flows, users may select the Inji Web Wallet as their method for presenting credentials. Currently, this requires manual navigation between verification screens and wallet interfaces, which can lead to user confusion and dropped verification attempts.

This feature enables *two-way navigation*:

1. *From Inji Verify → Inji Web Wallet*
When the verifier triggers a verification request, users can choose to open the Inji Web Wallet in a browser tab or window. Inji Verify should pass the correct OVP request parameters so the user can authenticate and present their VC smoothly.

1. *From Inji Web Wallet → Inji Verify*
After the VC is successfully presented, verified, or if the user cancels the action, the Inji Web Wallet should be able to automatically redirect the user to Inji Verify with:
#* Presentation status
#* Response tokens
#* Error messages (if any)

The goal is to create a *fluid, app-like verification experience* without requiring manual tab switching or URL re-entry.

1. *Acceptance Criteria*

1. *AC01 – Triggering the OVP Flow*

- Given a verifier initiates a verification request in Inji Verify

- When the user selects “Present via Inji Web Wallet”

- Then the system must open the Inji Web Wallet in a new browser tab/window

- And the OVP request (including client_id, presentation_definition, nonce, state, redirect_uri) must be correctly passed to the wallet.

1. *AC02 – Authentication and Credential Selection*

- Given the user is on Inji Web Wallet

- When they authenticate and select credentials

- Then the OVP flow must proceed according to OpenID4VP standards.

1. *AC03 – Redirect Back to Inji Verify*

- Given the user completes or cancels the credential presentation

- When the Inji Web Wallet processes the final OVP response

- Then the user must be redirected back to the Inji Verify redirect_uri with a proper response:

  - *Success:* vp_token, presentation_submission, state

  - *Failure:* error, error_description, state

  - *Cancelled:* user_cancelled=true, state

1. *AC04 – Display of Verification Result*

- When the user is redirected back to Inji Verify

- Then the application must display:

  - Verified credential details (if success)

  - Clear error message (if failure)

  - Session closure message (if cancelled)

1. *AC05 – No Hanging or Blank Screens*

- The redirection should never lead to a blank page

- Proper fallback messaging should appear if the redirect URI is inaccessible or malformed.

1. *AC06 – Security Compliance*

- All redirect flows must comply with OpenID4VP and OIDC redirect security requirements including:

  - Valid state checks

  - Validation of vp_token integrity

  - HTTPS enforcement

  - Prevention of open redirects

  - Protection from token leakage

1. *Non-Functional Requirements*

1. *NFR01 – Performance*

- Opening the Inji Web Wallet must occur in under *2 seconds* on a standard 4G network.

1. *NFR02 – User Experience*

- The user should perceive the navigation as smooth and intuitive, without needing to manually navigate between tabs.

1. *NFR03 – Compatibility*

- Flow must work across:

  - Desktop browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)

  - Mobile browsers

  - Inji Verify running as a PWA

1. *NFR04 – Reliability*

- The redirect back to Inji Verify must work *99% of the time* under normal network conditions.

title: INJIVER-1439: API: Ability to redirect User back from Inji Web to Inji Verify via redirect_uri (with response_code)
content:
Problem description:
1. *User Story: Redirecting the User Back From Inji Web to Inji Verify*

1. *Title:*

Return Navigation from Inji Web Wallet to Inji Verify After Credential Presentation

1. *User Story:*

As a *user presenting credentials through the Inji Web Wallet*, I want the system to *automatically redirect me back to Inji Verify after I complete or cancel my credential presentation*, so that I can *seamlessly return to the verification process without manually navigating or switching tabs*.

1. *Description:*

During the OpenID4VP (OpenID for Verifiable Presentations) flow, the user may choose to present credentials using the Inji Web Wallet. Once the user completes the presentation—whether successfully, unsuccessfully, or by cancelling—the wallet must send the result back to Inji Verify.

This feature ensures that Inji Web can *reliably return the user to the original verification session* by redirecting them to the redirect_uri provided by Inji Verify. The redirect should carry the appropriate response parameters, enabling Inji Verify to resume the flow, display results, handle errors, or close the session gracefully.

This capability is crucial for maintaining a *smooth, intuitive, and secure verification experience*, ensuring users are not left stranded on the wallet page and do not have to manually find Inji Verify again.

1. *Acceptance Criteria*

1. *AC01 – Redirect URI Handling*

- Given Inji Verify initiates an OVP flow

- When Inji Web Wallet receives the request

- Then it must store and trust only the redirect_uri that was part of the signed request (no open redirects).

1. *AC02 – Successful Credential Presentation*

- Given the user completes presenting their credentials in Inji Web Wallet

- When the OVP response is generated

- Then the user must be automatically redirected back to Inji Verify with:

  - `vp_token`

  - `presentation_submission`

  - `state`

1. *AC03 – Failure During Presentation*

- Given the presentation fails due to errors like authentication failure, invalid credentials, or policy mismatch

- When Inji Web constructs the error response

- Then it must redirect the user back to Inji Verify with:

  - `error`

  - `error_description`

  - `state`

1. *AC04 – User Cancelled Flow*

- Given the user chooses to cancel the presentation at any point

- When the wallet exits the flow

- Then it must redirect to Inji Verify with:

  - `user_cancelled=true`

  - `state`

1. *AC05 – No Blank or Dead-End Screens*

- After submission, the user should *never* remain stuck on the Inji Web Wallet page.

- Redirect must initiate automatically without requiring manual clicks.

1. *AC06 – State Validation*

- Upon redirect, Inji Verify must validate:

  - The `state` matches the initial value

  - The response has not been tampered with

  - Tokens comply with expected formats

1. *AC07 – Security Requirements*

- Redirect must:

  - Use HTTPS

  - Prevent token leakage in browser history

  - Avoid query parameters that expose sensitive data

  - Comply with OpenID4VP/OIDC redirect security rules

1. *Non-Functional Requirements*

1. *NFR01 – UX Smoothness*

- The user experience should feel unified, with the transition between Inji Web → Inji Verify taking *less than 2 seconds* on standard connections.

1. *NFR02 – Reliability*

- Redirect must work consistently across:

  - Desktop and mobile browsers

  - PWA versions of Inji Verify

  - Private/incognito modes

1. *NFR03 – Accessibility*

- Even users unfamiliar with multi-tab workflows should perceive the navigation as natural and predictable.

1. *NFR04 – Error Resilience*

- If redirect_uri is unreachable, Inji Web must show a fallback message explaining next steps.

title: INJIVER-1214: OpenID4VP Same Device Flow: Digital Credentials API (DC API) Support
content:
Problem description:
1. *Description:*

Enable seamless, secure interaction between the Verifier and the Wallet operating on the same mobile device and browser session by implementing the OpenID4VP Same Device Flow using the Digital Credentials API (DC API).

This implementation should thereafter support two wallet invocation mechanisms:

- *Digital Credentials API (DC API)*:
*_Default mechanism_* using Chrome’s origin-trial based *native browser-to-wallet invocation*.
_Reference_: [Introducing the Digital Credentials API origin trial ]( Chrome Developers|https://developer.chrome.com/blog/digital-credentials-api-origin-trial#how_the_api_works)

- *Deep Link*:
*_Fallback method_* using custom URI schemes to launch mobile wallets (e.g., `injiwallet://vp-request?...`).

This dual-approach ensures optimal compatibility and progressive enhancement for end-users.

----

1. *Basic Flow:*

Step 1: User clicks “Open Wallet” on the Inji Verify UI (Step 3 in  [INJIVER-526](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/INJIVER-526)).

Step 2: Attempt DC API invocation

1. The system checks if *DC API is supported* in the current browser (e.g., Chrome on Android with origin trial flag).

1. If supported, invoke wallet using: user user _pls provide code snippet_

    ```
    const vp = await navigator.credentials.get({
      web: {
        vp_token: true,
        mediation: 'optional', 
        presentationDefinition: {...}
      }
    });
    
    ```

Step 3: Fallback to Deep Link

- If DC API is unsupported or fails (e.g., user blocks permission),

- Invoke wallet via custom URI:
`injiwallet://vp-request?client_id=...&presentation_definition=...`

This layered approach ensures optimal user experience with progressive enhancement, prioritizing modern standards while maintaining compatibility with existing wallet implementations.

1. *Key Components:*

- *Authorization Request:*

  - Must include: `response_type=vp_token`, `response_mode=fragment`, `client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `nonce`, `state`

  - `presentation_definition`: Required as per PEv2 (Presentation Exchange v2) specification

- *Wallet Invocation:*

  - First attempt via DC API using `navigator.credentials.get`

  - Fallback to deep link invocation if needed

- *Authorization Response:*

  - Wallet returns the VP token via redirect URI (fragment)

  - Inji Verify parses and validates the VP based on:

    - Credential type and format

    - Signature verification

    - Expiry check

    - Issuer trust

1. *Acceptance Criteria:*

- Flow is implemented only for Android devices using Chrome browser (as per current DC API support scope).

- DC API is invoked when available, falling back to deep link if unsupported or fails.

- `navigator.credentials.get()` is used with the appropriate `presentationDefinition`.

- Wallet returns a valid vp_token via redirect URI fragment.

- Inji Verify validates the VP and renders appropriate verification results.

- QR fallback (cross-device flow) remains unchanged.

- User experience follows the design flow specified in INJIVER-526 and [Figma](https://www.figma.com/proto/eIPO4rRq5AZX9eqpby3KQQ/Inji_Verify?page-id=2504%3A5307&node-id=2546-4116&p=f&viewport=194%2C-1816%2C0.29&t=IYOr1zFXBPIPqMXb-1&scaling=scale-down&content-scaling=fixed&starting-point-node-id=2546%3A4116&show-proto-sidebar=1) attached in the same story.

Discussion and resolution:
[Ivanmeneges]: M Vibha Menon commented: [~accountid:62b35d6870d15a142e39bbcc] Please prepare documentation on DC-API & Deeplink, how to add flag etc

[Ivanmeneges]: M Vibha Menon commented: API automation is applicable for this story as confirmed by [~accountid:6213576f6b7e24006a7915ac] .

As confirmed by  [~accountid:6213576f6b7e24006a7915ac] - UI automation is not applicable because redirection between verifier and wallet cannot be achieved

title: INJIVER-1234:  Support Authorization Request via "request_uri" for other client id_scheme (pre-registered, https, x509 etc)
content:
Problem description:
Comments from user 

[https://openid.net/specs/openid-4-verifiable-presentations-1_0.html#section-5.9.3-3.1.1](https://openid.net/specs/openid-4-verifiable-presentations-1_0.html#section-5.9.3-3.1.1|smart-link)
As per specs, we can't have `request_uri` for client-id-scheme `redirect_uri` 

But we will have to support `request_uri` in Authorization Request for `client_id_scheme`: `did, pre_registered and https` from Inji Verify side.

As of now, we are supporting only `request_uri` in Authorization Request for `client_id_scheme: did.`

For now `https` is out of scope. 

But we will have to support `request_uri` in VP request for `client_id_scheme: pre_registered`

- Inji Verify will publish the client meta data with JWKS URL pointing to public key used to sign the `request_uri` JWT.

Inji mobile will also support the `client_id_scheme: pre_registered `and they are working using a Mock for now.

{color:#6554c0}X5C, HTTPS etc. client IDs should be supported{color}

Discussion and resolution:

title: INJIVER-1236: SD-JWT Support for Verifiable Credentials and Presentations
content:
Problem description:
*Goal:* Inji Verify must be able to verify Verifiable Credentials issued in SD‑JWT format and support selective disclosure during presentation in all supported verification modes.

*Description:*

Enhance the *VC Verifier Library* and integrate it with *Inji Verify* to support *end-to-end processing and verification* of SD-JWT-based Verifiable Credentials (VCs), as per [SD-JWT VC IETF draft](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-oauth-sd-jwt-vc/).

Verification includes:

- Parsing the SD-JWT and disclosures

- Verifying the JWT signature using public keys resolved via X.509, DID Documents, or JWT VC Issuer Metadata

- Validating selectively disclosed claims through cryptographic hash comparison

- Optionally verifying Key Binding JWT (KB-JWT) for holder binding

- Validating status (if present)

- Enforcing schema validation (if schema metadata is supplied)

*Purpose:*

To ensure that *Inji Verify* supports secure and privacy-respecting verification of *SD-JWT-based credentials*, enabling:

- Cryptographic assurance of issuer authenticity

- Field-level claim disclosure with integrity protection

- Compatibility with standards-based trust ecosystems

- Verifiability through Inji Verify using Scan / Upload and OpenID4VP- Cross & Same device flow.

*What is SD-JWT VC?*

*SD-JWT (Selective Disclosure JWT)* is a privacy-focused Verifiable Credential format. It allows users to *selectively disclose specific attributes* (like age or nationality) while preserving the *cryptographic integrity* of the credential as a whole.

*Why It's Important?*

- *Field-level Data Sharing* – Disclose only required fields (e.g., age, nationality)

- *Issuer Authenticity* – Signature verification confirms the credential’s origin

- *Tamper Detection* – Hash validation ensures data hasn’t been altered

- *Privacy-first* – Only essential claims are shared

- *Standards-aligned* – Built on IETF specifications

- *Interoperability* – Works across trusted ecosystems like Inji

- *Holder Binding (via KB-JWT)* – Confirms the credential presenter is the rightful holder

1. h3. *Flow Diagram:*

```
+------------------------------+
 | Receive SD-JWT VC & Discl.  |
 +------------------------------+
                |
 +--------------v---------------+
 | Parse JWT, Disclosures, KB-JWT|
 +--------------+---------------+
                |
 +--------------v---------------+
 | Resolve Public Key from iss |
 | (x5c / DID / Issuer Metadata)|
 +--------------+---------------+
                |
 +--------------v---------------+
 | Verify JWT Signature         |
 +--------------+---------------+
                |
 +--------------v---------------+
 | Hash Disclosures & Match _sd |
 +--------------+---------------+
                |
 +--------------v---------------+
 | Verify KB-JWT (if present)   |
 +--------------+---------------+
                |
 +--------------v---------------+
 | Validate Schema (if present) |
 +--------------+---------------+
                |
 +--------------v---------------+
 | Validate status (if present) |
 +--------------+---------------+
                |
 +--------------v---------------+
 |    Return True / False       |
 +------------------------------+

```

title: INJIVER-1281: Support for Key Binding JWT in SD-JWT VC verification in vc-verifier
content:
Problem description:
*Purpose:* As a Verifier, I want to verify SD-JWT based Verifiable Credentials (VCs) with Key Binding JWT (KB-JWT),so that I can ensure the credential actually belongs to the Holder presenting it and prevent credential replay or misuse.

1. Problem Statement

Currently, if a Holder simply forwards an SD-JWT VC string from the Issuer, the Verifier cannot confirm that the credential actually belongs to that Holder. This allows potential replay or misuse by unauthorized parties.

1. Solution / Feature

Introduce Key Binding JWT (KB-JWT) verification into Inji Verify.

- A KB-JWT is signed by the Holder’s private key and sent along with the SD-JWT + Disclosures during credential presentation.

- This proves that the entity presenting the credential controls the private key bound to the VC (cnf.jwk claim).

1. Preconditions

- Issuer issues an SD-JWT VC with a cnf claim containing the Holder’s public key (JWK).

- Holder has a valid private key corresponding to the cnf.jwk.

- Verifier is integrated with Inji Verify SDK supporting SD-JWT and KB-JWT verification.

1. Basic Flow

1. Issuance (Issuer → Holder)
#* Issuer issues SD-JWT + disclosures.
#* SD-JWT payload includes cnf.jwk binding the credential to Holder’s public key.

1. Presentation (Holder → Verifier)
#* Holder chooses disclosures to share.
#* Holder creates KB-JWT signed with their private key (corresponding to cnf.jwk).
#* Holder sends:
#** vp_token = <SD-JWT> ~ <Disclosure1> ~ <Disclosure2> ...
#** kb_jwt = <Holder-signed KB-JWT>

1. Verification (Verifier)
#* Validate Issuer’s SD-JWT signature.
#* Verify disclosures against _sd digests in SD-JWT.
#* Validate KB-JWT signature using cnf.jwk from SD-JWT.
#* Check aud matches Verifier and nonce matches challenge.
#* If successful, accept VC as authentic and bound to the Holder.

1. Alternate Flow / Error Handling

- If SD-JWT signature is invalid → Display “Credential verification failed: Invalid Issuer signature.”

- If disclosures do not match _sd digests → Display “Credential verification failed: Disclosure mismatch.”

- If KB-JWT signature validation fails → Display “Credential does not belong to the Holder.”

- If aud claim in KB-JWT does not match Verifier or nonce is invalid → Display “Credential presentation is invalid or replayed.”

1. Scenarios

1. Happy Path: Valid SD-JWT, valid disclosures, valid KB-JWT → VC is successfully verified.

1. Stolen Credential Attempt: Attacker presents SD-JWT + disclosures without valid KB-JWT → Verification fails.

1. Replay Attack Attempt: Attacker replays old KB-JWT with mismatched nonce → Verification fails.

1. Expired Credential: VC has expired → Verification fails with expiry message.

1. Acceptance Criteria

- Inji Verify must support parsing and verification of SD-JWT VCs with KB-JWT.

- Verifier must validate:

  - Issuer’s SD-JWT signature.

  - Disclosures against _sd digests.

  - KB-JWT signature using the cnf.jwk.

  - KB-JWT claims: aud (Verifier endpoint) and nonce (anti-replay).

- If verification fails, clear reason codes should be displayed to the Verifier.

- Logs should capture verification steps for debugging and audit.

- Feature should be tested with multiple disclosure scenarios (partial and full).

- Must handle expiry (exp) in SD-JWT correctly.

- UI should reflect success/failure clearly for Verifier.

1.

Discussion and resolution:
[Ivanmeneges]: **Jira Assignee:** M Vibha Menon (no GitHub mapping found)

[Ivanmeneges]: M Vibha Menon commented: h3\. Problem

If a Holder simply forwards an SD-JWT VC from the Issuer, the Verifier has *no proof that the credential actually belongs to that Holder*. Someone else who gets the string could reuse it.

h3\. Solution: Key Binding JWT

* A *Key Binding JWT* is a *separate JWT signed by the Holder’s private key*.
* It is sent _along with_ the *SD-JWT + Disclosures string* when the Holder presents the credential.
* This proves that the entity presenting the VC *possesses the key bound to the VC* (i.e., "this credential is mine").

h3\. Presentation Package

When the Holder sends the VC to the Verifier:

{noformat}vp_token = "<sd-jwt>
 ~
 <disclosure1>
  ~
  <disclosure2>
   ..." kb_jwt = "
   <holder-signed key binding jwt>
    "{noformat} h3\. Verifier checks # Validate *Issuer’s signature* on the SD-JWT. # Validate *disclosures* match {{_sd}} digests. # Validate *Holder’s KB-JWT signature* using the {{cnf.jwk}}. # Ensure that the KB-JWT proves possession of the key bound to the SD-JWT. h3\. *SD-JWT example with KB-JWT:* {noformat}eyJ0eXAiOiJzZCtqd3QiLCJhbGciOiJFUzI1NiJ9 # SD-JWT Header .eyJpZCI6IjEyMzQiLCJfc2QiOlsiYkRUUnZ....
    <payload>
     #SD-JWT Payload .n27NCtnuwytlBYt...
     <signature>
      #SD-JWT signature ~WyI1ZWI4Yzg2MjM0MDJjZjJlIiwiZmlyc3RuYW1lIiwiSm9obiJd # Disclosure 1 ~WyJjNWMzMWY2ZWYzNTg4MWJjIiwibGFzdG5hbWUiLCJEb2UiXQ # Disclosure 2 ~WyJmYTlkYTUzZWJjOTk3OThlIiwic3NuIiwiMTIzLTQ1LTY3ODkiXQ # Disclosure 3 ~eyJ0eXAiOiJzZCtqd3QiLCJhbGciOiJFUzI1NiJ9 #KB-JWT Header .eyJpZCI6IjEyMzQiLCJfc2QiOlsiYkRUUnZ....
      <payload>
       #KB-JWT Payload .n27NCtnuwytlBYt...<signature>#KB-JWT signature{noformat} h2\. How the Key Binding JWT (KB-JWT) proves the Holder is the rightful subject of the SD-JWT? h3\. 1\. Binding the VC to a Key at Issuance When the *Issuer issues an SD-JWT VC*, it includes a {{cnf}} *(confirmation) claim* in the payload. This {{cnf}} contains the Holder’s *public key* (or reference to it). Example SD-JWT payload snippet: {noformat}{ "iss": "https://university.example", "iat": 1690000000, "exp": 1720000000, "_sd": ["hashOfName", "hashOfDegree"], "cnf": { "jwk": { "kty": "EC", "crv": "P-256", "x": "....", "y": "...." } } } {noformat} 👉 This says: _“This credential belongs to whoever controls the private key for this JWK.”_ h3\. 2\. Presentation with Key Binding JWT When the Holder presents the VC, they must also send a *KB-JWT*: {noformat}{ "aud": "https://verifier.example.com", "iat": 1691000000, "nonce": "abc123", "cnf": { "jwk": { "kty": "EC", "crv": "P-256", "x": "....", "y": "...." } } } {noformat} * This KB-JWT is signed with the *private key matching the* {{cnf.jwk}}. * The {{aud}} + {{nonce}} protect against replay. h3\. 3\. Verifier’s Checks The Verifier: # *Validates Issuer’s SD-JWT signature* (issuer trusted). # *Reads the* {{cnf.jwk}} from the SD-JWT. # *Validates KB-JWT signature* using that {{cnf.jwk}}. #* If the signature verifies, it proves the presenter owns the private key bound to the VC. # Ensures the KB-JWT’s {{aud}} matches itself and {{nonce}} matches the challenge. h3\. ✅ Result * Even if someone *steals the SD-JWT string + disclosures*, * They *cannot generate a valid KB-JWT* without the Holder’s private key. That’s what makes SD-JWT *phishing-resistant and bound to the Holder’s key*. ---- h1\. {color:#4c9aff}SD JWT with KB JWT Full Flow{color} # *Issuance phase (Issuer → Holder):* #* Issuer creates *SD-JWT* (signed with Issuer’s private key). #* Includes {{cnf}} claim → binding the VC to Holder’s public key. #* Provides *disclosures* alongside SD-JWT. #* ✅ No KB-JWT here — only SD-JWT + disclosures. # *Presentation phase (Holder → Verifier):* #* Holder selects which disclosures to reveal. #* Holder creates *KB-JWT* (signed with Holder’s private key). #* Sends *SD-JWT + disclosures + KB-JWT* to Verifier. # *Verification phase (Verifier):* #* Checks Issuer’s signature (SD-JWT). #* Validates disclosures against {{_sd}} hashes. #* Validates Holder’s key binding (SD-JWT {{cnf}} vs KB-JWT signature). #* Accepts/rejects VC.</signature>
      </payload>
     </signature>
    </payload>
   </holder-signed>
  </disclosure2>
 </disclosure1>
</sd-jwt>

[Ivanmeneges]: Mayura Deshmukh commented: [~accountid:712020:5a1aca27-bb82-4507-99ee-c8ab6211b59f] 

As discussed with [~accountid:557058:694ce5f1-ed1b-41f7-a96a-879cb8a7e6c6]  in Engg Review Call on 9th Sept 2025, we will take this KB JWT verification in next release and not in 0.15.0.

Pls update fix version and sprint.

[Ivanmeneges]: Mayura Deshmukh commented: Updates from [~accountid:557058:cc7f3f06-5f70-4e7e-a2e3-4de09e09e29b] 

Okay, we can consider KBT out of scope for 1.5.0 of vc-verifier - basic we will add like validation and signature verification in vc-verifier
but other things would be handled at verifier like

# If Key Binding is required and the Holder has provided an SD-JWT (without Key Binding), the Verifier MUST reject the presentation.
# Determine that the Key Binding JWT is bound to the current transaction and was created for this Verifier (replay detection) by validating nonce and aud claims.

Spec Reference [https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-oauth-selective-disclosure-jwt-22.html#name-verification-by-the-verifie|https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-oauth-selective-disclosure-jwt-22.html#name-verification-by-the-verifie|smart-link]  

[http://ietf.org|http://ietf.org|smart-link] 

[*Selective Disclosure for JWTs (SD-JWT)*|https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-oauth-selective-disclosure-jwt-22.html#name-verification-by-the-verifie]

This specification defines a mechanism for the selective disclosure of individual elements of a JSON data structure used as the payload of a JSON Web Signature (JWS).
The primary use case is the selective disclosure of JSON Web Token (JWT) claims.

title: INJIVER-1287: Inji Verify | Performance Testing
content:
Problem description:
{color:#36b37e}*Epic Title*{color}*:* Performance Testing for Inji Verify

{color:#36b37e}*Epic Description*{color}*:*
To ensure that Inji Verify can reliably handle real-world usage at scale, we need to conduct comprehensive performance testing across various scenarios. This epic covers the planning, execution, and analysis of performance tests to validate system stability, responsiveness, and scalability. The focus will be on measuring throughput, response times, error rates, and resource utilization under different load conditions, including peak traffic and stress scenarios.

The outcome of this epic will provide clear benchmarks for expected performance, identify bottlenecks, and recommend optimizations to improve efficiency and user experience. This will help ensure that Inji Verify can seamlessly support a large number of concurrent verifications without degradation in service quality.

{color:#36b37e}*Goals*{color}*:*

- Validate that Inji Verify meets defined performance SLAs (latency, throughput, error tolerance).

- Identify system bottlenecks under load, stress, and endurance conditions.

- Provide recommendations for optimization and scaling strategies.

- Build repeatable test scripts and baselines for future performance testing cycles.

{color:#36b37e}*Success Criteria*{color}*:*

- System handles expected peak load without critical failures.

- Response times remain within defined thresholds under normal and peak usage.

- Performance test reports are documented and shared with stakeholders.

- Optimization backlog items (if any) are clearly defined.

Discussion and resolution:

title: INJIVER-1288: OpenID4VP: Open playstore if wallet is unavailable
content:
Problem description:
1. *User Story: Open Play Store if Wallet is Unavailable (OpenID4VP Flow)*

*Title:* Redirect user to Play Store when wallet app is not installed during OpenID4VP flow

*As a* user attempting to complete an OpenID4VP verification flow
*I want* to be redirected to the Play Store if the required wallet application is not installed
*So that* I can download the wallet and continue the verification process without confusion or flow breakage.

----

1. *Description*

During the OpenID4VP flow, when the system attempts to invoke the wallet application via deep link or app scheme, it should first check whether the wallet app is installed on the device.

If the wallet is unavailable:

- The user should be redirected to the wallet’s listing on the *Play Store*.

- The experience should be seamless and user-friendly.

- Clear messaging should inform the user why the redirection is happening.

----

|`wallet_unavailable`:|-Wallet could not be launched. Please ensure it is installed and try again-. [https://www.figma.com/proto/eIPO4rRq5AZX9eqpby3KQQ/Inji_Verify?page-id=2504%3A5307&node-id=2971-4646&p=f&viewport=194%2C-1816%2C0.29&t=IYOr1zFXBPIPqMXb-1&scaling=scale-down&content-scaling=fixed&starting-point-node-id=2971%3A4646&show-proto-sidebar=1](https://www.figma.com/proto/eIPO4rRq5AZX9eqpby3KQQ/Inji_Verify?page-id=2504%3A5307&node-id=2971-4646&p=f&viewport=194%2C-1816%2C0.29&t=IYOr1zFXBPIPqMXb-1&scaling=scale-down&content-scaling=fixed&starting-point-node-id=2971%3A4646&show-proto-sidebar=1|smart-link) (NA)

- DC API → if wallet not present, we fallback to deeplink. So this won’t trigger.

- Deeplink → if wallet not there, we use Deferred Deep Linking *so it opens the Play store/App store.*
 |

{color:#6554c0}Deeplink: Same device flow{color}

{color:#6554c0}If no supported wallet is available, take the user to playstore.{color}

1. *Acceptance Criteria*

1. *Wallet Detection*
#* System checks if the wallet app is installed before invoking the deep link.
#* Detection works reliably across supported Android versions.

1. *Redirection Behavior*
#* If wallet is not installed:
#** User is redirected to the wallet’s Play Store page.
#** Redirection opens directly in the Play Store app (preferred) or browser fallback.
#* If wallet is installed:
#** OpenID4VP deep link invocation proceeds normally.

1. *User Messaging*
#* UI displays a clear message such as:
“Wallet app not found. Please install the wallet to continue.”
#* Messaging should not expose technical details.

1. *Post-Installation Flow*
#* User can restart or resume the OpenID4VP flow after installation.
#* Clear instructions provided to re-initiate the verification request.

1. *Error Handling*
#* If Play Store cannot be opened, a fallback web URL should be triggered.
#* Proper logging should capture wallet-unavailable scenarios.

1. *Security*
#* Only approved wallet package IDs are allowed.
#* Prevent redirection to unauthorized or malicious apps.

----

1. *Non-Functional Requirements*

- Redirection should occur within acceptable UX latency.

- Solution should be scalable for supporting multiple wallet apps in the future.

- No sensitive transaction data should be exposed during redirection.
