title: INJICERT-1323: <Feature>Enable Inji Certify to Support Multiple SVG Templates for Multi-language and Front/Back Credential Formats
content:
Problem description:
As a credential issuer using **Inji Certify**, I want Certify to support multiple SVG template formats,
So that I can generate credentials in different languages and support separate front and back layouts of the credential.

### **Description:**

Currently, Inji Certify supports a single SVG template for credential rendering. To support multilingual deployments and enhanced visual presentation (such as front and back sides of a credential), Certify should allow configuration and selection of multiple SVG templates per credential type.

This feature should enable:

** Support for multiple SVG templates mapped to:
**** Different languages (e.g., English, French, Arabic, etc.)
**** Front side and back side layouts of a credential
** Dynamic template selection during credential generation
** Rendering of language-specific static labels
** Rendering of both front and back sides as separate SVG outputs (or combined, based on configuration)

This enhancement will improve usability for country implementations and align with multilingual and design flexibility requirements.

### **Acceptance Criteria:**

1. System allows configuration of multiple SVG templates per credential type.
1. SVG templates can be mapped to:
#** Language
#** Credential side (Front / Back)
1. During credential issuance:
#** Correct SVG template is selected based on language preference.
#** Both front and back SVGs are generated where applicable.
1. Static labels in SVG reflect the selected language.
1. If no language-specific template is available, system falls back to default template.
1. Backward compatibility is maintained for existing single-template credentials.

### **Alternate Flows:**

**AF1 – Language Not Available**

** If requested language template is not configured,
** System defaults to primary language SVG template.

**AF2 – Back Side Not Configured**

** If back-side template is not configured,
** System generates only the front-side SVG without failure.

**AF3 – Invalid SVG Template**

** If configured SVG template is malformed or invalid,
** Credential issuance fails with appropriate error message.

### Reference:

[https://mosip.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/Inji/pages/1430880599/SVG+Design+to+Template+Conversion?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNTQ5ZGI2YzRjZDE0NDQ4N2FhYTljYjI5MmM5Y2Q2M2YiLCJwIjoiY29uZmx1ZW5jZS1jaGF0cy1pbnQifQ](https://mosip.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/Inji/pages/1430880599/SVG+Design+to+Template+Conversion?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNTQ5ZGI2YzRjZDE0NDQ4N2FhYTljYjI5MmM5Y2Q2M2YiLCJwIjoiY29uZmx1ZW5jZS1jaGF0cy1pbnQifQ|smart-link)

title: INJICERT-1264: SVG Template – Face Image & Label attribute path mismatch issues
content:
Problem description:
The SVG rendering template currently has mismatched data paths for both *labels* and *images* when rendering Verifiable Credentials (VCs)


# Label Mismatch

```
<text><tspan>{{/credential_definition/credentialSubject/address/display/0/name}}</tspan></text>
```

However, the Verifiable Credential (VC) does not contain label fields in this structure — only the value structure ({{{{/credentialSubject/...}}}}) matches correctly.

As a result, the label placeholders ({{/credential_definition/.../display/.../name}}) are not being rendered properly in the generated SVG output.

*Current Behavior:*
Labels are defined as JSON Pointers referencing {{/credential_definition/.../display/.../name}}, which do not exist in the VC payload, causing them to appear blank in the rendered template.

*Expected Behavior:*
Labels should be static text elements directly written in the SVG (e.g., “Full Name”, “Date of Birth”, etc.), and only values should use placeholders matching VC paths.


```
<text><tspan>{{/credential_definition/credentialSubject/address/display/0/name}}</tspan></text>
<text><tspan>{{/credentialSubject/address/state}}</tspan></text>
```

```
<text><tspan>Address</tspan></text>
<text><tspan>{{/credentialSubject/address/state}}</tspan></text>
```

h3. *2. Image Mismatch*

h3. 

The template is currently configured to expect a QR code image as:

```
<image id="qrCodeImage" x="194.885" y="64.1274" width="93.2308" height="93.2308" preserveAspectRatio="none" xlink:href="{{/qrCodeImage}}"/>
```

h3. 

However, the VC provides a *face image* under:

```
<image id="image2_828_1898" x="15" y="59" width="70" height="99.2405" preserveAspectRatio="none" xlink:href="{{/credentialSubject/face}}"/>
```

h3. *Issue:*

The current template is rendering an empty QR code section since {{{{/qrCodeImage}}}} does not exist in the VC.
The expected binding should use {{{{/credentialSubject/face}}}} instead.

h4. *Expected Behavior:*

The {{<image>}} element should be updated to use the correct binding path and positioning if required.

*Proposed Fix:*

* Update the SVG template to replace dynamic label placeholders ({{{{/credential_definition/...}}}}) with static label text.
* Keep value bindings as per the VC structure (e.g., {{{{/credentialSubject/fieldName}}}}).
* Ensure all labels (like “Full Name”, “Farmer ID”, “Gender”, “Date of Birth”, “Phone Number”, etc.) match the new example format.

```
<image id="image2_828_1898" x="15" y="59" width="70" height="99.2405" preserveAspectRatio="none" xlink:href="{{/credentialSubject/face}}"/>
```

*Reference (Expected SVG Example):*


```
<text><tspan>Full Name</tspan></text>
<text><tspan>{{/credentialSubject/fullName}}</tspan></text>
<text><tspan>Farmer ID</tspan></text>
<text><tspan>{{/credentialSubject/farmerId}}</tspan></text>
<text><tspan>Gender</tspan></text>
<text><tspan>{{/credentialSubject/gender}}</tspan></text>
<text><tspan>Date of Birth</tspan></text>
<text><tspan>{{/credentialSubject/dateOfBirth}}</tspan></text>
<text><tspan>Phone Number</tspan></text>
<text><tspan>{{/credentialSubject/phoneNumber}}</tspan></text>
```

### Attachments
- [Screenshot 2025-11-11 113401.png](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/INJICERT-1264) (no direct link)
- [svg-template-vc.PNG](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/INJICERT-1264) (no direct link)

title: INJICERT-1157: INJICERT- Issues in sunbird usecase
content:
Problem description:
Issues in sunbird usecase 

1. VC fetch is failing from injiweb post latest image movement (DB scripts upgrade) `Invalid request: first item in type is not VerifiableCredential"`
1. After adding VC type from credential Config API, we still have to update git properties with new VC type in [https://github.com/mosip/inji-config/blob/release-0.10.x/certify-sunbird-insurance.properties#L14](https://github.com/mosip/inji-config/blob/release-0.10.x/certify-sunbird-insurance.properties#L14|smart-link) 
1. **Query** - Since the Sunbird plugin supports only Ed25519 signatures, using the Credential Configuration API to add VC types with different signature algorithms (e.g., RSA or ES256) has no practical effect.  Therefore, any VC type added via the API must align with the different `signature*crypto*suite` value other than ed25519, will fetch VC with proof ed25519signature only

### Attachments
- [sunbird-insurance-inji-certify-b86b7b9cc-ql6fb_inji-certify.log](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/INJICERT-1157) (no direct link)

[Ivanmeneges]: Piyush Shukla commented: Sunbird is currently used in VCIssuance plugin  mode, so it will not use the signature_crypto_suite added in credential_config table. Hence, it is getting signed by Ed25519 signature only

[Ivanmeneges]: Piyush Shukla commented: For point number 2, comma separated list of supported vc types is defined for sunbird plugin as a config property. This is an additional property where based on the values in this config, velocityTemplate is also fetched. Thats why this property is still used.

title: INJICERT-904: nonce Should Be Optional in Verifiable Credential Issuance
content:
Problem description:
*Description:*

* The {{nonce}} claim is currently marked as mandatory in the code, but the OpenID4VCI specification states that it should be optional.

*Impact:*

* Strict enforcement of {{nonce}} may cause interoperability issues with other implementations that treat it as optional.

*Resolution:*

* Update the implementation to make {{nonce}} an optional claim.

Discussion and resolution:
[Ivanmeneges]: Harsh Vardhan commented: This can be de-prioritised as discussed
cc [~accountid:60c378aa946928007023eb9a]

[Ivanmeneges]: varaniya commented: Will reconfirm with the spec and assign to the team

[Ivanmeneges]: varaniya commented: [~accountid:640192f9c6e77744a1dd7bd3] [~accountid:6108f61fae72b2006f50e6af] can you confirm whether it is optional or not? 
Will reprioritze post the confirmation

[Ivanmeneges]: Likhitha R L commented: [~accountid:712020:a354eedc-e17e-400c-b961-a8a3f716ad4f] nonce is mandatory in our code,

[Ivanmeneges]: Swati Goel commented: Analysis:

Exception should not be thrown from here [https://github.com/inji/inji-certify/blob/master/certify-service/src/main/java/io/mosip/certify/utils/VCIssuanceUtil.java#L177-L185|https://github.com/inji/inji-certify/blob/master/certify-service/src/main/java/io/mosip/certify/utils/VCIssuanceUtil.java#L177-L185|smart-link] 

Rather return cNonce and CNonce expiry from here.

After that while validating cNonce [https://github.com/inji/inji-certify/blob/master/certify-service/src/main/java/io/mosip/certify/proof/JwtProofValidator.java#L74|https://github.com/inji/inji-certify/blob/master/certify-service/src/main/java/io/mosip/certify/proof/JwtProofValidator.java#L74|smart-link] nonce validation should be happened as per below step

# Get cNonce and cNonce expiry from parsedAccessToken cached in Certify
# Get nonce from proof jwt
# Add logic
## If parsedAccessToken has cNonce 
### compare nonce of parsedAccessToken and proof jwt.
#### Both should be same
#### if not same then throw error
## If parsedAccessToken doesn’t have cNonce - it means auth server has not provided cNonce
### if proof jwt has nonce then throw the error
# Remove logic about mandatory check of having cNonce in parsedAccessToken as it’s not mandatory.

labels: bug, injicertify_0.13.x_release_testing, inji_certify_release_0.12.x_testing, inji_certify_sprint18_2025, known_issue_0.12.0, inji_certify_sprint8_2026_spillover
content:
Problem description:
Dependency on {{didUrl}} is still present — a mismatch between {{didUrl}} in git properties and database can cause VC verification failure, as the {{v1/certify/.well-known/did.json}} API relies on {{didUrl}} from git properties.

But in VC verification method allies kid value with did url from DB  

### Attachments
- image-20251106-072443.png (no link available)
- response.json (no link available)
- response VC.json (no link available)

Discussion and resolution:
[Ivanmeneges]: **Jira Assignee:** varaniya (no GitHub mapping found)

[Ivanmeneges]: varaniya commented: [~accountid:6108f61fae72b2006f50e6af] as discussed, this information will be called out in the release notes as “while VC type is getting configured, please make sure the value of didUrl in config file and value sent through API is the same else VC issuance will be failed“

Hence reducing the severity of the bug

[Ivanmeneges]: varaniya commented: Current process is that didUrl is mentioned in both API and Configuration to be configured by the issuer and the limitation as of today is that, in both places you need to mention the same value else VC download gets failed.

[~accountid:5f9ae4c7c824730070268e86] can we prioritze here for the system to pick the value from API and if it is not present then system can check on config, this way we can make this truly configurable without any dependency

[Ivanmeneges]: varaniya commented: as per the discussion with [~accountid:5f9ae4c7c824730070268e86] , the validation logic to check the value to be same in both API and Configuration need to be removed.

[Ivanmeneges]: Piyush Shukla commented: This behaviour is expected. 
1. Certify service will host the did document based on the config property provided. 
2. If didUrl in VC type is different from  the issuer's didUrl (i.e. certify), then the DID document from did.json endpoint can be copied  and hosted to the credential_config(VC type) did url.
3. In point no 2, the referenced did urls in the doc has to be replaced with the correct url.

[Ivanmeneges]: Likhitha R L commented: Issue still existing, VC verification fails even on following the below steps 

!image-20251106-072443.png|width=479,alt="image-20251106-072443.png"!

[^response.json]

Reopening the ticket, tested in [qa-inji1.mosip.net|http://qa-inji1.mosip.net]

title: INJICERT-1264: SVG Template – Face Image & Label attribute path mismatch issues
content:
Problem description:
The SVG rendering template currently has mismatched data paths for both *labels* and *images* when rendering Verifiable Credentials (VCs).


# Label Mismatch

{noformat}<text><tspan>{{/credential_definition/credentialSubject/address/display/0/name}}</tspan></text>{noformat}

However, the Verifiable Credential (VC) does not contain label fields in this structure — only the value structure ({{{{/credentialSubject/...}}}}) matches correctly.

As a result, the label placeholders ({{/credential_definition/.../display/.../name}}) are not being rendered properly in the generated SVG output.

*Current Behavior:*
Labels are defined as JSON Pointers referencing {{/credential_definition/.../display/.../name}}, which do not exist in the VC payload, causing them to appear blank in the rendered template.

*Expected Behavior:*
Labels should be static text elements directly written in the SVG (e.g., “Full Name”, “Date of Birth”, etc.), and only values should use placeholders matching VC paths.

content:
Problem description:
upload ca cert for ecck1 signalgo is failing

Steps used to generate CA cert

# openssl ecparam -name secp256k1 -genkey -noout -out ca_ecck1.key
# openssl ec -in ca_ecck1.key -pubout -out ca_ecck1.pub
# openssl req -new -x509 -days 3650 -key ca_ecck1.key -out ca_ecck1.crt
# openssl x509 -req -in ecc.csr -CA ca_ecck1.crt -CAkey ca_ecck1.key -CAcreateserial -out server_signed_ecck1.crt -days 730

Getting error {
      "errorCode": "unknown_error",
      "errorMessage": "KER-PCM-005 --\u003e Root CA Certificate not found."
    }





### Attachments
- ECCK1CA-ca.p12 (no link available)

Discussion and resolution:
[Ivanmeneges]: **Jira Assignee:** Sakshi Jhanwar (no GitHub mapping found)

[Ivanmeneges]: Sakshi Jhanwar commented: The K1 Root CA upload is failing because the service’s self‑signed validation uses X509Certificate.verify(), which defaults to the SunEC provider. SunEC does not support secp256k1, so the verify step fails and the K1 root is treated as a Sub‑CA, resulting in KER‑PCM‑005.
I added BouncyCastle, updated the ECDSA allow‑list (SHA256withECDSA), and re‑issued the K1 Root CA.
BC loads correctly at startup, but at runtime the provider order changes, pushing BC to the end and causing verify() to fall back to SunEC again. Because of this provider reordering, the K1 Root CA verification still fails even though BC is available.

title: INJICERT-1274: license compliance issue-- hibernate core
content:
Problem description:
Hibernate follows a dual-licensing policy where all legacy Hibernate components are licensed under LGPL, while the latest Hibernate ORM versions are licensed under Apache 2.0.

In Certify, we are currently using:

* *Hibernate Commons Annotations 6.0.6.Final*
* *Hibernate Core / ORM 6.4.4.Final*
* *Hibernate HikariCP Integration 6.4.4.Final*

All of these fall under the legacy Hibernate line and are therefore licensed under *LGPL*, which is not allowed under MOSIP’s licensing policy.

We recommend upgrading to *Hibernate ORM 7.x (or later)* because it is licensed under *Apache 2.0*, aligns with MOSIP’s compliance requirements, includes recent *security fixes*, and is part of the actively maintained and stable release line.

{{PS256}}, {{RS256}} and {{ES256}}

title: INJICERT-1290: INJICERT-CSR Certificate Upload via Automation Causes DID kid Mismatch and VC Verification Failures
content:
Problem description:
Uploading CSR certificates through Certify automation dynamically updates signing keys, which changes the {{kid}} in {{did.json}}.
However, {{did.json}} is *not updated at runtime*, causing a mismatch for dependent modules.

As a result, *Mobile and Web applications face VC verification and download failures* due to outdated {{kid}} values.

Currently, the only workaround is a *manual update of* {{did.json}} *on a daily basis*. If this update is missed, Mobile and Web teams are blocked from downloading and verifying VCs, making the process error-prone and operationally inefficient.

Discussion and resolution:
[Ivanmeneges]: **Jira Assignee:** varaniya (no GitHub mapping found)

Discussion and resolution:
[Ivanmeneges]: varaniya commented: [~accountid:6108f61fae72b2006f50e6af] as discussed please re test this bug

[Ivanmeneges]: Likhitha R L commented: We have the issue in dev-int-inji and qa-inji1 env also [~accountid:712020:a354eedc-e17e-400c-b961-a8a3f716ad4f] . Attached report for reference [^mosip-api-internal.dev-int-inji-injicertify-landregistry-2026-03-10_04-51-full-report_T-622_P-324_S-0_F-2_I-279_KI-17.html] [^mosip-api-internal.qa-inji1-injicertify-landregistry-2026-03-10_02-51-full-report_T-622_P-319_S-0_F-7_I-279_KI-17.html]

[Ivanmeneges]: Swati Goel commented: [~accountid:6108f61fae72b2006f50e6af] [~accountid:61891f6751e8750072e60a3a] I have checked the attached logs and found the cause.

Reason is 

{"@timestamp":"2026-03-02T03:46:43.412Z","@version":"1","message":"Error occurred during canonicalization.","logger_name":"io.mosip.certify.utils.CredentialUtils","thread_name":"http-nio-8090-exec-10","level":"ERROR","level_value":40000,"stack_trace":"foundation.identity.jsonld.JsonLDException: There was a problem encountered loading a remote context [[https://www.w3.org/2018/credentials/v1]\\n\\tat|https://www.w3.org/2018/credentials/v1%5D%5C%5Cn%5C%5Ctat] foundation.identity.jsonld.JsonLDObject.normalize(JsonLDObject.java:396)\n\tat foundation.identity.jsonld.JsonLDObject.normalize(JsonLDObject.java:404)\n\tat info.weboftrust.ldsignatures.canonicalizer.URDNA2015Canonicalizer.canonicalize(URDNA2015Canonicalizer.java:41)\n\tat io.mosip.certify.utils.CredentialUtils.generateLdProof(CredentialUtils.java:62)\n\tat io.mosip.certify.credential.W3CJsonLD.addProof(W3CJsonLD.java:124)\n\tat io.mosip.certify.services.CertifyIssuanceServiceImpl.getVerifiableCredential(CertifyIssuanceServiceImpl.java:302)\n\tat io.mosip.certify.services.CertifyIssuanceServiceImpl.getCredential(CertifyIssuanceServiceImpl.java:178)\n\tat io.mosip.certify.controller.VCIssuanceController.getCredentialV12Draft(VCIssuanceController.java:59)\n\tat 



As we haven’t implemented context caching right now, so it might happen that context api has reached api rate limit hence there was error to load the context.

Actual error is {{Error occurred during canonicalization}} due to context loading.

Any error thrown with exception {{CertifyException}} in method {{getVerifiableCredential}} is propagated as {{ERROR_SIGNING_QR_DATA}}. This is not correct.

[https://github.com/inji/inji-certify/blob/release-0.14.x/certify-service/src/main/java/io/mosip/certify/services/CertifyIssuanceServiceImpl.java#L312-L315|https://github.com/inji/inji-certify/blob/release-0.14.x/certify-service/src/main/java/io/mosip/certify/services/CertifyIssuanceServiceImpl.java#L312-L315|smart-link] 

We will have to fix this error code here.

Let us know if we want to take this as known issue or want to fix error code.

[Ivanmeneges]: varaniya commented: As discussed, this is an interim issue which also will be resolved with the fix on cache. we will be prioritising the same in 0.15.0 hence reducing the severity as well

[swatigoel]: This issue has been fixed by handling proper error.

title: Enhancement of Credential Issuance Endpoint to Support OpenID4VCI 1.0 Features
content:
Problem description:
### Purpose:
As an issuer system, I want to enhance the credential issuance endpoint to support updated validation mechanisms, improved error handling, and multiple credential responses, so that the system complies with OpenID4VCI 1.0 specification.

### Pre-requisites:
- Credential issuance endpoint is already implemented.
- Proof JWT validation mechanism exists.
- Redis or equivalent cache is available for nonce validation.
- SD-JWT generation capability is available.

### Key Constraints
- credential_configuration_id Field — Mandatory
- format field must NOT be accepted in the request payload. Any request containing the format field must be rejected with an invalid_request error.
- The proofs.jwt field must always be an array. A single proof JWT is valid when provided as a one-element array. Passing a proof JWT as a bare string outside the array structure is not valid

### Basic flow:
- Client sends a credential request to the issuance endpoint.
- System validates that credential_configuration_id  is present
- System validates that the request payload does NOT contain a format field; rejects if present.
- System validates proof_jwt as an array of one or more proof values per OpenID4VCI 1.0 specification
- If nonce is present, system validates nonce.
- System processes the credential request.
- System generates one credential
- System returns response with single credential 
- In case of failure, system returns standardized error response.

### Alternate flows:
- If request payload contains format field → reject with invalid_request.
- If proof_jwt is not an array, or is an empty array → reject request.
- If proof_jwt is invalid → reject request.
- If nonce validation fails → reject request.
- If processing fails → return appropriate error message.

### Scenarios:
- Successful issuance — single proof JWT supplied → single credential in credentials array.
- Successful issuance — multiple proof JWTs supplied → one credential per proof in credentials array.
- Request rejected — neither credential_configuration_id nor credential_identifier is present.
- Invalid proof_jwt
- Invalid or expired nonce
- JSON processing failure during credential generation
- Malformed request payload


### Business rules (With Audit):
- Number of proof JWTs received and validated.
- Nonce validation must be performed when nonce is present.
- Response structure must support array data type for multiple credentials.
- Error responses must follow standardized format.
- Audit logs must capture:
   - Validation results (proof and nonce)
   - Error occurrences

### Acceptance criteria:
- Endpoint validates proof_jwt correctly.
- Nonce validation works when applicable.
- Endpoint supports returning requested credential
- Error responses follow defined format.
- JSON processing errors are handled and returned correctly.

### Exceptions:
- Invalid proof →
   - error: invalid_proof
   - error_description: "proof_jwt validation failed"
- Invalid nonce →
   - error: invalid_nonce
   - error_description: "c_nonce is invalid or expired"
- JSON processing failure →
   - error: json_processing_error
   - error_description: "Failed to process JSON during SD-JWT creation."
- Malformed request →
   - error: invalid_request
   - error_description: "Invalid request payload"

### Documentation:
- Update API specification for credential issuance endpoint.
- Provide examples for single credential responses.
- Document error codes and messages.

### Compatibility:
- Compatible with OpenID4VCI 1.0 requirements.

### Environment:
- Applicable across Local and Dev enviornment

### Implementation Details:
- Add request payload validation to ensure either credential_configuration_id  is present.
- Add request payload validation to reject any request containing a format field.
- Update validation logic for proof_jwt.
- Integrate nonce validation logic
- Implement centralized error handling mechanism.
- Wrap SD-JWT generation logic with exception handling for JSON errors.
- Ensure response serialization supports object in array data type.

### Non-Functional Requirements:
- Performance: Efficient handling of credential generation.
- Security: Strong validation for proof and nonce.
- Reliability: Robust error handling and graceful failures.
- Scalability: Handle concurrent requests effectively.
- Auditability: Log all validation and issuance activities.

title: Replace Credential Format from vc+sd-jwt to dc+sd-jwt for OpenID4VCI 1.0 Compliance
content:
Problem description:
### Purpose:
As an issuer system, I want to replace the credential format from vc+sd-jwt to dc+sd-jwt, so that Inji Certify aligns with OpenID4VCI 1.0 specification and supports the updated data credential format for selective disclosure.

### Pre-requisites:
- Existing support for vc+sd-jwt credential format is implemented.
- Understanding of dc+sd-jwt structure and specification requirements.
- Cryptographic libraries support SD-JWT and disclosure mechanisms.
- Wallet compatibility with dc+sd-jwt format is validated.

### Basic flow:
- Wallet requests credential issuance.
- Issuer processes the request using OpenID4VCI 1.0 flow.
- Issuer generates credential in dc+sd-jwt format:
     - Applies selective disclosure structure
     - Signs the credential
- Issuer returns the credential to the wallet in the updated format.
- Wallet verifies and stores the credential.
- Enhance the Add/Update Credential Config API to support the dc+sd-jwt format.
- Provide DB migration scripts to add support for dc+sd-jwt format in relevant tables.

### Alternate flows:
- If client requests legacy format → return error
- If wallet does not support new format → return appropriate error or fallback (if enabled).
- If format conversion fails → return issuance error.

### Scenarios:
- Successful issuance using dc+sd-jwt
- Wallet rejects unsupported format
- Credential generation failure due to format issues
- Validation of issued credential in new format

### Data Fields:
- format: dc+sd-jwt [Updated]
- credential (string): Signed SD-JWT credential
- disclosures (array): Selective disclosure elements
- issuer (string)
- subject (string)
- claims (object)

### Business rules (With Audit):
- Default credential format must be dc+sd-jwt for all new issuances.
- vc+sd-jwt must be deprecated as per migration strategy.
- Credential must follow SD-JWT structure compliant with OpenID4VCI 1.0.
- All disclosures must be properly encoded and verifiable.
- Audit logs must capture:
    - Credential format used during issuance
    - Credential generation success/failure

### Acceptance criteria:
- Credential issuance uses dc+sd-jwt format by default.
- Issued credentials conform to OpenID4VCI 1.0 specification.
- format field in responses reflects dc_sd+jwt.
- System successfully signs and returns valid SD-JWT credentials.
- No regression in credential issuance flow.

### Exceptions:
- Unsupported format → invalid_request: "Unsupported credential format"
- Credential generation failure → server_error: "Unable to generate credential"
- Signing failure → server_error: "Credential signing failed"

### Documentation:
- Update API documentation to reflect new format: dc+sd-jwt
- Provide sample credential structure for new format.
- Document deprecation plan for vc_sd+jwt.

### Compatibility:
- Forward compatible with OpenID4VCI 1.0 wallets.


### Environment:
Applicable to local and dev environments

### Implementation Details:
- Update credential generation module to use dc+sd-jwt
- Refactor format identifier in API responses and metadata.
- Update signing and disclosure logic
- Ensure validation pipeline supports new format.

### Non-Functional Requirements:
- Security: Ensure integrity and confidentiality of disclosures.
- Performance: No significant latency increase in credential generation.
- Scalability: Handle large volume of credential issuance.
- Maintainability: Modularize format handling for future updates.
- Interoperability: Ensure compatibility with standard-compliant wallets.

### Out of Scope
- Backward compatibility to support vc+sd-jwt is out of scope

title: Update Credential Issuer Well-Known Metadata for OpenID4VCI 1.0 Adoption
content:
Problem description:
### Purpose:
As an issuer system, I want to update the well-known metadata endpoint to align with OpenID4VCI 1.0, exposing the nonce_endpoint, and modifying claim display properties, to support the latest specification.

### Pre-requisites:
- well-known metadata endpoint is operational.
- nonce_endpoint implementation is completed.
- Configuration support for metadata fields is available.

### Basic flow:
- Wallet or client requests issuer metadata from the well-known endpoint.
- System routes the request to the appropriate endpoint
- The new metadata response includes:
   - nonce_endpoint
   - Updated claim display structure
- Wallet consumes metadata and proceeds with the 1.0 compliant flow.

### Alternate flows:
- If nonce_endpoint is unavailable → request will be processed without any error
- If claim display configuration is missing → fallback to default structure. if it is null then null value will be displayed.

### Scenarios:
- Retrieval of metadata from well known metadata endpoint
- Metadata includes nonce_endpoint, credential_metadata
- Updated claim display properties reflected correctly

### Data Fields:
- credential_issuer (string)
- authorization_servers (Array of string)
- credential_endpoint (string)
- nonce_endpoint (string)
-  display (modified structure) [Updated]
- credential_configuration_supported (obj)
   - format
   - scope
   - proof_type_supported
   - credetential_metadata
  
### Business rules (With Audit):
- Existing wellknown endpoint will be re used 
- nonce_endpoint must be includedmetadata response.
- Claim display property must follow updated OpenID4VCI 1.0 structure.
- Metadata responses must be consistent and version-specific.
- Audit logs must capture:
   - Metadata endpoint access (version used)
   - Metadata response generation
   - Configuration used for claims display

### Acceptance criteria:
- nonce_endpoint is present in the new metadata response.
- Claim display structure is updated as per 1.0 specification.
- Metadata responses are validated against the specification.

### Exceptions:
- Metadata generation failure → server_error: "Unable to fetch issuer metadata"
- Missing configuration → fallback to default metadata structure
- Invalid configuration → server_error: "Invalid metadata configuration"

### Documentation:
- Update OpenAPI / API specification.

title: Implementation of nonce_endpoint for c_nonce generation and replay attack prevention
content:
Problem description:
### Description
As an issuer system, I want to introduce a nonce_endpoint that generates and provides a c_nonce with a configurable expiry, so that wallet proofs are protected against replay attacks while allowing flexibility in expiry management across environments.

### Pre-requisites:
- Redis cache is available and configured.
- Configuration management system is available (application properties / env variables).
- Configurable property for c_nonce expiry is defined and accessible at runtime.
- Issuer metadata supports inclusion of nonce_endpoint.
- Secure random generator for nonce creation is available.

### Basic flow:
- Wallet invokes the nonce_endpoint.
- Issuer generates a unique c_nonce.
- Issuer reads the configured expiry value (c_nonce_expiry).
- Issuer stores c_nonce in Redis with TTL based on configured expiry.
- Issuer returns c_nonce and c_nonce_expires_in to the wallet.
- Wallet signs the proof using the received c_nonce.
- During credential request, issuer validates the c_nonce:
- Checks existence in cache
    - Validates expiry
    - Marks nonce as used (invalidates it)

### Alternate flows:
- If expiry configuration is missing → fallback to default expiry value.
- If expiry configuration is invalid (e.g., negative/zero) → reject startup or use safe default.
- If Redis is unavailable → return service error.
- If nonce is expired → reject request during validation.
- If nonce is already used → reject proof.

### Scenarios:
- Successful nonce generation using configured expiry
- Expiry value updated via configuration and reflected without code change


### Response Structure:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
Cache-Control: no-store
{
  "c_nonce": "wKI4LT17ac15ES9bw8ac4"
}
```
### Business rules (With Audit):
- c_nonce expiry must be configurable via certify-default.properties
- Default expiry must be defined (e.g., 300 seconds) if config is absent.
- Redis TTL must always align with configured expiry.
- Each nonce is valid only once.
- Audit logs must capture:
   - Request status and nonce generation status to be captured

### Acceptance criteria:
- System reads c_nonce expiry from configuration.
- Nonce is stored in Redis with TTL equal to configured value.
- API response with c_nonce generated
- Changing configuration updates expiry behavior without code change.
- Once the expiry is changed, legacy c_nounce will follow the previous expiry value and the new one will follow the updated one
- Default expiry is used when configuration is missing.
- Invalid configuration is handled safely.
- Expired nonce is rejected correctly.

### Exceptions:
- network issue -> internal server error 500

### Documentation:
- Document configuration property, e.g.:
`inji.certify.nonce.expiry: 300`
- Document behaviour of configurable expiry and defaults.

### Compatibility:
- Compatible with OpenID4VCI 1.0 specification.
- Backward compatibility (draft 11, 12 & 13)will not be maintained 

### Environment:

- Applicable across Local & dev enviornment
- Environment-specific expiry values can be configured.

### Implementation Details:

- Externalize expiry configuration 
- Read configuration at runtime (support dynamic refresh if applicable).
- Apply TTL while storing nonce in Redis.
- Return c_nonce value in API response.
- Add validation for configuration values.

### Non-Functional Requirements:

- Configurability: Expiry must be adjustable without redeployment (preferred). Restart will be required
- Security: Short-lived nonce reduces replay risk.
- Performance: Minimal latency in config read and Redis operations.
- Reliability: Safe fallback for invalid/missing config.
- Auditability: Log configuration usage and changes.

title: Adoption of OpenID4VCI 1.0 in Inji Certify (Migration from Draft 13)
content:
Problem description:
## Epic Description:
This epic focuses on upgrading Inji Certify from OpenID for Verifiable Credential Issuance (OpenID4VCI) Draft 13 to the OpenID4VCI 1.0 specification.
The migration is essential to ensure alignment with the latest stable standard, improve interoperability with wallets and issuers, and enhance security features such as replay attack prevention, standardized metadata handling, and improved proof mechanisms.
OpenID4VCI 1.0 introduces several structural and behavioral changes compared to Draft 13, including updates to credential offer handling, proof formats, metadata definitions, and new security constructs like nonce_endpoint. This upgrade will require coordinated changes across issuer APIs, credential flows, metadata exposure, and validation logic.
The epic will ensure that Inji Certify remains compliant with global standards, supports newer wallet implementations, and is future-ready for ecosystem integrations.

## Objectives:

- Align Inji Certify with OpenID4VCI 1.0 specification
- Ensure backward compatibility (where required) or define migration strategy
- Strengthen security mechanisms (nonce, proof validation, replay protection)
- Enable interoperability with compliant wallets and ecosystems
- Refactor existing flows to match updated specification requirements

## Scope:
- Migration of all OpenID4VCI flows from Draft 13 to 1.0
- Updates to issuer metadata and discovery endpoints
- Implementation of new endpoints (e.g., nonce_endpoint)
- Changes to credential offer structure and handling
- Proof generation and validation updates
- Token and credential request/response alignment
- Error handling standardization
- Configuration and extensibility updates

## Key Features / Enhancements:
- Introduction of nonce_endpoint for replay attack prevention
- Updated credential offer format and delivery mechanisms
- Enhanced proof structure and validation requirements
- Improved metadata definitions and discovery mechanisms
- Standardized error responses and codes
- Better support for pre-authorized and authorized flows

## High-Level Components Impacted:
- Credential Issuance APIs
- Issuer Metadata & Discovery ծառայ
- Token Endpoint
- Credential Endpoint
- Proof Validation Module
- Key Manager / Cryptographic Services
- Configuration Management

## Business Value:
- Ensures compliance with the latest OpenID standards
- Improves trust and security in credential issuance
- Enables seamless integration with modern wallets
- Reduces technical debt from supporting outdated drafts
- Positions Inji Certify as a standards-compliant issuer in global ecosystems

## Risks & Considerations:
- Breaking changes between Draft 13 and 1.0 may impact existing integrations
- Wallet compatibility needs validation
- Migration strategy required for existing deployments
- Thorough regression and interoperability testing required

## Success Criteria:
- All OpenID4VCI flows comply with 1.0 specification
- Interoperability verified with at least one compliant wallet
- Security enhancements (e.g., nonce handling) fully implemented
- No critical regressions in existing issuance flows
- Documentation updated and published

## Dependencies:
- Availability of OpenID4VCI 1.0 specification and clarifications
- Redis or equivalent for nonce/state handling
- Cryptographic library support for updated proof formats

## Deliverables:
- Updated APIs and endpoints compliant with 1.0
- Configuration changes and migration guidelines
- Technical documentation and API specs
- Test cases (unit, integration, interoperability)
- Upgrade scripts if any to adopt new endpoints

Problem description:
### Ticket Contents

## Description
The project aims to demonstrate the Pre-Authorized Code Flow for Verifiable Credential (VC) issuance using the Inji Stack, specifically focusing on the Inji Certify module. The use case simulates a real-world educational institute scenario where a degree certificate is issued as a Verifiable Credential to a student.

In this workflow, an educational institute administrator logs into an institute portal and registers student academic details, which are stored in the backend database. When a student logs into the portal and requests their degree certificate, the system interacts with Inji Certify to generate a Pre-Authorized Code as defined in the OpenID for Verifiable Credential Issuance (OID4VCI) specification.
The portal displays the Pre-Authorized Code in QR format and also sends a notification to the student via email. The student can scan the QR code using a compatible wallet to receive their degree certificate as a Verifiable Credential.

The demonstration highlights how the issuer portal, backend service, Inji Certify, and wallet applications interact to complete the credential issuance flow securely and seamlessly.

## Impact
The feature demonstrates a real-world use case of digital credential issuance with pre authorised code using the Inji Stack.

Benefits include:
- Showcases how educational institutions can issue digital degrees as verifiable credentials.
- Demonstrates OID4VCI Pre-Authorized Code Flow integration with issuer portals.
- Enables students to securely receive credentials in a digital wallet.
- Improves trust and interoperability in digital credential ecosystems.

### Goals

## Goals

- **Implement Pre-Authorized Code VC Issuance**
Enable the educational institute portal to interact with Inji Certify to generate a Pre-Authorized Code that allows students to retrieve their credential securely.
- **Demonstrate End-to-End Credential Issuance**
  - Demonstrate the full lifecycle from:
      - Student record creation
      - Credential request
      - Pre-authorized code generation
      - Wallet retrieval
      - VC storage in wallet
 **- Integrate Issuer Portal with Certify**
      - Develop backend integration where the portal calls the Certify API to initiate credential issuance using Pre-Authorized Code Flow.
**- Generate QR Code for Credential Retrieval**
      - The portal must generate a QR code containing the pre-authorized code and credential offer information which the student wallet can scan.
**- Email Notification to Credential Holder**
      - Send an automated email notification to the student’s registered email address when the credential becomes available.
      - Support Wallet Retrieval
- **Allow students to retrieve credentials using:**
    - Mobile wallet scanning QR code
    - Web wallet scanning QR code


### Expected Outcome

The outcome of this epic is a working demonstration of Pre-Authorized Code Flow for VC issuance using the Inji Stack.
The educational institute portal will:

1. Allow administrators to register student academic information.
2. Store student records in the backend database.
3. Allow students to request their degree certificate.
4. Generate a Pre-Authorized Code through Certify.
5. Display a QR code containing the credential offer.
6. Send an email notification to the student.
7. Allow the student to retrieve the VC using a compatible wallet.
8. The student will receive the Degree Certificate as a Verifiable Credential, stored securely in their wallet.


### Acceptance Criteria

**Admin Portal**

- Admin MUST be able to login to the portal.
- Admin MUST be able to add student records.
- Student data fields include:
      1. studentId
      2. fullName
      3. courseName
      4. CGPA
      5. graduationMonth
      6. graduationYear
      7. specialization
      8. emailAddress

**Student Portal**
- Student MUST login to the portal.
- Student MUST be able to request a degree certificate using Student ID.
- Certify Integration
- Portal MUST call Certify API to generate a Pre-Authorized Code.
- Certify MUST return a valid credential offer with pre-authorized code.
- pre-authorised code should be valid only for 30mins. portal should display the validity

**QR Code**
- Portal MUST generate a QR code containing credential offer information.

**Email Notification**
- System MUST send an email notification to the student with QR code
- Validity of the QR code should be displayed 

**Wallet Retrieval**
- Student MUST be able to retrieve credential via:
1. Mobile wallet scanning QR
2. Web wallet scanning QR

### Implementation Details

**Basic Flow**

**- Step 1 – Admin Adds Student Record**
   1. Admin logs into the institute portal and registers student details.
   2. The portal stores student data in the backend database.
**- Step 2 – Student Requests Credential**
   1. Student logs into the portal and selects:
   2. Download Degree Certificate
   3. Student enters Student ID.
**- Step 3 – Portal Retrieves Student Record**
   1. Portal backend fetches the student record and prepares credential data.
- **Step 4 – Portal Calls Certify**
   1. Portal sends request to Certify:
   2. POST /credential-offer
   3. Certify generates:
   4. Pre-Authorized Code
   5. Credential Offer URI
**- Step 5 – QR Code Generation**
   1. Portal generates a QR code containing credential offer URI.
**- Step 6 – Email Notification**
   1. System sends email notification to student.
- **Step 7 – Wallet Retrieves Credential**
   1. Student scans QR code using wallet.
   2. Wallet performs:
   3. Token request using pre-authorized code
   4. Credential request
   5. Certify issues the Degree Certificate VC.

**Error Scenarios**

1. Student Not Found
If student ID does not exist:

```
}
```

2. Credential Generation Failure

```
 "code": 500
}
```
3. Invalid Pre-Authorized Code
If wallet uses invalid code:
```
{
 "error": "Invalid pre-authorized code",
 "code": 401
}
```

title: Migrate custom Jwk class to Nimbus JWK
content:
Problem description:
## Summary

Migrate the custom `Jwk` data class to use the Nimbus JWK library (`com.nimbusds:nimbus-jose-jwt`) natively.

## Motivation

The current codebase uses a hand-rolled `Jwk` data class for key representation. Nimbus already provides a full-featured `JWK` model that:

- Supports RFC 7638 JWK Thumbprint computation natively via `ThumbprintUtils.compute(JWK)` / `jwk.computeThumbprint().decode()`
- Handles EC, OKP, RSA, and other key types out of the box
- Eliminates the need for manual canonical JSON construction in `jwkThumbprintBytes()` in `CborUtils.kt`

A TODO was added in [`CborUtils.kt`](https://github.com/inji/inji-openid4vp/blob/ovp-spec-v1-support/kotlin/openID4VP/src/commonMain/kotlin/io/mosip/openID4VP/common/CborUtils.kt) (PR #174) calling this out explicitly:
```kotlin
// TODO: Nimbus has ThumbprintUtils.compute(JWK) / jwk.computeThumbprint().decode() which does this natively,
//  but it requires a Nimbus JWK instance. Replace once Jwk -> Nimbus migration ticket is done.
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Replace the custom `Jwk` data class with `com.nimbusds.jose.jwk.JWK` (or appropriate Nimbus subclasses) across the codebase
- [ ] Replace the manual `jwkThumbprintBytes()` implementation in `CborUtils.kt` with Nimbus native thumbprint computation
- [ ] Ensure RSA key type is also supported (currently throws `IllegalArgumentException` due to missing `n`/`e` fields in the custom model)
- [ ] Update all call sites and tests accordingly

## References

- PR #174 (OVP spec v1 support) — comment: https://github.com/inji/inji-openid4vp/pull/174#discussion_r3377959152
- Requested by @swatigoel
